# Overview – Stage 1 of 6

This is the first of six stage files that together align two LiDAR point cloud
scans (`las_1` and `las_2`) of the same forest plot taken at two epochs.

| Stage | File | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `Stage1_TemporalPairs.qmd` | Stage-1 ellipses, temporal pairs, `pivot1` |
| 2 | `Stage2_XYZRotation.qmd` | full XYZ rotation matrix `R_xyz` (solved, **not** applied) |
| 3 | `Stage3_ZTranslation.qmd` | axis-perpendicular ellipses, Z-shift `t_trans_z` (recorded, **not** applied) |
| 4 | `Stage4_ZRotation.qmd` | Z-only rotation `z_rotation_deg`|
| 5 | `Stage5_XYTranslation.qmd` |  XY shift `t_trans_xy` |
| 6 | `Stage6_Export.qmd` | single composed transform applied to the point cloud, exported |

Each stage hands off to the next through a single `.rds` checkpoint. Only
Stages 1, 3 and 6 ever load point-cloud data; Stages 2, 4 and 5 work purely on
the fitted ellipse geometry.

What Stage 1 does

- loads both clouds and records the file paths so every later stage can
  reload exactly the same data
- **rough vertical alignment (Stage 1A)**: first tests the per-tree **bounding
  boxes** for a **sideways** forest (1A.0) and, if it finds one, tips `las_1` 90
  degrees upright before anything is fitted; then fits a coarse ellipse set up
  every epoch-1 stem, diagnoses right-side-up vs upside-down from the
  area-vs-height trend, builds a forest-average axis, and rotates `las_1` so that
  axis points along global +Z. Only `las_1` is touched; the total rotation
  `R_align_1` (sideways tip composed in) and the verdict are recorded
- computes **`pivot1`** – the footprint centre of `las_1` (mid-point of its
  horizontal *and* vertical extent). It is fixed once, before the Stage 1A
  rotation, and never recomputed - every rotation in the pipeline turns about it.
  This single point is the rotation origin used in Stage 3 and Stage 6, so both
  stages rotate about identical geometry
- fits brute-force RANSAC ellipses to stem slices, cleans them, refits and
  recleans them
- matches trees across epochs by **triangle correspondence** (spatial mode) or a
  manual CSV mapping
- writes the Stage 1 checkpoint

## Pair-list naming convention

`pairs_df` is **not** reused as a mutable object anywhere in this workflow.
Every time the kept-pair set changes, a new named object is created, so the
provenance of any pair list is readable from its name alone:

In Stage 1 the raw pairing produces `pairs_matched`, which becomes
`pairs_stage1` once the unmatched stems are dropped. Every later stage that
narrows the kept-pair set again creates a new named object rather than
mutating an existing one, so the provenance of any pair list is readable from
its name alone.

# Stage 0 - Setup


## 0.1 Load libraries
```{r}
#| label: setup
#| code-summary: "Load libraries and set plot theme"

library(lidR)       # LAS I/O and point cloud processing
library(dbscan)     # kNN search (spatial temporal pairing)
library(ggplot2)    # Plotting
library(dplyr)      # Data wrangling
library(plotly)     # Interactive 3D stem/pair figures
library(base64enc)  # Embed rendered plots into HTML galleries
library(htmltools)  # Assemble the HTML gallery output

# ── Driver-supplied parameter overrides ──────────────────────────────────────
# Every params-* chunk in this file ends with .par_apply("<its label>"). Run the
# file by hand and that call does nothing: the values the chunk just assigned
# stand. Run it under the batch driver, which puts a .batch_params list in the
# environment before the first chunk, and any entry keyed to that chunk label is
# assigned here - AFTER the defaults, so the driver's value is the one that
# survives into the functional chunk that follows.
#
# Why this exists. Parameters used to sit in the same chunk as the code that
# consumed them, so the driver's overrides - which land after a chunk finishes -
# arrived too late to matter, and every pair silently used the .qmd's hardcoded
# value. Splitting each chunk in two fixes the ordering; this helper is what the
# driver reaches through.
#
# The defaults stay in this file rather than moving into the driver. They are
# the single definition, the driver names only what a batch changes, and there
# is no second copy of ~670 parameters to drift out of step with this one.
#
# envir = parent.frame() so a call at chunk top level lands in the environment
# the chunk is being evaluated in - globalenv by hand, the pair environment
# under the driver - without needing .stage_env(), which is defined further down.
.par_apply <- function(label, envir = parent.frame()) {
  bp <- mget(".batch_params", envir = envir, ifnotfound = list(NULL),
             inherits = TRUE)[[1]]
  if (is.null(bp) || is.null(bp[[label]])) return(invisible(character(0)))
  vals <- bp[[label]]
  if (!length(vals)) return(invisible(character(0)))
  if (is.null(names(vals)) || any(!nzchar(names(vals))))
    stop(sprintf("[.par_apply] .batch_params[['%s']] must be a fully NAMED list.", label))
  # A name the chunk did not define is almost always a typo or a rename in the
  # .qmd that the driver has not caught up with. Silence there would mean the
  # batch runs on the default while looking like it was overridden, so it stops.
  unknown <- names(vals)[!vapply(names(vals), exists, logical(1),
                                 envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)]
  if (length(unknown))
    stop(sprintf(paste0("[.par_apply] %s: %d override(s) name nothing this chunk assigns:\n  %s\n",
                        "  Fix the name in the driver's .build_params(), or remove it."),
                 label, length(unknown), paste(unknown, collapse = "\n  ")))
  for (nm in names(vals)) assign(nm, vals[[nm]], envir = envir)
  cat(sprintf("  [params] %s <- driver (%s)\n", label, paste(names(vals), collapse = ", ")))
  invisible(names(vals))
}
```

## 0.2 Global Helpers
```{r}
#| label: params-helpers
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Colours, ggplot theme, shared cleaning/plot helpers, and the stage save/load utilities"

# ============================================================
# Colours
# #BF9ACA
# ============================================================
COL_1     <- "#2196F3"
COL_2     <- "#FF5722"
COL_MATCH <- "#D9F9A5"
WINNER    <- "#F5E5FC"
LOSER     <- "#721121"

# ============================================================
# Progress bars
# ============================================================
# One set of helpers, two renderers, chosen at the moment a bar is created.
#
#   cli    a redrawing bar, when there is a terminal able to show one
#   lines  one ordinary printed line per update, when there is not
#
# The choice is not cosmetic. cli draws on STDERR, and the batch driver holds a
# sink(type = "message"), which cannot split - so under the driver a cli bar
# goes to the log file and nowhere else, arriving as carriage returns and
# escape codes wrapped around each other. That is what the last run's log shows
# for every fitting step except the library's own: minutes of work with nothing
# on screen, and an unreadable smear in the log afterwards.
#
# The printed-line renderer is what the RANSAC library's cat handler already
# does, and it is the one visible line in that log. Same format here, so a fit
# reports identically whether the progress comes from the library or from a
# loop in this file.
show_progress_bars <- TRUE

# Print at most one line per 5% of the total or per 15 seconds, whichever comes
# first, plus always the first and last. A 20-stem fit gives ~20 lines; a
# 5000-slice loop does not give 5000.
progress_step_frac    <- 0.05
progress_min_seconds  <- 15

.par_apply("params-helpers")
```

```{r}
#| label: helpers
#| code-summary: "Colours, ggplot theme, shared cleaning/plot helpers, and the stage save/load utilities"

# ============================================================
# ggplot theme
# ============================================================
theme_set(
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      plot.title       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      legend.position  = "bottom"
    )
)
# ============================================================
# Pre-clean minimum ellipse count filter
# Used in Step 1.2 (.filter_min_ellipses) AND Step 3.3
# (.filter_min_ellipses_s5 was identical logic – unified here).
# ============================================================
.filter_min_ellipses <- function(raw, label, min_count = 5L) {
  counts  <- sapply(raw, function(df)
    if (is.null(df)) 0L else
      sum(!is.na(df$center_x) & !is.na(df$semi_a) & !is.na(df$semi_b)))
  keep    <- counts >= min_count
  removed <- names(raw)[!keep]
  if (length(removed) > 0)
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s] Pre-clean filter: removed %d tree(s) with fewer than %d fitted ellipses: %s\n",
      label, length(removed), min_count, paste(removed, collapse = ", ")
    ))
  else
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s] Pre-clean filter: all %d trees have >= %d fitted ellipses.\n",
      label, length(raw), min_count
    ))
  raw[keep]
}

# ============================================================
# Shared ellipse cleaning plot helpers
# (used in Step 1.2 and Step 3.3 vis blocks)
# ============================================================

#' Single ggplot panel: one variable vs height, with outlier crosses.
make_cleaning_plot <- function(pts, y_col, outlier_col, y_lab,
                               title, caption, colour,
                               h_col           = "slice_z",
                               pt_size_inlier  = 3.0,
                               pt_size_outlier = 4.5,
                               pt_alpha        = 0.6,
                               line_width      = 0.4) {

  if (is.null(pts) || nrow(pts) == 0)       return(NULL)
  if (!y_col       %in% names(pts))          return(NULL)
  if (!outlier_col %in% names(pts))          pts[[outlier_col]] <- FALSE
  if (!"isolated"  %in% names(pts))          pts$isolated       <- FALSE
  pts <- pts[!is.na(pts[[y_col]]), ]
  if (nrow(pts) == 0)                        return(NULL)

  pts_inlier   <- pts[!pts[[outlier_col]] & !pts$isolated, ]
  pts_spike    <- pts[ pts[[outlier_col]], ]
  pts_isolated <- pts[!pts[[outlier_col]] &  pts$isolated, ]

  ggplot() +
    geom_line(
      data      = pts_inlier,
      aes(.data[[h_col]], .data[[y_col]]),
      colour    = colour, linewidth = line_width, alpha = 0.5
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data   = pts_inlier,
      aes(.data[[h_col]], .data[[y_col]]),
      colour = colour, shape = 16,
      size   = pt_size_inlier, alpha = pt_alpha
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data   = pts_spike,
      aes(.data[[h_col]], .data[[y_col]]),
      colour = colour, shape = 4,
      size   = pt_size_outlier, stroke = 1.4
    ) +
    geom_point(
      data   = pts_isolated,
      aes(.data[[h_col]], .data[[y_col]]),
      colour = colour, shape = 1,        # hollow circle
      size   = pt_size_outlier, stroke = 1.2
    ) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Height (m)", y = y_lab, caption = caption) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 13)
}

#' Build all six cleaning panels for every tree in one cloud's result list.
make_cloud_plots_ellipse <- function(clean_result_list, cloud_label, colour,
                                     mad_tol_xy, local_k,
                                     mad_tol_r,  local_k_r,
                                     h_col = "slice_z") {

  caption_xy <- sprintf(
    "\u2715 = XY spike  \u25cb = isolated  |  MAD tol = %.1f  |  local_k = %d",
    mad_tol_xy, local_k
  )
  caption_r <- sprintf(
    "\u2715 = radius spike  \u25cb = isolated  |  MAD tol = %.1f  |  local_k_r = %d",
    mad_tol_r, local_k_r
  )
  caption_all <- sprintf(
    "\u2715 = any radius outlier  \u25cb = isolated  |  MAD tol R = %.1f  |  local_k_r = %d",
    mad_tol_r, local_k_r
  )

  setNames(
    lapply(names(clean_result_list), function(tid) {
      flagged  <- clean_result_list[[tid]]$flagged
      title_p  <- sprintf("[%s] Tree %s", cloud_label, tid)

      if (is.null(flagged) || nrow(flagged) == 0)
        return(list(cx = NULL, cy = NULL, ca = NULL,
                    cb = NULL, ar = NULL, ec = NULL))

      df_xy <- flagged

      drop_mask <- rep(FALSE, nrow(flagged))
      if ("spike_xy"  %in% names(flagged)) drop_mask <- drop_mask | flagged$spike_xy
      df_r <- flagged[!drop_mask, ]

      mk <- function(df, y, out, ylab, cap)
        make_cleaning_plot(df, y_col = y, outlier_col = out,
                           y_lab = ylab, title = title_p,
                           caption = cap, colour = colour,
                           h_col = h_col)

      list(
        cx = mk(df_xy, "center_x",  "spike_xy",   "Centre X (m)",            caption_xy),
        cy = mk(df_xy, "center_y",  "spike_xy",   "Centre Y (m)",            caption_xy),
        ca = mk(df_r,  "semi_a",    "spike_a",    "Semi-major axis a (m)",   caption_r),
        cb = mk(df_r,  "semi_b",    "spike_b",    "Semi-minor axis b (m)",   caption_r),
        ar = mk(df_r,  "ell_area",  "spike_radii","Ellipse area (m\u00b2)",  caption_all),
        ec = mk(df_r,  "ell_ecc",   "spike_radii","Eccentricity",            caption_all)
      )
    }),
    names(clean_result_list)
  )
}

#' Render a scrollable 2-column gallery of cleaning panels as HTML with lightbox.
render_gallery_pairs <- function(plot_list, lb_id) {

  has_content <- vapply(plot_list, function(x)
    !is.null(x$cx) || !is.null(x$cy), logical(1))
  if (!any(has_content)) return(HTML("<p>No data.</p>"))

  encode_plot <- function(p, w = 10, h = 4.5, dpi = 180) {
    if (is.null(p)) return(NULL)
    tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
    on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
    ggsave(tmp, plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi)
    paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(tmp))
  }

  img_tag <- function(src) {
    if (is.null(src)) return('<div style="background:#f4f4f4;border-radius:6px;min-height:200px;"></div>')
    sprintf(
      '<img src="%s"
            style="width:100%%;border-radius:6px;
                   box-shadow:0 2px 10px rgba(0,0,0,.18);
                   cursor:zoom-in;display:block;"
            onclick="openLb_%s(this.src)" />',
      src, lb_id
    )
  }

  row2 <- function(left_src, right_src)
    sprintf(
      '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr;gap:18px;margin-bottom:18px;">%s%s</div>',
      img_tag(left_src), img_tag(right_src)
    )

  blocks <- paste(
    vapply(names(plot_list)[has_content], function(tid) {
      p   <- plot_list[[tid]]
      b64 <- lapply(p, encode_plot)
      paste(
        sprintf('<h4 style="margin:14px 0 8px 0;">Tree %s</h4>', tid),
        row2(b64$cx, b64$cy),
        row2(b64$ca, b64$cb),
        row2(b64$ar, b64$ec),
        '<hr style="margin:22px 0;border-color:#ccc;"/>'
      )
    }, character(1)),
    collapse = "\n"
  )

  HTML(sprintf('
<style>
  #lbOv_%s{display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9999;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,.82);align-items:center;justify-content:center;}
  #lbOv_%s.open{display:flex;}
  #lbOv_%s img{max-width:95vw;max-height:95vh;border-radius:6px;
    box-shadow:0 4px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6);}
  #lbCl_%s{position:fixed;top:16px;right:20px;font-size:32px;color:#fff;
    cursor:pointer;line-height:1;user-select:none;z-index:10000;}
</style>
<div id="lbOv_%s" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeLb_%s()">
  <span id="lbCl_%s" onclick="closeLb_%s()">&#x2715;</span>
  <img id="lbIm_%s" src=""/>
</div>
<div style="padding:25px;">%s</div>
<script>
  window.openLb_%s  = s => {
    document.getElementById("lbIm_%s").src = s;
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.add("open");
  };
  window.closeLb_%s = () =>
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.remove("open");
</script>',
    lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
    lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
    blocks,
    lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id
  ))
}
# ============================================================
# 1.0.6  Ellipse ring geometry helper
# ============================================================
.ellipse_ring <- function(cx, cy, a, b, angle_deg, z_abs, n, tid) {
  if (any(is.na(c(cx, cy, a, b, angle_deg, z_abs)))) return(NULL)
  tht   <- angle_deg * pi / 180
  t_seq <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n + 1L)
  x_pts <- cx + a * cos(t_seq) * cos(tht) - b * sin(t_seq) * sin(tht)
  y_pts <- cy + a * cos(t_seq) * sin(tht) + b * sin(t_seq) * cos(tht)
  rbind(
    data.frame(X = x_pts, Y = y_pts, Z = z_abs, TreeID = tid),
    data.frame(X = NA_real_, Y = NA_real_, Z = NA_real_, TreeID = tid)
  )
}

# ============================================================
# Stage save/load utilities – shared by every stage file.
#
# Contract (identical in all six stage files):
#   SAVE  → hard ERROR if any *required* object is missing from the
#           environment, so a checkpoint can never be written half-empty.
#           A *warning* is raised for any missing *optional* object
#           (diagnostic products that may legitimately not have been run);
#           those are simply omitted from the file.
#   LOAD  → never errors on content. A *warning* is raised for each
#           requested object that is absent from the RDS. Objects present in
#           the RDS but not requested are COUNTED in the summary line and
#           never listed. Everything found in the file is loaded either way,
#           so nothing is silently discarded.
#   PATHS → a save never overwrites: if the target path exists, a numeric
#           suffix (_001, _002, ...) is appended until the name is free.
# ============================================================

#' Return `path` if free, otherwise path_001 / path_002 / ... (first free one).
.unique_path <- function(path) {
  if (!file.exists(path)) return(path)
  base_noext <- tools::file_path_sans_ext(path)
  ext        <- tools::file_ext(path)
  counter    <- 1L
  repeat {
    candidate <- sprintf("%s_%03d.%s", base_noext, counter, ext)
    if (!file.exists(candidate)) {
      cat(sprintf("Target already exists - using unique name: %s\n", candidate))
      return(candidate)
    }
    counter <- counter + 1L
  }
}

#' Which environment do the stage helpers read and write?
#'
#' A .qmd rendered or run by hand evaluates its chunks in the global
#' environment. The batch driver does not: it gives every LAS pair a fresh
#' environment of its own, so that a leftover object from the previous pair
#' cannot be picked up by one of the exists() guards this pipeline is full of.
#' Under the driver, everything the stages assign therefore lives THERE, and
#' not in globalenv.
#'
#' parent.env(environment()) is the environment this chunk was evaluated in:
#' globalenv() by hand, the pair environment under the driver. It is resolved
#' from where .stage_env was DEFINED rather than from where it is called, so it
#' returns the same environment inside a function as it does at chunk top
#' level, and nothing has to be told which mode it is in.
#'
#' This replaced a hardcoded .stage_env() throughout. Under the driver that
#' pointed at an environment the pipeline had never written to, so every object
#' in a save manifest read as missing and the checkpoint refused to write - the
#' Stage 1 failure that reported 30 missing required objects after a 64-minute
#' fit. (`run_counts` was the one it did find, and only because .tally()'s `<<-`
#' walked past the pair environment into globalenv. That is fixed below too.)
.stage_env <- function() parent.env(environment())

#' Is a batch driver running this file?
#'
#' The driver assigns .batch_mode <- TRUE into the pair environment before the
#' first chunk runs. It changes one thing, and only for the checkpoints: in a
#' batch, every stage runs in ONE session, so Stage N+1 already holds in memory
#' everything Stage N computed and never has to read it back off disk. The
#' checkpoints stop being load-bearing and become a record of the run.
#'
#' So under a batch: nothing in a manifest is required (a missing object is
#' reported and left out, and the pair carries on), a failed write is reported
#' rather than thrown, and .stage_load is a no-op. Run the same .qmd by hand and
#' every one of those is an error again, which is what it should be when the
#' checkpoint is the only thing carrying the stage forward.
.in_batch <- function() {
  isTRUE(mget(".batch_mode", envir = .stage_env(),
              ifnotfound = list(FALSE), inherits = FALSE)[[1]])
}

#' Read one of the driver's batch settings out of the pair environment.
#' Absent - i.e. this file is being run by hand - gives `default`.
.batch_opt <- function(name, default = NULL) {
  v <- mget(name, envir = .stage_env(), ifnotfound = list(NULL), inherits = FALSE)[[1]]
  if (is.null(v)) default else v
}

#' Where a checkpoint goes when a batch is running.
#'
#' Every save chunk in this pipeline assigns its .rds path and then USES it a
#' few lines later, in the same chunk. The driver applies its overrides AFTER a
#' chunk has run, so an override of stage1_rds_path arrives after the file has
#' already been written to the path hardcoded here - which means, without this,
#' every sample in a batch writes over the same hardcoded name.
#'
#' So in batch mode the destination is derived instead, from two values the
#' driver puts in the environment before anything runs: .batch_rds_dir and
#' .batch_sample. The label the save chunk already passes supplies the rest, so
#' "Stage 3.2" becomes <dir>/<sample>_Stage3_2.rds with nothing to keep in sync.
#'
#' NULL means: not in a batch, or the driver did not set the directory - use the
#' path the chunk asked for.
.batch_rds_path <- function(label) {
  dir <- .batch_opt(".batch_rds_dir")
  smp <- .batch_opt(".batch_sample")
  if (is.null(dir) || is.null(smp)) return(NULL)
  file.path(dir, sprintf("%s_%s.rds", smp,
                         gsub("\\.", "_", gsub("\\s+", "", label))))
}

#' Save a stage checkpoint. Errors on missing required objects - unless the
#' batch driver is running this file, in which case nothing is required, the
#' destination is the per-sample one derived above, and a failure to write is
#' reported rather than thrown. See .in_batch() above.
`%||%` <- function(a, b) if (is.null(a)) b else a

.stage_save <- function(path, required, optional = character(0),
                        label = "stage", envir = .stage_env(),
                        strict = !.in_batch()) {

  required <- unique(required)
  optional <- setdiff(unique(optional), required)

  # A batch may switch an individual checkpoint off by label - the driver's
  # keep_stage3_fit_checkpoint does exactly this for "Stage 3.1", whose chunk
  # must still RUN (the final Stage 3 manifest inherits from it) but need not
  # write a second large file per sample.
  if (!strict && label %in% .batch_opt(".batch_skip_saves", character(0))) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Skipped - switched off for this batch.\n", label))
    return(invisible(NA_character_))
  }

  # inherits = FALSE, matching the mget() below, which has always been strict.
  # With inheritance on, an object could be FOUND in a parent environment and
  # then fail to be FETCHED, and under the driver the parent is globalenv -
  # i.e. the previous pair's leftovers.
  .have <- function(x)
    if (!length(x)) logical(0)
    else vapply(x, exists, logical(1), envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)

  missing_req <- required[!.have(required)]
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L) {
    if (strict)
      stop(sprintf(
        "[%s save] Cannot save - %d required object(s) missing from the environment:\n  %s",
        label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))
    cat(sprintf(
      "[%s save] %d required object(s) missing - treated as optional and omitted (batch mode):\n  %s\n",
      label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))
  }

  missing_opt <- optional[!.have(optional)]
  if (length(missing_opt) > 0L) {
    msg <- sprintf(
      "[%s save] %d optional object(s) missing - omitted from the checkpoint:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_opt), paste(missing_opt, collapse = "\n  "))
    if (strict) warning(msg) else cat(msg, "\n", sep = "")
  }

  present  <- c(setdiff(required, missing_req), setdiff(optional, missing_opt))
  n_opt_in <- length(setdiff(optional, missing_opt))
  dat      <- mget(present, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE)

  # ── The checkpoint describes itself ────────────────────────────────────────
  # The manifest travels INSIDE the file. Without it, loading a checkpoint means
  # first reconstructing the exact `required`/`optional` vectors it was written
  # with - and those are built by chunks, so a later checkpoint could only be
  # loaded after running the chunks that define an earlier one's manifest. That
  # made resuming from an arbitrary point in a fresh session impossible: the
  # Stage 3.2 chunk, for instance, stops outright unless .stage3_1_required is
  # already in scope.
  #
  # Stored under a name no manifest can collide with, and stripped again on
  # load, so it never reaches the session as an object.
  dat[[".__manifest__"]] <- list(
    required = setdiff(required, missing_req),
    optional = setdiff(optional, missing_opt),
    label    = label,
    saved_utc = format(Sys.time(), tz = "UTC", usetz = TRUE))

  .write <- function() {
    p <- path
    if (!strict) {
      bp <- .batch_rds_path(label)
      if (!is.null(bp)) p <- bp
    }
    dir.create(dirname(p), recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    # .unique_path only interactively. A batch path already carries the sample
    # name, so it cannot collide with another sample, and a re-run of the same
    # sample should REPLACE its checkpoint rather than leave _001, _002 behind
    # for the next reader to guess between.
    if (strict) p <- .unique_path(p)
    saveRDS(dat, p)
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Saved %d object(s) (%d required, %d optional) -> %s\n",
                label, length(dat), length(present) - n_opt_in, n_opt_in, p))
    p
  }

  if (strict) return(invisible(.write()))

  out <- tryCatch(.write(), error = function(e) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Checkpoint NOT written: %s\n", label, conditionMessage(e)))
    cat(sprintf("[%s save] Batch mode - the objects are still in this session, so the run continues.\n",
                label))
    NA_character_
  })
  invisible(out)
}

#' Load a stage checkpoint. Warns (never errors) on content mismatches, and
#' under the batch driver does not read at all - see .in_batch() above.
.stage_load <- function(path, required, optional = character(0),
                        label = "stage", envir = .stage_env(),
                        strict = !.in_batch()) {

  # In a batch the objects this would read are already live in `envir`, put
  # there by the stage that just ran. Reading them back would at best be a
  # no-op. At worst it would be wrong: checkpoint paths are per-sample and
  # .unique_path() means a re-run writes _001 rather than replacing the
  # original, so the path named here can easily be an EARLIER run's file. And
  # if the write failed or was partial, there would be nothing to read and the
  # pair would die at the start of the next stage having done all the work.
  if (!strict) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s load] Skipped - batch mode: this stage's objects are already in the session.\n",
                label))
    return(invisible(character(0)))
  }

  if (!file.exists(path))
    stop(sprintf("[%s load] File not found:\n  %s", label, path))

  dat <- readRDS(path)

  # ── Prefer the manifest the file carries ───────────────────────────────────
  # A checkpoint written by .stage_save records what it holds, so a load needs
  # nothing from the session - no earlier chunk, no earlier checkpoint, no
  # reconstructed name vectors. `required` and `optional` become a CHECK against
  # what the caller expected rather than the definition of what to read, which
  # is what lets any stage be resumed from any checkpoint in a fresh session.
  #
  # Files written before manifests existed simply have none; those fall back to
  # the caller's vectors, exactly as before.
  mf <- dat[[".__manifest__"]]
  dat[[".__manifest__"]] <- NULL
  caller_req <- unique(required)
  caller_opt <- setdiff(unique(optional), caller_req)

  if (!is.null(mf)) {
    required <- unique(mf$required)
    optional <- setdiff(unique(mf$optional), required)
    src <- sprintf("its own manifest (written %s)", mf$saved_utc %||% "?")
  } else {
    required <- caller_req; optional <- caller_opt
    src <- "the caller's manifest - this file predates self-describing checkpoints"
  }
  expected <- c(required, optional)

  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Reading %d object(s) from: %s\n",
              label, length(dat), path))
  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Manifest: %s\n", label, src))

  # Named by the caller but absent from the file: the real incompatibility, and
  # the only one worth a warning when the file describes itself.
  if (!is.null(mf)) {
    unmet <- setdiff(caller_req, names(dat))
    if (length(unmet))
      warning(sprintf(
        "[%s load] %d object(s) this stage expects are not in the checkpoint:\n  %s",
        label, length(unmet), paste(unmet, collapse = "\n  ")))
  }

  missing_req <- required[!required %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(missing_req) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s load] %d REQUIRED object(s) absent from the RDS - downstream chunks that use them will fail:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_req), paste(missing_req, collapse = "\n  ")))

  missing_opt <- optional[!optional %in% names(dat)]
  if (length(missing_opt) > 0L)
    warning(sprintf(
      "[%s load] %d optional object(s) absent from the RDS:\n  %s",
      label, length(missing_opt), paste(missing_opt, collapse = "\n  ")))

  # Unrequested objects are COUNTED, never listed. Every checkpoint from Stage 2
  # onward is cumulative, so this set is routinely hundreds of names long and
  # printing it buried the two messages that actually matter - an absent
  # required object, and an absent optional one - under a wall of text. The
  # count still appears in the summary line below, which is the only part of it
  # anyone reads.
  extra <- setdiff(names(dat), expected)

  # ── Publish what was loaded, for the next stage's save manifest ────────────
  # Every stage's SAVE manifest is built as "the previous stage's manifest, plus
  # my own objects", and the previous manifest is a vector defined by that
  # stage's LOAD chunk. Load a LATER checkpoint directly and that chunk never
  # runs, so the save dies on a missing .stageN_required - which is exactly the
  # resume-from-anywhere case these checkpoints now exist to support.
  #
  # Recording the manifest here breaks the dependency: .manifest_from() below
  # falls back to whatever was actually loaded, whichever chunk did it.
  assign(".stage_last_manifest",
         list(required = required, optional = optional,
              names = names(dat), label = label, path = path),
         envir = envir)

  list2env(dat, envir = envir)

  cat(sprintf("[%s load] Loaded %d object(s) | required present: %d/%d | optional present: %d/%d | unrequested: %d\n",
              label, length(dat),
              length(required) - length(missing_req), length(required),
              length(optional) - length(missing_opt), length(optional),
              length(extra)))
  invisible(names(dat))
}

#' The manifest a save chunk inherits from the stage before it.
#'
#' Looks for the named vector first - that is the normal path, when this
#' session's own load chunk built it. Falls back to the manifest carried by
#' whichever checkpoint was last loaded, which is what makes it possible to load
#' any checkpoint and still save the next one.
#'
#' `which` is "required" or "optional". Stops with something actionable rather
#' than returning character(0): a save that silently inherits nothing writes a
#' checkpoint missing every object from every earlier stage, and nothing would
#' notice until a later stage failed to find them.
.manifest_from <- function(name, which = c("required", "optional"),
                           envir = .stage_env()) {
  which <- match.arg(which)
  if (exists(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))
    return(get(name, envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))

  lm <- if (exists(".stage_last_manifest", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE))
          get(".stage_last_manifest", envir = envir, inherits = FALSE) else NULL

  if (!is.null(lm)) {
    cat(sprintf("[manifest] %s not in the session - inheriting from the %s checkpoint that was loaded.\n",
                name, lm$label))
    # For "required", everything the loaded file actually held is the honest
    # inheritance: it is what this session has, regardless of how the file that
    # produced it split required from optional.
    return(if (identical(which, "required")) lm$names else character(0))
  }

  # ── Last resort: the session itself ────────────────────────────────────────
  # No named vector and no checkpoint loaded. That is the ordinary case for a
  # session built by RUNNING chunks rather than by loading - Stage 1 through
  # Stage 3 straight down the document, or an interactive session where the
  # objects were produced rather than read. There is nothing wrong with it, and
  # a save must not refuse.
  #
  # So fall back to what Stages 4 and 5 have always done: take the manifest from
  # the environment. Every non-function, non-dotted object in scope is what this
  # stage inherited, by definition - it is the same rule, just applied later.
  #
  # Only "required" gets this. Optional means "save it if it happens to exist",
  # which is meaningless once the list IS everything that exists.
  if (identical(which, "required")) {
    nm <- setdiff(ls(envir = envir), lsf.str(envir = envir))
    nm <- nm[!startsWith(nm, ".")]
    if (length(nm)) {
      cat(sprintf(paste0("[manifest] %s not found and no checkpoint was loaded - taking the manifest\n",
                         "           from the session instead (%d object(s)). This is the normal path\n",
                         "           when the stage was RUN rather than loaded.\n"), name, length(nm)))
      return(nm)
    }
  } else {
    return(character(0))
  }

  stop(sprintf(paste0("[manifest] %s not found, no checkpoint has been loaded, and the session is\n",
                      "  empty - there is nothing to save. Run this stage's chunks, or load a\n",
                      "  checkpoint, before the save chunk."), name))
}

#' Print the Stage 1 pivot point.
.report_pivot1 <- function() {
  if (exists("pivot1")) {
    cat(sprintf("pivot1 (Stage 1 footprint centre): (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
                pivot1[1], pivot1[2], pivot1[3]))
  } else {
    cat("pivot1 NOT available.\n")
  }
}

# ============================================================
# Run tally - one cumulative record of how many things survived each filter
#
# Every stage prints its own counts, but those printouts vanish with the render
# and cannot be compared across runs. .tally() writes the same numbers into a
# single named list, `run_counts`, that travels in the checkpoints and is read
# out whole by the Stage 6 error report. A run then answers "how many pairs
# reached the Z-translation" without anyone re-reading five HTML files.
#
# Cumulative and idempotent: each call updates only the keys it names, so
# re-running one chunk refreshes that chunk's numbers and leaves the rest alone.
# It never errors - a tally is bookkeeping, and a missing count must not be able
# to stop a stage from saving.
# ============================================================
.tally <- function(...) {
  vals <- list(...)
  e    <- .stage_env()
  base <- if (exists("run_counts", envir = e, inherits = FALSE))
            get("run_counts", envir = e) else list()
  assign("run_counts", utils::modifyList(base, vals), envir = e)
  invisible(get("run_counts", envir = e))
}

# ============================================================
# Progress bars
#
# Thin wrappers around cli, using EXACTLY the idiom Stage 3's axis-RANSAC fit
# has always used, because that one works when these documents are run on their
# own. Their only job is to save repeating the same six lines at every long
# loop.
#
# THE ONE THING THAT MUST NOT BE CHANGED HERE is `.envir = parent.frame()`.
# cli ties a progress bar's lifetime to a frame and tears the bar down when
# that frame exits. .pb_new() is a function, so a bar created with cli's
# default `.envir` would be created and immediately destroyed the moment
# .pb_new returned - the loop then ticks a bar that no longer exists and
# nothing is ever drawn. parent.frame() hands the bar to the CALLER's frame,
# which is the loop, and is the difference between this working and silently
# doing nothing. (An earlier revision passed globalenv() here, which is why the
# bars added through this helper never appeared while the hand-written ones in
# 3.3, 3.6 and 3.9 did.)
#
# Under the batch driver these will NOT be visible: cli draws on stderr, and
# the driver holds a message sink, which cannot be split. That is expected and
# is not worked around here - the driver prints its own progress instead.
# ============================================================
# 1.0.x  Local stem lean: one predictor, used by both the consensus filter
#        and the masked refit
#
# WHY THIS EXISTS
#
# Both steps previously assumed the stem is VERTICAL between adjacent slices,
# and both were wrong in the same way.
#
#   The consensus filter compared raw adjacent centres against a tolerance of
#   frac_c x semi_minor. On a stem leaning theta with slice step s, the centre
#   MUST move s * tan(theta) between neighbours - that is geometry, not error.
#   At the Stage 1A step of 0.40 m and a 20 deg lean the expected offset is
#   ~0.15 m against a tolerance of ~0.03 m, so the test failed on every pair of
#   a perfectly fitted leaning stem. It was measuring lean, not agreement.
#
#   The masked refit placed its circle at the ANCHOR's centre, at the anchor's
#   height. Displaced by ~0.15 m with a radius of ~0.09 m, that mask can enclose
#   nothing but air - which is where the too_few_pts and fit_failed refit
#   statuses were coming from.
#
# One predictor fixes both, and it must be the SAME one: if the filter and the
# refit disagreed about where the stem is, the refit would be fed slices the
# filter rejected for being where the refit expects them.
#
# ROBUSTNESS
#
# The slope is a Theil-Sen estimate - the median of pairwise slopes - not a
# least-squares fit. That matters more here than anywhere else in this file: at
# consensus time NOTHING has been cleaned yet, so the centres being fitted
# include the very outliers the filter is about to remove. Least squares would
# let one wild centre drag the predicted lean toward itself and so excuse the
# outlier that caused it. Theil-Sen tolerates up to ~29% bad points before its
# median breaks down.
# ============================================================

#' Theil-Sen slope: the median of all pairwise slopes.
#'
#' Returns NA when fewer than two points have distinct z.
.ts_slope <- function(z, v) {
  ok <- is.finite(z) & is.finite(v)
  z <- z[ok]; v <- v[ok]
  n <- length(z)
  if (n < 2L) return(NA_real_)
  ij <- utils::combn(n, 2L)
  dz <- z[ij[2L, ]] - z[ij[1L, ]]
  dv <- v[ij[2L, ]] - v[ij[1L, ]]
  keep <- abs(dz) > 1e-9
  if (!any(keep)) return(NA_real_)
  stats::median(dv[keep] / dz[keep])
}

#' Local lean (dx/dz, dy/dz) around a height, from a set of usable centres.
#'
#' @param z,cx,cy  Slice heights and centres, same length.
#' @param usable   Logical: which entries may be fitted.
#' @param z0       Height the lean is wanted at.
#' @param exclude  Indices to withhold from the fit. For the consensus test this
#'                 is the PAIR being judged: a pair allowed into its own
#'                 reference fit would help predict itself, and two adjacent
#'                 outliers sharing an error would then validate each other.
#' @param k_side   Most centres to take from each side.
#' @param bracket  If TRUE and both sides have centres, take from both -
#'                 interpolating between them rather than extrapolating from
#'                 one, which is markedly more accurate.
#'
#' @return list(sx, sy, cx0, cy0, n_used, span, resid_rms, mode). `mode` is
#'         "bracket", "below", "above" or "none"; on "none" the slope is 0,
#'         i.e. the old vertical assumption, so a stem with too little context
#'         degrades to previous behaviour rather than failing.
.local_lean <- function(z, cx, cy, usable, z0,
                        exclude = integer(0),
                        k_side  = 4L,
                        bracket = TRUE) {

  none <- list(sx = 0, sy = 0, cx0 = NA_real_, cy0 = NA_real_,
               n_used = 0L, span = NA_real_, resid_rms = NA_real_, mode = "none")

  ok <- which(usable & is.finite(z) & is.finite(cx) & is.finite(cy))
  ok <- setdiff(ok, exclude)
  if (length(ok) < 2L) return(none)

  below <- ok[z[ok] <  z0]
  above <- ok[z[ok] >= z0]
  # Nearest first, so "k_side nearest" means nearest in height, not in index.
  below <- below[order(z0 - z[below])]
  above <- above[order(z[above] - z0)]

  if (bracket && length(below) >= 1L && length(above) >= 1L) {
    used <- c(utils::head(below, k_side), utils::head(above, k_side))
    mode <- "bracket"
  } else if (length(below) >= 2L) {
    # One-sided: allow twice as many, since extrapolation needs a longer base
    # to pin the slope down than interpolation does.
    used <- utils::head(below, 2L * k_side)
    mode <- "below"
  } else if (length(above) >= 2L) {
    used <- utils::head(above, 2L * k_side)
    mode <- "above"
  } else {
    return(none)
  }

  zu <- z[used]; xu <- cx[used]; yu <- cy[used]
  if (diff(range(zu)) < 1e-9) return(none)

  sx <- .ts_slope(zu, xu)
  sy <- .ts_slope(zu, yu)
  if (!is.finite(sx) || !is.finite(sy)) return(none)

  # Robust intercept to match the robust slope: a mean here would reintroduce
  # the outlier sensitivity Theil-Sen was chosen to avoid.
  cx0 <- stats::median(xu - sx * zu)
  cy0 <- stats::median(yu - sy * zu)

  rx <- xu - (cx0 + sx * zu)
  ry <- yu - (cy0 + sy * zu)
  resid_rms <- sqrt(mean(rx^2 + ry^2))

  list(sx = sx, sy = sy, cx0 = cx0, cy0 = cy0,
       n_used = length(used), span = diff(range(zu)),
       resid_rms = resid_rms, mode = mode)
}

#' Centre predicted at z0 by a local lean fit. NA when the fit found no context.
.local_centre <- function(fit, z0) {
  if (identical(fit$mode, "none") || !is.finite(fit$cx0))
    return(c(NA_real_, NA_real_))
  c(fit$cx0 + fit$sx * z0, fit$cy0 + fit$sy * z0)
}


#' TRUE when a cli bar can actually be seen.
#'
#' All four conditions matter: cli absent, output being knitted, a message sink
#' in the way (the batch driver), or a terminal that cannot redraw - any one of
#' them and the bar is invisible, mangled, or both.
.pb_cli_usable <- function() {
  isNamespaceLoaded("cli") || requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE)
  requireNamespace("cli", quietly = TRUE) &&
    !isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress")) &&
    sink.number(type = "message") == 0L &&
    isTRUE(try(cli::is_dynamic_tty(), silent = TRUE))
}

.pb_fmt_dur <- function(s) {
  if (!is.finite(s)) return("--")
  if (s < 90) sprintf("%.0fs", s) else if (s < 5400) sprintf("%.1fm", s / 60)
  else sprintf("%.1fh", s / 3600)
}

#' Start a bar. Returns an opaque handle for .pb_tick()/.pb_done(), or NULL.
#'
#' .envir = parent.frame() is load-bearing for the cli branch: cli ties a bar's
#' lifetime to a frame, so a bar created with the default .envir would be torn
#' down the instant this function returned and every later tick would silently
#' do nothing. That was a real bug here once.
.pb_new <- function(total, label) {
  total <- as.integer(total)
  if (!isTRUE(show_progress_bars) || is.na(total) || total < 1L) return(NULL)

  if (.pb_cli_usable()) {
    id <- cli::cli_progress_bar(
      name   = label,
      total  = total,
      format = paste0(label,
                      " {cli::pb_bar} {cli::pb_current}/{cli::pb_total}",
                      " | {cli::pb_elapsed} | {cli::pb_eta} left"),
      .envir = parent.frame())
    return(structure(list(kind = "cli", id = id), class = ".pb"))
  }

  # An ENVIRONMENT, not a list: a tick inside lapply() has to update the
  # caller's counter, and a list passed by value would not.
  st <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
  st$i <- 0L; st$total <- total; st$label <- label
  st$t0 <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]; st$last_t <- -Inf; st$last_i <- -1L
  structure(list(kind = "lines", st = st), class = ".pb")
}

.pb_tick <- function(pb, by = 1L) {
  if (is.null(pb)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (identical(pb$kind, "cli")) {
    cli::cli_progress_update(id = pb$id, inc = by)
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  st <- pb$st
  st$i <- st$i + by
  now <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  step <- max(1L, as.integer(ceiling(st$total * progress_step_frac)))
  due  <- st$i >= st$total || st$i == 1L ||
          (st$i - st$last_i) >= step ||
          (now - st$last_t) >= progress_min_seconds
  if (!due) return(invisible(NULL))
  st$last_i <- st$i; st$last_t <- now
  el   <- now - st$t0
  frac <- st$i / st$total
  eta  <- if (st$i > 0L) el / st$i * (st$total - st$i) else NA_real_
  nfill <- as.integer(round(20 * frac))
  cat(sprintf("  %s [%s%s] %d/%d %3.0f%% | %s elapsed | ~%s left\n",
              st$label, strrep("#", nfill), strrep("-", 20L - nfill),
              st$i, st$total, 100 * frac, .pb_fmt_dur(el), .pb_fmt_dur(eta)))
  flush.console()
  invisible(NULL)
}

.pb_done <- function(pb) {
  if (is.null(pb)) return(invisible(NULL))
  if (identical(pb$kind, "cli")) {
    cli::cli_progress_done(id = pb$id)
  } else if (pb$st$i < pb$st$total) {
    # The loop ended early (an epoch with nothing to do, say). Say so rather
    # than leaving a bar stopped at 12/25 as though something had hung.
    cat(sprintf("  %s: finished after %d of %d | %s\n", pb$st$label, pb$st$i,
                pb$st$total, .pb_fmt_dur(proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - pb$st$t0)))
  }
  invisible(NULL)
}
```

## 0.4 Thread Configuration and Source RANSAC Library

```{r}
#| label: params-thread-config
```

## 0.5 Ellipse Pipeline Functions

The consensus + MAD cleaner, the masked refit and the second-pass cleaner are
used in two places now: the Stage 1A alignment fit that follows, and the main
Step 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 pipeline. Their pure function definitions live here, once,
so both callers share identical behaviour. The Step 1.2 / 1.3 / 1.4 chunks keep
only their own parameter blocks and run logic and call these definitions. This
chunk sits after the RANSAC library is sourced (0.7), so the refit can call
`custom_ransac_ellipse_fit`.

```{r}
#| label: ellipse-pipeline-functions
#| code-summary: "Shared fit/clean/refit/reclean functions + a one-cloud pipeline wrapper"

# ── Stage A implementation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
.consensus_flag_one <- function(df, frac_c, frac_maj, frac_min,
                                max_gap = NULL, sort_axes = TRUE,
                                tol_floor = NULL, tol_cap = NULL,
                                use_local_lean = TRUE, lean_k = 4L) {

  n <- nrow(df)
  if (n == 0L) return(df)

  fitted <- !is.na(df$center_x) & !is.na(df$center_y) &
            !is.na(df$semi_a)   & !is.na(df$semi_b)   & !is.na(df$slice_z)

  maj  <- if (sort_axes) pmax(df$semi_a, df$semi_b) else df$semi_a
  min_ <- if (sort_axes) pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b) else df$semi_b

  .clamp <- function(t) {
    if (!is.null(tol_floor)) t <- max(t, tol_floor)
    if (!is.null(tol_cap))   t <- min(t, tol_cap)
    t
  }

  agrees  <- rep(FALSE, n)
  n_agree <- rep(0L,    n)

  # Per-slice record of the lean correction actually applied, for the
  # diagnostics and so a run can be audited without re-deriving anything.
  lean_mag  <- rep(NA_real_, n)   # |(dx/dz, dy/dz)| used for this slice
  lean_pred <- rep(NA_real_, n)   # predicted centre displacement removed, m
  lean_mode <- rep(NA_character_, n)

  tol_c_used   <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  tol_min_used <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  tol_maj_used <- rep(NA_real_, n)

  idx <- which(fitted)
  if (length(idx) >= 2L) {
    ord <- idx[order(df$slice_z[idx])]
    for (k in seq_len(length(ord) - 1L)) {
      i <- ord[k]; j <- ord[k + 1L]

      gap <- abs(df$slice_z[j] - df$slice_z[i])
      if (!is.null(max_gap) && gap > max_gap) next

      tol_c   <- .clamp(frac_c   * mean(c(min_[i], min_[j])))
      tol_min <- .clamp(frac_min * min(min_[i], min_[j]))
      tol_maj <- .clamp(frac_maj * min(maj[i],  maj[j]))

      tol_c_used[c(i, j)]   <- pmax(tol_c_used[c(i, j)],   tol_c,   na.rm = TRUE)
      tol_min_used[c(i, j)] <- pmax(tol_min_used[c(i, j)], tol_min, na.rm = TRUE)
      tol_maj_used[c(i, j)] <- pmax(tol_maj_used[c(i, j)], tol_maj, na.rm = TRUE)

      # ── Centre agreement, measured against the LOCAL LEAN ─────────────────
      # The raw offset between adjacent centres is dominated by the stem's lean:
      # it must be step * tan(theta) even on a flawless fit. So the lean is
      # predicted from the surrounding slices - with THIS PAIR withheld, or the
      # pair would help predict itself and two neighbours sharing an error would
      # validate each other.
      #
      # BOTH i and j are checked against the robust local fit's OWN intercept
      # (.local_centre), each at its own height, rather than comparing j to a
      # prediction anchored on i's raw centre. Anchoring on i (the previous
      # approach) has two failure modes: if i is bad, projecting the slope
      # forward from i's bad position can still land near a genuinely bad j
      # sharing a similar-direction error, so two adjacent outliers validate
      # each other; conversely, testing only j against the fit's intercept
      # (independent of i) lets a bad i ride through for free whenever its
      # OTHER neighbour j happens to be good, since j's own agreement no longer
      # depends on i at all. Requiring each point to independently sit within
      # tolerance of the surrounding robust trend avoids both: a slice must
      # match the trend on its own merits to count as agreeing, and a pair can
      # no longer validate itself just because the trend was fit around it.
      #
      # When there is too little context to fit a lean (.local_centre returns
      # NA), fall back to the raw i-to-j distance with a zero slope, which
      # reduces exactly to the old raw-distance test, so a short stem or a
      # sparse neighbourhood behaves as before rather than failing.
      if (isTRUE(use_local_lean)) {
        lf <- .local_lean(df$slice_z, df$center_x, df$center_y,
                          usable  = fitted,
                          z0      = df$slice_z[j],
                          exclude = c(i, j),
                          k_side  = lean_k)
        dz_ij <- df$slice_z[j] - df$slice_z[i]
        pc_i  <- .local_centre(lf, df$slice_z[i])
        pc_j  <- .local_centre(lf, df$slice_z[j])

        if (is.finite(pc_i[1]) && is.finite(pc_j[1])) {
          d_i <- sqrt((df$center_x[i] - pc_i[1])^2 + (df$center_y[i] - pc_i[2])^2)
          d_j <- sqrt((df$center_x[j] - pc_j[1])^2 + (df$center_y[j] - pc_j[2])^2)
          d_centre <- max(d_i, d_j)
        } else {
          d_centre <- sqrt((df$center_x[j] - df$center_x[i])^2 +
                           (df$center_y[j] - df$center_y[i])^2)
        }

        .lm <- sqrt(lf$sx^2 + lf$sy^2)
        .lp <- abs(dz_ij) * .lm
        lean_mag[c(i, j)]  <- .lm
        lean_pred[c(i, j)] <- .lp
        lean_mode[c(i, j)] <- lf$mode
      } else {
        d_centre <- sqrt((df$center_x[j] - df$center_x[i])^2 +
                         (df$center_y[j] - df$center_y[i])^2)
      }

      ok <- d_centre               <= tol_c   &&
            abs(min_[j] - min_[i]) <= tol_min &&
            abs(maj[j]  - maj[i])  <= tol_maj

      if (ok) {
        agrees[i] <- TRUE; agrees[j] <- TRUE
        n_agree[i] <- n_agree[i] + 1L
        n_agree[j] <- n_agree[j] + 1L
      }
    }
  }

  # Semi-minor as used by both stages, stored so Stage B and the diagnostics
  # score exactly the value the consensus test compared (respects sort_axes).
  df$minor_len <- ifelse(fitted, min_, NA_real_)
  df$major_len <- ifelse(fitted, maj,  NA_real_)

  df$n_agreeing   <- n_agree
  df$lean_mag     <- lean_mag
  df$lean_pred_m  <- lean_pred
  df$lean_mode    <- lean_mode
  df$tol_centre   <- tol_c_used
  df$tol_minor    <- tol_min_used
  df$tol_major    <- tol_maj_used
  df$no_consensus <- fitted & !agrees
  df$unfitted     <- !fitted

  if (!"ell_ecc" %in% names(df)) {
    a_ <- pmax(df$semi_a, df$semi_b); b_ <- pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b)
    df$ell_ecc <- sqrt(pmax(0, 1 - (b_ / a_)^2))
  }

  df
}

# ── Stage B implementation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Scores the semi-minor axis of the consensus survivors against that stem's own
# median, using MAD (constant = 1.4826, so it estimates sigma for normal data).
# A near-zero MAD means the values are effectively identical – the test is then
# skipped rather than flagging everything.
.mad_minor_flag_one <- function(df, mult, min_n) {

  n <- nrow(df)
  df$mad_minor_z   <- NA_real_
  df$mad_minor_out <- rep(FALSE, n)
  if (n == 0L) return(df)

  eligible <- !df$unfitted & !df$no_consensus & !is.na(df$minor_len)
  if (sum(eligible) < min_n) return(df)

  b   <- df$minor_len[eligible]
  med <- median(b, na.rm = TRUE)
  m   <- mad(b, center = med, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m) || m < 1e-12) return(df)

  df$mad_minor_z[eligible]   <- (b - med) / m
  df$mad_minor_out[eligible] <- abs(b - med) > mult * m

  df
}

# ── Stage C implementation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The same MAD rule on the semi-major axis, scored over the slices still
# standing after Stage B. Eligibility excludes mad_minor_out, so a slice already
# removed for its semi-minor is neither re-flagged nor allowed to influence this
# median – the semi-major test sees only the population it is judging.
.mad_major_flag_one <- function(df, mult, min_n) {

  n <- nrow(df)
  df$mad_major_z   <- NA_real_
  df$mad_major_out <- rep(FALSE, n)
  if (n == 0L) return(df)

  minor_out <- if ("mad_minor_out" %in% names(df)) df$mad_minor_out else rep(FALSE, n)

  eligible <- !df$unfitted & !df$no_consensus & !minor_out & !is.na(df$major_len)
  if (sum(eligible) < min_n) return(df)

  a   <- df$major_len[eligible]
  med <- median(a, na.rm = TRUE)
  m   <- mad(a, center = med, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m) || m < 1e-12) return(df)

  df$mad_major_z[eligible]   <- (a - med) / m
  df$mad_major_out[eligible] <- abs(a - med) > mult * m

  df
}

.consensus_clean <- function(raw_list, frac_c, frac_maj, frac_min,
                             max_gap = NULL, sort_axes = TRUE,
                             tol_floor = NULL, tol_cap = NULL,
                             do_mad = TRUE, mad_mult = 3.0, mad_min_n = 5L,
                             do_mad_maj = TRUE, mad_maj_mult = 3.0,
                             mad_maj_min_n = 5L,
                             use_local_lean = TRUE, lean_k = 4L) {

  lapply(raw_list, function(df) {
    if (is.null(df)) df <- data.frame()

    flagged <- .consensus_flag_one(df, frac_c, frac_maj, frac_min,
                                   max_gap, sort_axes, tol_floor, tol_cap,
                                   use_local_lean = use_local_lean,
                                   lean_k         = lean_k)

    flagged <- if (do_mad && nrow(flagged) > 0L)
      .mad_minor_flag_one(flagged, mad_mult, mad_min_n) else {
        flagged$mad_minor_z   <- NA_real_
        flagged$mad_minor_out <- rep(FALSE, nrow(flagged))
        flagged
      }

    flagged <- if (do_mad_maj && nrow(flagged) > 0L)
      .mad_major_flag_one(flagged, mad_maj_mult, mad_maj_min_n) else {
        flagged$mad_major_z   <- NA_real_
        flagged$mad_major_out <- rep(FALSE, nrow(flagged))
        flagged
      }

    # ── Flag names the plotting helpers expect ────────────────────────────────
    # Consensus failures drive the XY-centre panels; MAD failures drive the
    # semi-axis panels, so the two removals are visually separable there too.
    # spike_b tracks the semi-minor stage and spike_a the semi-major stage, so
    # the two axis panels each show the removals that its own axis caused.
    if (nrow(flagged) > 0L) {
      flagged$spike_cx    <- flagged$no_consensus
      flagged$spike_cy    <- flagged$no_consensus
      flagged$spike_xy    <- flagged$no_consensus
      flagged$spike_b     <- flagged$mad_minor_out
      flagged$spike_a     <- flagged$mad_major_out
      flagged$spike_radii <- flagged$mad_minor_out | flagged$mad_major_out
      flagged$spike       <- flagged$no_consensus | flagged$unfitted |
                             flagged$mad_minor_out | flagged$mad_major_out
      flagged$isolated    <- FALSE
    }

    valid  <- if (nrow(flagged)) flagged[!flagged$spike, , drop = FALSE] else flagged
    before <- nrow(flagged)

    list(
      flagged            = flagged,
      valid              = valid,
      ellipses_before    = before,
      ellipses_after     = nrow(valid),
      n_removed_unfitted = if (before) sum(flagged$unfitted,      na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
      n_removed_orphan   = if (before) sum(flagged$no_consensus,  na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
      n_removed_mad      = if (before) sum(flagged$mad_minor_out, na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
      n_removed_mad_maj  = if (before) sum(flagged$mad_major_out, na.rm = TRUE) else 0L,
      med_tol_centre     = if (before) median(flagged$tol_centre, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
      med_lean_mag       = if (before) median(flagged$lean_mag,    na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
      med_lean_pred_m    = if (before) median(flagged$lean_pred_m, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
      prop_kept          = if (before > 0L) nrow(valid) / before else NA_real_
    )
  })
}

.print_consensus_summary <- function(clean_result, label) {
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("\n[%s] Cleaning - consensus (adaptive), MAD semi-minor, MAD semi-major\n",
           "      centre <= %.0f%% of mean semi-minor | ",
           "minor <= %.0f%% of lower semi-minor | ",
           "major <= %.0f%% of lower semi-major\n",
           "      MAD semi-minor: %s (mult = %.1f, min n = %d)\n",
           "      MAD semi-major: %s (mult = %.1f, min n = %d)\n"),
    label, consensus_frac_centre * 100,
    consensus_frac_minor * 100, consensus_frac_major * 100,
    if (run_mad_minor) "on" else "off", mad_minor_mult, mad_minor_min_n,
    if (run_mad_major) "on" else "off", mad_major_mult, mad_major_min_n))

  if (!is.null(consensus_tol_floor) || !is.null(consensus_tol_cap))
    cat(sprintf("      guard rails: floor %s | cap %s\n",
                if (is.null(consensus_tol_floor)) "-" else sprintf("%.3f m", consensus_tol_floor),
                if (is.null(consensus_tol_cap))   "-" else sprintf("%.3f m", consensus_tol_cap)))

  tab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
    r <- clean_result[[tid]]
    data.frame(TreeID = tid,
               before = r$ellipses_before,
               unfit  = r$n_removed_unfitted,
               orphan = r$n_removed_orphan,
               madB   = r$n_removed_mad,
               madA   = r$n_removed_mad_maj,
               kept   = r$ellipses_after,
               lean   = round(r$med_lean_mag, 4),      # median |dc/dz| used
               leanm  = round(r$med_lean_pred_m, 4),   # median lean offset removed, m
               pct    = round(100 * r$prop_kept, 1),
               tol_cm = round(100 * r$med_tol_centre, 2),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
  if (is.null(tab) || nrow(tab) == 0L) { cat("  (no trees)\n"); return(invisible(NULL)) }

  print(tab, row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("  TOTAL: %d in -> %d kept (%.1f%%) | %d unfitted, %d orphaned, %d MAD semi-minor, %d MAD semi-major\n",
              sum(tab$before), sum(tab$kept),
              100 * sum(tab$kept) / max(1L, sum(tab$before)),
              sum(tab$unfit), sum(tab$orphan), sum(tab$madB), sum(tab$madA)))
  cat("  madB = removed by the semi-minor stage | madA = by the semi-major stage\n")
  cat("  tol_cm = median centre tolerance actually applied, per tree (cm)\n")
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("  lean  = median local |dc/dz| the centre test corrected for\n",
           "  leanm = median centre displacement that lean accounts for over one step (m).\n",
           "          Compare with tol_cm/100: where leanm exceeds it, the OLD raw-distance\n",
           "          test was rejecting slices for leaning rather than for disagreeing.\n"
  )))
  invisible(tab)
}
# ── Refit one tree ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Targets are processed from the BOTTOM UP. Each one looks for the nearest
# available slice BELOW it; only if none exists does it look above. "Available"
# means kept by cleaning OR successfully refit earlier in this same loop, so a
# refit cascades upward through a run of consecutive failures.
#
# Projection follows the stem's LOCAL LEAN, not the vertical. The mask centre is
# the anchor's measured centre plus lean * dz, the lean coming from .local_lean()
# - the same predictor the consensus filter uses, so the refit looks for the stem
# where the filter expects it. Stage 1 has no global stem-axis vector (Stage 2
# solves that), but it does not need one: the lean is estimated locally from the
# kept centres bracketing the target slice.
#
# This replaced a vertical projection, which carried the anchor's centre straight
# up. Over a 0.4 m step at a 20 deg lean that misses by ~0.15 m - further than
# the mask radius itself - so the mask enclosed air and the fit returned
# too_few_pts or fit_failed. It was never something a slightly larger mask factor
# could absorb.
.refit_one_tree <- function(pts_tree, tid, flagged, width,
                            mask_scale, min_pts, seed,
                            dist_thr, n_iter, early_exit,
                            include_mad, track_hist = TRUE,
                            iter_pp = NULL, iter_mx = 1000L, iter_mn = 1L,
                            # ── Local-lean mask placement ─────────────────────
                            # k centres per side for the axis fit; bracketing
                            # (both sides) is preferred over extrapolation.
                            lean_k        = 4L,
                            use_local_lean = TRUE,
                            # Mask radius padding for prediction uncertainty, as
                            # a multiple of the axis fit's residual RMS. The
                            # further the prediction reaches, the wider the mask
                            # has to be to still contain the stem.
                            pred_pad_mult = 2.0,
                            # Floor on the mask radius, as a fraction of this
                            # stem's own median semi-major. Stops one
                            # spuriously tiny anchor ellipse from shrinking the
                            # mask to a few centimetres and starving the refit.
                            r_floor_frac  = 0.75) {

  df <- as.data.frame(flagged)
  n  <- nrow(df)

  df$refit          <- rep(FALSE, n)
  df$refit_status   <- rep(NA_character_, n)   # ok | no_anchor | too_few_pts | fit_failed
  df$refit_anchor_z <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  df$refit_mask_r   <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  df$refit_n_masked <- rep(NA_integer_, n)
  # Where the mask went, and why - so a failed refit can be diagnosed without
  # re-running it.
  df$refit_mask_x   <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  df$refit_mask_y   <- rep(NA_real_, n)
  df$refit_lean_mode <- rep(NA_character_, n)   # bracket | below | above | none
  df$refit_lean_n    <- rep(NA_integer_, n)
  df$refit_pred_shift <- rep(NA_real_, n)       # mask offset vs the old anchor-centre placement

  if (n == 0L) return(df)

  # Slices eligible to serve as anchors at the start: everything cleaning kept.
  available <- !df$spike & !is.na(df$center_x)

  target <- df$no_consensus & !df$unfitted
  if (include_mad && "mad_minor_out" %in% names(df))
    target <- target | (df$mad_minor_out & !df$unfitted)
  if (include_mad && "mad_major_out" %in% names(df))
    target <- target | (df$mad_major_out & !df$unfitted)
  if (!any(target)) return(df)

  # Bottom-up, so a refit slice can anchor the slice above it.
  for (t in order(df$slice_z)[order(df$slice_z) %in% which(target)]) {

    z_t <- df$slice_z[t]

    # ── Pick the anchor: nearest below, else nearest above ───────────────────
    avail_idx <- which(available)
    if (length(avail_idx) == 0L) { df$refit_status[t] <- "no_anchor"; next }

    below <- avail_idx[df$slice_z[avail_idx] <  z_t]
    above <- avail_idx[df$slice_z[avail_idx] >  z_t]

    anchor <- if (length(below) > 0L) below[which.max(df$slice_z[below])] else
              if (length(above) > 0L) above[which.min(df$slice_z[above])] else NA_integer_

    if (is.na(anchor)) { df$refit_status[t] <- "no_anchor"; next }

    # ── Place the mask on the PREDICTED stem centre at this height ───────────
    # Not at the anchor's centre. A leaning stem moves step * tan(theta) between
    # slices, so an anchor-centred mask is displaced by more than its own radius
    # at Stage 1A's 0.40 m step and any appreciable lean, and encloses nothing
    # but air. That was the source of the too_few_pts and fit_failed statuses.
    #
    # The lean comes from .local_lean, the same predictor the consensus filter
    # uses - deliberately the same, so the refit looks for the stem where the
    # filter expects it to be. Slices ABOVE the target are eligible too, so a
    # gap in the middle of a stem is bracketed (interpolated) rather than
    # extrapolated across; only a gap at an end forces one-sided extrapolation.
    #
    # `available` is the usable set: cleaning survivors, plus anything already
    # refit successfully below, since the loop runs bottom-up.
    lf <- if (isTRUE(use_local_lean))
            .local_lean(df$slice_z, df$center_x, df$center_y,
                        usable  = available,
                        z0      = z_t,
                        k_side  = lean_k)
          else list(sx = 0, sy = 0, cx0 = NA_real_, cy0 = NA_real_,
                    n_used = 0L, span = NA_real_, resid_rms = NA_real_,
                    mode = "none")

    # Anchor the prediction on the anchor slice and lean from there, rather than
    # on the fit's own robust intercept. The intercept is extrapolated from the
    # whole window and can sit a long way off when the window is short; the
    # anchor is a real measured centre and is the nearest one there is.
    cx_m <- df$center_x[anchor] + lf$sx * (z_t - df$slice_z[anchor])
    cy_m <- df$center_y[anchor] + lf$sy * (z_t - df$slice_z[anchor])

    # ── Mask radius ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Three terms, each guarding a different failure:
    #   the anchor's own semi-major   - the stem's size here
    #   a floor from the stem median  - a tiny bad anchor cannot starve the refit
    #   a pad from the fit residual   - the further the prediction reaches, the
    #                                   less certain it is
    .r_med   <- stats::median(df$semi_a[available], na.rm = TRUE)
    .r_base  <- max(df$semi_a[anchor],
                    if (is.finite(.r_med)) r_floor_frac * .r_med else 0)
    .pad     <- if (is.finite(lf$resid_rms)) pred_pad_mult * lf$resid_rms else 0
    r_m      <- .r_base * mask_scale + .pad

    df$refit_anchor_z[t]    <- df$slice_z[anchor]
    df$refit_mask_r[t]      <- r_m
    df$refit_mask_x[t]      <- cx_m
    df$refit_mask_y[t]      <- cy_m
    df$refit_lean_mode[t]   <- lf$mode
    df$refit_lean_n[t]      <- lf$n_used
    df$refit_pred_shift[t]  <- sqrt((cx_m - df$center_x[anchor])^2 +
                                    (cy_m - df$center_y[anchor])^2)

    # ── Slice window, matching the first pass exactly ────────────────────────
    # ransac_ellipse_fit_one() takes Z in [zi, zi + width) and records
    # slice_z = zi + width/2, so the window is recovered as below.
    z_lo <- z_t - width / 2
    pts_i <- pts_tree[pts_tree$Z >= z_lo & pts_tree$Z < z_lo + width, , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(pts_i) == 0L) { df$refit_status[t] <- "too_few_pts"
                             df$refit_n_masked[t] <- 0L; next }

    # ── Apply the circular mask ──────────────────────────────────────────────
    inside <- (pts_i$X - cx_m)^2 + (pts_i$Y - cy_m)^2 <= r_m^2
    pts_m  <- pts_i[inside, , drop = FALSE]
    df$refit_n_masked[t] <- nrow(pts_m)

    if (nrow(pts_m) < min_pts) { df$refit_status[t] <- "too_few_pts"; next }

    # ── Second-pass RANSAC on the masked points ──────────────────────────────
    # Seeded on (seed, TreeID, slice index) so a refit is reproducible
    # independently of how many other slices were refit before it.
    set.seed(as.integer(seed) + as.integer(tid) * 1000L + t)

    rr <- tryCatch(
      custom_ransac_ellipse_fit(
        pts_m[, c("X", "Y")],
        n_iterations       = n_iter,
        iter_per_point     = iter_pp,
        iter_max           = iter_mx,
        iter_min           = iter_mn,
        distance_threshold = dist_thr,
        early_exit         = early_exit,
        track_history      = track_hist
      ),
      error = function(e) list(ellipse = rep(NA_real_, 5), inliers = integer(0),
                               inlier_history = integer(0),
                               segs_history   = integer(0),
                               n_points       = nrow(pts_m))
    )

    ell <- rr$ellipse
    if (length(ell) < 5L || is.na(ell[3])) { df$refit_status[t] <- "fit_failed"; next }

    # ── Write the new geometry back ──────────────────────────────────────────
    df$center_x[t]  <- ell[1]
    df$center_y[t]  <- ell[2]
    df$semi_a[t]    <- ell[3]
    df$semi_b[t]    <- ell[4]
    df$angle_deg[t] <- ell[5]

    if ("inlier_ids" %in% names(df))
      df$inlier_ids[[t]] <- if (length(rr$inliers) > 0L)
        pts_m$point_id[rr$inliers] else integer(0)

    # NOTE: slice_point_ids now holds the MASKED candidate set for this slice,
    # not the full slice. Anything that treats it as "every point RANSAC could
    # have chosen from" (the threshold-sensitivity diagnostic does) will be
    # scoring a narrower set for refit slices.
    if ("slice_point_ids" %in% names(df))
      df$slice_point_ids[[t]] <- pts_m$point_id

    # Convergence record for THIS fit replaces the first pass's, and n_cand_pts
    # becomes the masked count – so the diagnostic's fraction uses the points
    # this fit actually drew from.
    if ("n_cand_pts" %in% names(df))
      df$n_cand_pts[t] <- nrow(pts_m)
    if ("inlier_history" %in% names(df))
      df$inlier_history[[t]] <- if (is.null(rr$inlier_history))
                                  integer(0) else rr$inlier_history
    if ("segs_history" %in% names(df))
      df$segs_history[[t]]   <- if (is.null(rr$segs_history))
                                  integer(0) else rr$segs_history

    df$refit[t]        <- TRUE
    df$refit_status[t] <- "ok"
    available[t]       <- TRUE     # this slice can now anchor the one above
  }

  df
}
.strip_pass1 <- function(d) {
  drop <- c("minor_len", "major_len", "ell_ecc", "n_agreeing",
            "tol_centre", "tol_minor", "tol_major",
            "no_consensus", "unfitted",
            "mad_minor_z", "mad_minor_out",
            "mad_major_z", "mad_major_out",
            "spike_cx", "spike_cy", "spike_xy",
            "spike_a", "spike_b", "spike_radii", "spike", "isolated")
  d[, setdiff(names(d), drop), drop = FALSE]
}

.refit_candidates <- function(refit_flagged) {
  if (is.null(refit_flagged)) return(NULL)
  lapply(refit_flagged, function(d) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(d)
    keep <- (!d$spike) |
            (d$refit & !is.na(d$refit_status) & d$refit_status == "ok")
    .strip_pass1(d[keep, , drop = FALSE])
  })
}

# A stem whose every fitted slice failed pass-1 consensus, and whose refit had
# no anchor to work from, arrives here with zero rows. The MAD helpers assign
# whole columns by value, which R rejects on a zero-row frame, so those stems
# are held back and reinstated afterwards as empty results – keeping their
# TreeID present downstream instead of silently vanishing from the list.
.empty_clean_entry <- function(d) {
  list(
    flagged            = d,
    valid              = d,
    ellipses_before    = 0L,
    ellipses_after     = 0L,
    n_removed_unfitted = 0L,
    n_removed_orphan   = 0L,
    n_removed_mad      = 0L,
    n_removed_mad_maj  = 0L,
    med_tol_centre     = NA_real_,
    prop_kept          = NA_real_
  )
}

.clean2_with_empties <- function(cand, args, label) {
  if (is.null(cand) || length(cand) == 0L) return(NULL)

  n_rows  <- vapply(cand, function(d) if (is.null(d)) 0L else nrow(d), integer(1))
  empties <- names(cand)[n_rows == 0L]

  if (length(empties) > 0L)
    cat(sprintf("[%s] %d stem(s) enter pass 2 with no surviving slices: %s\n",
                label, length(empties), paste(empties, collapse = ", ")))

  res <- if (any(n_rows > 0L))
           do.call(.consensus_clean, c(list(cand[n_rows > 0L]), args)) else list()

  for (tid in empties) res[[tid]] <- .empty_clean_entry(cand[[tid]])

  res[names(cand)]          # restore the original stem order
}

# ============================================================
# One-cloud fit -> clean -> refit -> reclean pipeline
# Packages the exact Step 1.1-1.4 sequence for a single LAS so
# Stage 1A can run it on las_1 with its own slice band and
# parameters. Returns the pass-2 valid ellipse set per stem
# (the same object the main pipeline calls ellipses_zt_*_valid2_all)
# plus every intermediate for inspection.
#
#   clean_args   : named list matching .consensus_clean() arguments
#   refit_args   : list(mask_scale, min_pts, seed, distance_threshold,
#                        n_iterations, early_exit, targets,
#                        iter_per_point, iter_max, iter_min)
#   reclean_args : named list matching .consensus_clean() arguments
# NULL distance_threshold / n_iterations in refit_args inherit fp.
# ============================================================
.fit_clean_refit_reclean <- function(las, label, seed,
                                     slice_bot, slice_top, slice_step,
                                     slice_width, height_min,
                                     distance_threshold,
                                     iter_per_point, iter_max, iter_min,
                                     clean_args, refit_args, reclean_args,
                                     min_ellipses = 5L, track_history = FALSE) {

  fp <- ransac_ellipse_fit_params(
    bot                = slice_bot,
    top                = slice_top,
    height_min         = height_min,
    step               = slice_step,
    width              = slice_width,
    distance_threshold = distance_threshold,
    n_iterations       = 1000L,
    iter_per_point     = iter_per_point,
    iter_max           = iter_max,
    iter_min           = iter_min,
    early_exit         = FALSE,
    track_history      = track_history
  )

  cat(sprintf("[%s] fit: slice %.0f cm / step %.0f cm, %s\n",
              label, slice_width * 100, slice_step * 100,
              if (is.null(slice_top)) "full stem range" else
                sprintf("up to %.1f m", slice_top)))
  # No bar on this call: the per-tree loop is inside the sourced RANSAC library,
  # where nothing here can wrap one. Its formals are checked for a progress
  # argument and it is passed through if one exists; otherwise the elapsed time
  # is reported afterwards so the step is not simply silent. The masked refit
  # below, which is this file's own loop, does get a bar.
  .run_args <- list(las = las, fit_params = fp, clean = FALSE,
                    seed = seed, label = label)
  .pg <- intersect(c("show_progress", "progress", "verbose"),
                   names(formals(ransac_ellipse_run)))
  if (length(.pg)) .run_args[[.pg[1]]] <- isTRUE(show_progress_bars)

  .t_fit <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  res <- do.call(ransac_ellipse_run, .run_args)
  cat(sprintf("[%s] fit done in %.1f min\n", label,
              (proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - .t_fit) / 60))

  windowed <- .filter_min_ellipses(res$raw, label, min_count = min_ellipses)

  # ── Pass 1: consensus + MAD ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
  clean_result <- do.call(.consensus_clean, c(list(windowed), clean_args))

  # ── Masked refit (bottom-up), per tree ───────────────────────────────────────
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(las@data)[, .(TreeID, point_id, X, Y, Z)]
  .rd  <- if (is.null(refit_args$distance_threshold)) fp$distance_threshold else refit_args$distance_threshold
  .ri  <- if (is.null(refit_args$n_iterations))       fp$n_iterations       else refit_args$n_iterations
  .pb_refit <- .pb_new(length(clean_result), sprintf("%s masked refit", label))
  on.exit(.pb_done(.pb_refit), add = TRUE)

  refit_flagged <- setNames(lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
    .pb_tick(.pb_refit)
    pts_tree <- as.data.frame(dt[TreeID == as.integer(tid)])
    .refit_one_tree(pts_tree, tid, clean_result[[tid]]$flagged,
                    width       = fp$width,
                    mask_scale  = refit_args$mask_scale,
                    min_pts     = refit_args$min_pts,
                    seed        = refit_args$seed,
                    dist_thr    = .rd,
                    n_iter      = .ri,
                    early_exit  = refit_args$early_exit,
                    include_mad = identical(refit_args$targets, "consensus_mad"),
                    track_hist  = track_history,
                    iter_pp     = refit_args$iter_per_point,
                    iter_mx     = refit_args$iter_max,
                    iter_mn     = refit_args$iter_min)
  }), names(clean_result))

  # ── Pass 2: reclean the refit survivors ──────────────────────────────────────
  cand   <- .refit_candidates(refit_flagged)
  clean2 <- .clean2_with_empties(cand, reclean_args, label)
  valid2 <- if (is.null(clean2))
              lapply(refit_flagged, function(d)
```
