```{r}
                if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) d else d[!d$spike, , drop = FALSE])
            else lapply(clean2, `[[`, "valid")

  list(fp = fp, raw = res$raw,
       clean_result  = clean_result,
       refit_flagged = refit_flagged,
       clean2        = clean2,
       valid1        = lapply(clean_result, `[[`, "valid"),
       valid2        = valid2)
}
```

## 0.6 Load Point Clouds
```{r}
#| label: load
#| code-summary: "Read LAS files and report point + TreeID counts"

# Step 0.6 - Load Point Clouds

las_1 <- readLAS(las_1_path)
las_2 <- readLAS(las_2_path)

# ── Drop the test-sample generator's marker box ──────────────────────────────
# A cloud from the generator carries sixteen extra points that are not returns:
# eight TargetBox = 1 corners at their truth positions and eight TargetBox = 2
# corners moved by the applied transform. They exist so Stage 6 can measure the
# residual on geometry rather than on a matrix, and Stage 6 reads them from the
# ORIGINAL file on disk (las_1_raw), not from this in-memory cloud - so removing
# them here costs nothing downstream and prevents three separate problems:
#
#   1. point_id is assigned below as seq_len(nrow(...)), so with the markers
#      present the IDs enumerate rows that are not returns. Every later join on
#      point_id then carries sixteen rows that no slice, tree or fit can explain.
#   2. The box-2 corners are the transform's own extremes - at a large tilt they
#      sit far outside the forest - so they inflate the cloud's bounding box.
#      pivot1_auto is the centre of that box, and Stage 1A's sideways-forest test
#      reads its dimensions. Both would be measuring the markers, not the trees.
#   3. Their TreeID is NA, which makes `las@data$TreeID == tid` return NA rather
#      than FALSE for those rows. Where that logical vector reaches a data.frame
#      subset, NA rows come back instead of no rows.
#
# The PivotPoint marker is deliberately NOT dropped here - Step 0.7 needs to read
# it, and drops it itself once it has.
.drop_marker_box <- function(las, label) {
  fld <- "TargetBox"
  if (is.null(las@data[[fld]])) return(las)
  keep <- is.na(las@data[[fld]]) | las@data[[fld]] == 0L
  n_drop <- sum(!keep)
  if (n_drop == 0L) return(las)
  las <- suppressWarnings(lidR::filter_poi(las, keep))
  las <- lidR::las_update(las)
  cat(sprintf("[0.6] Dropped %d %s marker point(s) from %s; %s point(s) remain.\n",
              n_drop, fld, label, format(nrow(las@data), big.mark = ",")))
  las
}
las_1 <- .drop_marker_box(las_1, "las_1")
las_2 <- .drop_marker_box(las_2, "las_2")

# Assign unique point IDs. AFTER the drop, so they enumerate returns only and
# run 1..n with no gaps.
las_1 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(
  las_1,
  x    = seq_len(nrow(las_1@data)),
  name = "point_id",
  desc = "Unique ID for las_1 points"
)

las_2 <- lidR::add_lasattribute(
  las_2,
  x    = seq_len(nrow(las_2@data)),
  name = "point_id",
  desc = "Unique ID for las_2 points"
)

xyz_1 <- as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
xyz_2 <- as.matrix(las_2@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])

# Unique TreeID counts (excluding NA and 0)
treeids_1 <- unique(las_1@data$TreeID)
treeids_1 <- treeids_1[!is.na(treeids_1) & treeids_1 != 0L]

treeids_2 <- unique(las_2@data$TreeID)
treeids_2 <- treeids_2[!is.na(treeids_2) & treeids_2 != 0L]

# Print summary (no warnings, no listing of TreeIDs)
cat(sprintf("las_1: %s points | %d unique TreeID values (NA and 0 not counted)\n",
            format(nrow(xyz_1), big.mark=","), length(treeids_1)))

cat(sprintf("las_2: %s points | %d unique TreeID values (NA and 0 not counted)\n",
            format(nrow(xyz_2), big.mark=","), length(treeids_2)))

.tally(n_points_1 = nrow(xyz_1), n_points_2 = nrow(xyz_2),
       n_treeids_1 = length(treeids_1), n_treeids_2 = length(treeids_2))

```

## 0.7 Select Pivot

`pivot1` is the single rotation origin the whole pipeline turns about - Stage 3
re-slices about it, Stage 6 exports about it. It is not a free parameter: rotating
about a far-off origin turns a fraction of a degree into a translation of hundreds
of metres, so every stage has to agree on the same point.

Three ways to set it.

**`"auto"`** - the mid-point of the cloud's EXTENT in all three axes, the centre
of the bounding box. Not the centroid of the points: a centroid moves whenever
point density changes, so denser canopy on one side or a partially scanned stem
shifts it, while the extent mid-point depends only on where the cloud's outer
limits are and is reproducible from the loaded cloud alone. Because Stage 6
reloads `pivot1` from the checkpoint rather than recomputing it, any drift here
would silently rotate the exported cloud about a different point than Stage 3
used. Computed BEFORE any CSV-based TreeID subsetting in Step 1.1, so it
describes the whole plot rather than just the paired trees. The one weakness: the
cloud is not noise-filtered, so a single stray far-flung return drags the bounding
box. Check the extents printed below look plausible for the stand.

**`"custom"`** - typed in directly, in world coordinates.

**`"las"`** - read from the cloud itself. A cloud produced by the test-sample
generator carries the point it was turned about as a single extra point with the
scalar field `PivotPoint = 1`. Reading it means the pipeline solves its rotation
about the *same* origin the damage was applied about, with no coordinate typed
anywhere and no CSV to keep in step with the file. For a batch of generated
samples this is the mode to use: each pair carries its own pivot, so nothing has
to be looked up per-sample.

That point is then **removed** from `las_1` (see `pivot1_drop_marker`). It is not
a return from a tree - it is a marker - and leaving it in puts a lone point at
the plot centre that widens the cloud extent, joins the forest-axis fit, and gets
written into every export downstream. It has already served its purpose once its
coordinates are read.

**`"csv"`** - the same pivot, but read from the generator's truth CSV rather
than from the cloud. Equivalent to `"las"` up to the LAS scale factor (the CSV
copy is exact, the in-file one is quantised). Useful when the marker point was
stripped from the cloud before it reached here.

None of these modes is *required* for a valid comparison - Stage 6 re-refers both
transforms to the truth pivot regardless - but matching the generator's pivot
removes a lever arm from the error terms and makes the intermediate stage
printouts directly readable against the truth.

```{r}
#| label: params-pivot1
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Resolve pivot1 - bounding-box centre, custom coordinates, or a generator truth CSV"


# "auto" | "custom" | "las" | "csv"
pivot1_mode <- "las"

pivot1_custom <- c(0, 0, 0)

# Used only when pivot1_mode == "las". The scalar field the generator writes.
pivot1_las_field <- "PivotPoint"

# Drop the marker point from las_1 once its coordinates have been read. Leave
# this TRUE unless there is a specific reason to keep a non-return in the cloud.
pivot1_drop_marker <- TRUE

# Used only when pivot1_mode == "csv". The generator's truth CSV for THIS sample.
pivot1_csv_path <- "C:/Users/ascsh/Documents/1_Artemis/11_PaqLab/115_TreeTimeAlign/TestSamples/Generated/SNBG_BOS_F1_Feb2020_March2026_ULS_TLS.csv"

.par_apply("params-pivot1")
```

```{r}
#| label: pivot1
#| code-summary: "Resolve pivot1 - bounding-box centre, custom coordinates, or a generator truth CSV"
#| code-fold: false

# The cloud is measured ONCE, after the switch below - the "las" branch may
# remove a point, and measuring on both sides of that just to report the same
# three ranges twice is two extra passes over a multi-million-point cloud for
# nothing. "auto" therefore resolves after the switch rather than inside it.
pivot1 <- switch(
  pivot1_mode,

  auto = NULL,   # filled in below, from the extents measured after any drop

  custom = {
    v <- as.numeric(pivot1_custom)
    if (length(v) != 3L || anyNA(v))
      stop("[0.7] pivot1_custom must be three finite coordinates.")
    v
  },

  las = {
    if (is.null(las_1@data[[pivot1_las_field]]))
      stop(sprintf(paste0("[0.7] pivot1_mode is \"las\" but las_1 carries no %s field. ",
                          "This cloud was not written by the test-sample generator, or the ",
                          "field was dropped in between. Use \"csv\" or \"auto\"."),
                   pivot1_las_field))

    .mk <- which(!is.na(las_1@data[[pivot1_las_field]]) &
                   las_1@data[[pivot1_las_field]] == 1L)

    # Exactly one, or this is not the marker it claims to be. Zero means the
    # field survived but the point did not; more than one means two generator
    # runs have been merged, and silently averaging them would invent a pivot
    # that neither run used.
    if (length(.mk) != 1L)
      stop(sprintf(paste0("[0.7] Expected exactly one point with %s == 1 in las_1, found %d. ",
                          "Zero: the marker point was filtered out upstream. More than one: ",
                          "two generated samples have been merged into this file."),
                   pivot1_las_field, length(.mk)))

    v <- as.numeric(las_1@data[.mk, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
    cat(sprintf("[0.7] Pivot read from the %s marker point in las_1.\n", pivot1_las_field))

    if (isTRUE(pivot1_drop_marker)) {
      las_1 <- suppressWarnings(lidR::filter_poi(las_1, seq_len(nrow(las_1@data)) != .mk))
      las_1 <- lidR::las_update(las_1)

      # xyz_1 was snapshotted in Step 0.6, one step before this drop, so it is
      # now one row longer than the cloud it is supposed to mirror - a stale
      # snapshot is a trap left lying for the next person to add a step, so it
      # is refreshed where the cloud changes. Dropping the one row beats
      # rebuilding from the data.table: same result, same order, no second
      # full-cloud conversion.
      xyz_1 <- xyz_1[-.mk, , drop = FALSE]

      cat(sprintf("      Marker point removed; las_1 now holds %s point(s).\n",
                  format(nrow(las_1@data), big.mark = ",")))
    } else {
      cat("      Marker point KEPT in las_1 (pivot1_drop_marker = FALSE) - it will widen\n")
      cat("      the cloud extent and take part in the Stage 1A forest-axis fit.\n")
    }
    rm(.mk)
    v
  },

  csv = {
    if (!file.exists(pivot1_csv_path))
      stop("[0.7] Generator truth CSV not found:\n  ", pivot1_csv_path)
    .tr <- utils::read.csv(pivot1_csv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    if (nrow(.tr) != 1L)
      stop(sprintf("[0.7] Truth CSV has %d rows; expected exactly 1. Subset it to this sample.",
                   nrow(.tr)))
    .need <- c("pivot_shifted_x", "pivot_shifted_y", "pivot_shifted_z")
    if (!all(.need %in% names(.tr)))
      stop("[0.7] The CSV carries no pivot_shifted_* columns - it is not a generator truth file.")
    # pivot_shifted, NOT pivot_base: the generator moved the cloud first and
    # turned it about the MOVED pivot, so pivot_shifted is the point that sits
    # inside the sample as it exists on disk. pivot_base belongs to a cloud that
    # was never written.
    v <- as.numeric(.tr[1, .need])
    cat(sprintf("[0.7] Pivot read from %s\n", basename(pivot1_csv_path)))
    if (!is.null(.tr$sample_name))
      cat(sprintf("      sample: %s\n", .tr$sample_name))
    v
  },

  stop('[0.7] pivot1_mode must be "auto", "custom", "las" or "csv".')
)

# ── One pass over the cloud, now that it is final ────────────────────────────
# vapply over the three columns, not as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X","Y","Z")]):
# the matrix form copies the entire cloud to compute three ranges.
.rng <- vapply(c("X", "Y", "Z"),
               function(cl) range(las_1@data[[cl]], na.rm = TRUE),
               numeric(2))                     # row 1 = min, row 2 = max
pivot1_auto <- colMeans(.rng)

if (is.null(pivot1)) pivot1 <- pivot1_auto     # "auto" mode
names(pivot1) <- c("X", "Y", "Z")

cat(sprintf("\n\u2500\u2500 pivot1 (mode: %s) \u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500\n",
            pivot1_mode))
for (.i in 1:3)
  cat(sprintf("  %s extent: [%.4f, %.4f]  (range %.4f m)  -> bbox centre %.4f\n",
              c("X", "Y", "Z")[.i], .rng[1, .i], .rng[2, .i],
              .rng[2, .i] - .rng[1, .i], pivot1_auto[.i]))
cat(sprintf("\n  pivot1 <- c(%.6f, %.6f, %.6f)\n", pivot1[1], pivot1[2], pivot1[3]))
cat("  (Stage 3 and Stage 6 both rotate about this point.)\n")

# ── Is the chosen pivot sane? ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Reported, not enforced. A pivot outside the cloud is legitimate - a shared
# origin across several plots, say - but it is nearly always a typo or the wrong
# CSV row, and the lever arm it creates turns a small rotation error into a large
# displacement. Skipped in "auto" mode, where the offset is zero by construction.
if (!identical(pivot1_mode, "auto")) {
  .off <- pivot1 - pivot1_auto
  cat(sprintf("\n  Offset from the bounding-box centre: (%+.4f, %+.4f, %+.4f) m | %.4f m\n",
              .off[1], .off[2], .off[3], sqrt(sum(.off^2))))
  if (any(abs(.off) > (.rng[2, ] - .rng[1, ]) / 2))
    warning(sprintf(paste0("pivot1 lies OUTSIDE the las_1 bounding box (offset %.3f m). ",
                           "Every rotation will act on a lever arm from a point the ",
                           "cloud does not contain."),
                    sqrt(sum(.off^2))), call. = FALSE)
  rm(.off)
}

.tally(pivot1_mode = pivot1_mode)
rm(.rng, .i)
```


# Stage 1A - Rough Vertical Alignment (epoch 1 only)

Before any temporal work, `las_1` is rotated so its stems stand roughly vertical
with the right way up. An unaligned cloud that is upside-down would undermine the
later use of the lowest stem sections; one lying on its side would undermine the
precision of the fitted stem axes. This block fits a coarse set of ellipses up
every epoch-1 stem, diagnoses orientation from the area-vs-height trend, builds a
forest-average axis, and rotates `las_1` so that axis points along global +Z.

It touches **only `las_1`**. `las_2` is left exactly as loaded. The rotation
matrix, pivot, forest axis and the upside-down verdict are all recorded so the
alignment can be composed into the final export downstream. Everything Stage 1A
fits is discarded once the rotation is known - the main pipeline (Step 1.1
onward) re-fits from scratch on the aligned cloud.

## 1.0 Helpers

```{r}
#| label: step1-helpers
#| code-summary: "Step 1 helper functions"

# ============================================================
# 1.0.1  Raw RANSAC inlier statistics
# ============================================================
summarise_inlier_stats <- function(las, ellipses_all, bot, top, cloud_label) {

  # NULL bot/top mean "adaptive": no lower/upper bound is imposed, matching
  # the per-tree adaptive behaviour in ransac_ellipse_fit_one(). bot/top and
  # Z are both absolute (heights are not re-normalised per tree).
  bot_f <- if (is.null(bot)) -Inf else bot
  top_f <- if (is.null(top))  Inf else top

  tree_ids <- unique(las@data$TreeID[!is.na(las@data$TreeID) & las@data$TreeID != 0])

  pts <- as.data.frame(las@data) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(TreeID) & TreeID != 0) |>
    dplyr::filter(Z >= bot_f & Z <= top_f) |>
    dplyr::group_by(TreeID) |>
    dplyr::summarise(total_pts_in_window = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop")

  stats <- lapply(tree_ids, function(tid) {
    tid_chr <- as.character(tid)
    df_all  <- ellipses_all[[tid_chr]]

    mean_pts_slice <- NA_real_
    mean_inliers   <- NA_real_

    if (!is.null(df_all) && nrow(df_all) > 0) {
      mean_pts_slice <- mean(lengths(df_all$slice_point_ids), na.rm = TRUE)
      fitted <- df_all[!is.na(df_all$center_x), ]
      if (nrow(fitted) > 0)
        mean_inliers <- mean(lengths(fitted$inlier_ids), na.rm = TRUE)
    }

    data.frame(
      TreeID                 = as.integer(tid),
      mean_pts_per_slice     = round(mean_pts_slice, 1),
      mean_inliers_per_slice = round(mean_inliers, 1)
    )
  })

  dplyr::bind_rows(stats) |>
    dplyr::left_join(pts, by = "TreeID") |>
    dplyr::mutate(cloud = cloud_label) |>
    dplyr::select(cloud, TreeID, total_pts_in_window,
                  mean_pts_per_slice, mean_inliers_per_slice)
}

# ============================================================
# 1.0.3  Ellipse cleaning diagnostic plots
# make_cleaning_plot, make_cloud_plots_ellipse, and
# render_gallery_pairs have been moved to the Global Helpers
# block so they can be shared with Step 3.
# ============================================================

# ============================================================
# 1.0.4  Temporal pairing helpers
# ============================================================
avg_centre_from_valid <- function(valid_list, las) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(valid_list), function(tid) {
    df  <- valid_list[[tid]]

    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0)
      return(data.frame(TreeID    = as.integer(tid),
                        cx        = NA_real_,
                        cy        = NA_real_,
                        mean_semi = NA_real_,
                        z_avg     = NA_real_))

    # slice_z is already an absolute Z value (heights are no longer
    # re-normalised per tree), so the representative height is just the mean
    # of the fitted slices' own slice_z – no offset needed.
    data.frame(
      TreeID    = as.integer(tid),
      cx        = mean(df$center_x, na.rm = TRUE),
      cy        = mean(df$center_y, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_semi = mean((df$semi_a + df$semi_b) / 2, na.rm = TRUE),
      z_avg     = mean(df$slice_z, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }))
}

# ============================================================
# 1.0.7  Per-pair mini 3-D inspection helpers
# ============================================================
build_pair_rings <- function(valid_list, tid, las, n = 60L) {
  ell <- valid_list[[as.character(tid)]]
  if (is.null(ell) || nrow(ell) == 0L) return(NULL)
  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(ell)), function(i) {
    .ellipse_ring(
      cx        = ell$center_x[i],
      cy        = ell$center_y[i],
      a         = ell$semi_a[i],
      b         = ell$semi_b[i],
      angle_deg = ell$angle_deg[i],
      z_abs     = ell$slice_z[i],
      n         = n,
      tid       = tid
    )
  }))
}

# ============================================================
# 1.0.8  Temporal pairing summary helpers
# ============================================================
get_avg_diam_valid <- function(tid, valid_list) {
  df <- valid_list[[as.character(tid)]]
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  mean((df$semi_a + df$semi_b), na.rm = TRUE)
}

get_clean_stat <- function(tid, results_list, stat) {
  res <- results_list[[as.character(tid)]]
  if (is.null(res)) return(NA_real_)
  val <- res[[stat]]
  if (is.null(val)) return(NA_real_)
  val
}

mad_flag <- function(x, k = pair_xy_mad_mult) {
  med <- median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  m   <- mad(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  if (is.na(m) || m < 1e-10) return(rep(FALSE, length(x)))
  !is.na(x) & abs(x - med) > k * m
}

# ============================================================
# Shared RANSAC threshold x epoch x slice grid helpers
# ============================================================

#' Single small ggplot panel for one (slice, epoch, threshold) cell.
make_threshold_panel <- function(row_data, las_pts_all,
                                 colour_inlier = "#82B211",
                                 colour_outlier = LOSER,
                                 colour_ellipse = "gold",
                                 pt_size = 0.35, line_width = 0.5) {

  if (is.null(row_data)) return(NULL)

  slice_pids  <- row_data$slice_point_ids[[1]]
  inlier_pids <- row_data$inlier_ids[[1]]

  # Slices thinner than the fitter's five-point minimum never produce an
  # ellipse, so they arrive here as NA rows and are dropped upstream.
  pts_i <- las_pts_all[las_pts_all$point_id %in% slice_pids, ]
  if (nrow(pts_i) == 0) return(NULL)

  pts_i$Status <- ifelse(pts_i$point_id %in% inlier_pids, "Inlier", "Outlier")
  x0 <- min(pts_i$X); y0 <- min(pts_i$Y)
  pts_i$Xn <- pts_i$X - x0
  pts_i$Yn <- pts_i$Y - y0

  theta <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 121)
  ang   <- row_data$angle_deg * pi / 180
  ex    <- row_data$semi_a * cos(theta)
  ey    <- row_data$semi_b * sin(theta)
  ell <- data.frame(
    Xn = ex * cos(ang) - ey * sin(ang) + row_data$center_x - x0,
    Yn = ex * sin(ang) + ey * cos(ang) + row_data$center_y - y0
  )

  ggplot(pts_i, aes(Xn, Yn)) +
    geom_point(aes(color = Status), size = pt_size, alpha = 0.85, show.legend = FALSE) +
    geom_path(data = ell, aes(Xn, Yn), color = colour_ellipse,
              linewidth = line_width, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(Inlier = colour_inlier, Outlier = colour_outlier)) +
    coord_equal() +
    theme_void() +
    theme(plot.margin = margin(1, 1, 1, 1))
}

# make_threshold_grid / render_gallery_grid: the row x (epoch|threshold) panel
# matrix and its HTML gallery are built by the *_flagged variants defined
# locally in the Step 1.2 and Step 1.4 vis chunks, which add removal-status
# borders. The plain versions here were never called and have been removed;
# make_threshold_panel above is the shared cell builder both variants use.

# ============================================================
# 1.0.9  Stage 1A orientation + forest-axis helpers
# Shared by 1A.2 (upside-down evaluation) and 1A.3 (forest axis),
# so the slope, verdict and Theil-Sen axis logic lives in exactly
# one place. Sideways is NOT decided here - see 1.0.10.
# ============================================================

#' Per-stem OLS slope of ellipse area (pi*a*b) on slice height (slice_z).
.align_slope_one <- function(df, min_n = 3L) {
  if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) < min_n) return(NA_real_)
  d <- df[!is.na(df$semi_a) & !is.na(df$semi_b) & !is.na(df$slice_z), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(d) < min_n) return(NA_real_)
  area <- pi * d$semi_a * d$semi_b
  h    <- d$slice_z
  if (stats::var(h) < 1e-12) return(NA_real_)
  unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(area ~ h))[2])
}

#' Slope frame (TreeID, slope, n_kept) for a kept-ellipse list.
.align_slope_frame <- function(kept, min_n = 3L) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(names(kept), function(tid) {
    data.frame(TreeID = tid,
               slope  = .align_slope_one(kept[[tid]], min_n),
               n_kept = if (is.null(kept[[tid]])) 0L else nrow(kept[[tid]]),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}

#' Slope-sign counts for an orientation verdict.
#'
#' Returns the counts of negative / positive area-vs-height slopes and the
#' n_neg / n_pos ratio. It does NOT decide the verdict: 1A.2 derives that from
#' the fraction n_neg / (n_neg + n_pos) against an ASYMMETRIC band, and the
#' band belongs with the chunk that owns the parameters.
#'
#' There is deliberately no "sideways" outcome here any more. Sideways is now
#' decided GEOMETRICALLY in 1A.0, from the per-tree bounding boxes, and a
#' sideways forest is already standing upright by the time this runs - so by
#' 1A.2 the taper sign is readable along Z and the question is only which end
#' is up. `majority_upside_down` is reported for reference only; nothing acts
#' on it.
.align_orientation_verdict <- function(slope_df) {
  s     <- slope_df$slope[is.finite(slope_df$slope)]
  n_pos <- sum(s > 0)
  n_neg <- sum(s < 0)
  ratio <- if (n_pos > 0L) n_neg / n_pos else NA_real_
  list(n_scored = length(s), n_pos = n_pos, n_neg = n_neg,
       ratio = ratio,
       majority_upside_down = n_pos > n_neg)
}

#' Per-stem Theil-Sen axis over all kept centres, averaged into one unit
#' forest vector (BEFORE any upside-down flip). Returns a list with the unit
#' `axis` and the stem counts, or NULL if no stem yielded a vector. Every
#' per-stem vector is built as (b_x, b_y, 1) normalised, so vz > 0 by
#' construction and the averaged axis always points up pre-flip.
.align_forest_axis <- function(kept, min_n = 4L, ts_max_n = 120L,
                               ts_pairs = 20000L, seed = 42L) {
  set.seed(seed)
  ts_one <- function(z, v) {
    n <- length(z)
    if (n <= ts_max_n) {
      ij <- utils::combn(n, 2L); i <- ij[1, ]; j <- ij[2, ]
    } else {
      i <- sample.int(n, ts_pairs, replace = TRUE)
      j <- sample.int(n, ts_pairs, replace = TRUE)
      ok <- i != j; i <- i[ok]; j <- j[ok]
    }
    dz <- z[j] - z[i]
    ok <- abs(dz) > 1e-9
    if (!any(ok)) return(NA_real_)
    median((v[j][ok] - v[i][ok]) / dz[ok])
  }
  stem_axis <- function(df) {
    na <- c(vx = NA_real_, vy = NA_real_, vz = NA_real_)
    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) < min_n) return(na)
    d <- df[!is.na(df$center_x) & !is.na(df$center_y) & !is.na(df$slice_z), , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(d) < min_n) return(na)
    z <- d$slice_z
    if (diff(range(z)) < 1e-6) return(na)
    bx <- ts_one(z, d$center_x)
    by <- ts_one(z, d$center_y)
    if (is.na(bx) || is.na(by)) return(na)
    v <- c(bx, by, 1); v <- v / sqrt(sum(v^2))
    c(vx = v[1], vy = v[2], vz = v[3])
  }
  mat <- do.call(rbind, lapply(kept, stem_axis))
  ok  <- mat[stats::complete.cases(mat), , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(ok) == 0L) return(NULL)
  fmean <- colMeans(ok)
  list(axis = fmean / sqrt(sum(fmean^2)), n_ok = nrow(ok), n_total = length(kept))
}

# ============================================================
# 1.0.10  Stage 1A sideways-forest detection (bounding boxes)
# Purely geometric, so it runs BEFORE any ellipse is fitted:
# a stem lying on its side is longer across than it is tall,
# and a whole forest recorded on its side shares ONE such
# horizontal axis. Both facts are read straight off the
# per-tree bounding boxes.
# ============================================================

#' Per-tree axis-aligned bounding-box extents for one cloud.
#'
#' Returns a data.table with TreeID, bbox_x, bbox_y, bbox_z and bbox_max_dim
#' (the largest of the three). When `R` is supplied the points are rotated
#' about `pivot` first, so the extents are measured in the ROTATED frame
#' without touching the cloud - that is how the 45-degree probe in 1A.0
#' re-tests a forest it may well decide not to rotate at all.
.tree_bbox_frame <- function(las, R = NULL, pivot = NULL) {
  dt <- data.table::as.data.table(las@data)[
    !is.na(TreeID) & TreeID != 0L, .(TreeID, X, Y, Z)]      # subset = a copy
  if (!is.null(R)) {
    if (is.null(pivot))
      stop(".tree_bbox_frame(): pivot is required when R is supplied.")
    # Rotate about pivot componentwise (no big matrix transpose), and rebuild the
    # table rather than := into a subset, which keeps data.table's self-reference
    # unambiguous. Extents are translation-invariant, so the pivot cancels out -
    # it is carried only to keep this the same rotation the cloud would get.
    x <- dt$X - pivot[1]; y <- dt$Y - pivot[2]; z <- dt$Z - pivot[3]
    dt <- data.table::data.table(
      TreeID = dt$TreeID,
      X = pivot[1] + R[1, 1] * x + R[1, 2] * y + R[1, 3] * z,
      Y = pivot[2] + R[2, 1] * x + R[2, 2] * y + R[2, 3] * z,
      Z = pivot[3] + R[3, 1] * x + R[3, 2] * y + R[3, 3] * z)
    rm(x, y, z)
  }
  bb <- dt[, .(bbox_x = diff(range(X)),
               bbox_y = diff(range(Y)),
               bbox_z = diff(range(Z))), by = TreeID]
  bb[, bbox_max_dim := pmax(bbox_x, bbox_y, bbox_z)]
  bb[]
}

#' Sideways verdict for a whole cloud from its per-tree bounding boxes.
#'
#' A tree is WIDE when max(bbox_x, bbox_y) > bbox_z - longer across than tall.
#' The forest is POTENTIALLY sideways when at least `wide_frac_min` of trees
#' are wide, and SIDEWAYS when, on top of that, at least `axis_frac_min` of
#' the WIDE trees are longest along the same horizontal axis (each wide tree
#' votes x when bbox_x >= bbox_y, else y). The second test is what separates a
#' felled forest from a stand of short broad crowns: crowns are wide in no
#' particular direction, a felled forest is wide in one.
.sideways_verdict <- function(bb, wide_frac_min = 0.60, axis_frac_min = 0.80) {
  n         <- nrow(bb)
  wide      <- pmax(bb$bbox_x, bb$bbox_y) > bb$bbox_z
  n_wide    <- sum(wide, na.rm = TRUE)
  frac_wide <- if (n > 0L) n_wide / n else NA_real_
  wide_ok   <- is.finite(frac_wide) && frac_wide >= wide_frac_min

  n_x       <- sum(wide & bb$bbox_x >= bb$bbox_y, na.rm = TRUE)
  n_y       <- n_wide - n_x
  frac_axis <- if (n_wide > 0L) max(n_x, n_y) / n_wide else NA_real_
  axis_ok   <- is.finite(frac_axis) && frac_axis >= axis_frac_min
  prominent <- if (n_wide == 0L) NA_character_ else if (n_x >= n_y) "x" else "y"

  list(n_trees = n, n_wide = n_wide, frac_wide = frac_wide, wide_ok = wide_ok,
       n_x = n_x, n_y = n_y, prominent = prominent,
       frac_axis = frac_axis, axis_ok = axis_ok,
       sideways = wide_ok && axis_ok)
}

#' Rotation about global +Z. Positive `deg` is anticlockwise seen from above,
#' so the 45-degree CLOCKWISE probe is deg = -45.
.yaw_matrix <- function(deg) {
  th <- deg * pi / 180
  matrix(c(cos(th), -sin(th), 0,
           sin(th),  cos(th), 0,
           0,        0,       1), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)
}

#' 90-degree rotation standing the prominent horizontal axis up onto +Z, about
#' the OTHER (non-prominent) horizontal axis. prominent = "x" -> rotate about
#' Y so (1,0,0) -> (0,0,1); prominent = "y" -> rotate about X so (0,1,0) ->
#' (0,0,1). Either sign of the turn would stand the forest up; this one is
#' chosen so the long axis lands on +Z rather than -Z, which simply gives 1A.2
#' the easier of the two questions to answer.
.axis90_matrix <- function(prominent) {
  if (identical(prominent, "x")) {
    matrix(c(0, 0, -1,
             0, 1,  0,
             1, 0,  0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)     # R_y(-90)
  } else {
    matrix(c(1, 0,  0,
             0, 0, -1,
             0, 1,  0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)     # R_x(+90)
  }
}
```


## 1A.0 Sideways Forest Detection

Whether the cloud is lying on its side is settled **before anything is fitted**,
from the per-tree bounding boxes alone. Standing this test ahead of 1A.1 means a
sideways forest is tipped upright first and the coarse ellipse fit then runs
once, on a cloud whose Z axis is already roughly height.

The test has two parts, and both must pass:

1. **Are the trees wider than they are tall?** A tree is *wide* when the longer
   of its X and Y bounding-box extents exceeds its Z extent. At least
   `align_sw_wide_frac` (60%) of trees must be wide for the forest to be
   *potentially* sideways.
2. **Do the wide trees agree on a direction?** Each wide tree votes for the axis
   it is longest along (X when `bbox_x >= bbox_y`, else Y). At least
   `align_sw_axis_frac` (80%) of the wide trees must share that **prominent
   axis**. This is what separates a felled forest from a stand of short, broad
   crowns: crowns are wide in no particular direction, a felled forest is wide in
   one.

**The 45-degree probe.** A forest lying diagonally across the X/Y axes splits its
votes - every stem is long in both X and Y, and which one wins is decided by
noise, so part 2 fails on a forest that really is sideways. When part 1 passes
and part 2 fails, the bounding boxes are re-measured in a frame yawed
`align_sw_probe_deg` (45 degrees clockwise about global +Z, through `pivot1`),
which brings a diagonal forest onto an axis. The whole test is then re-run
**once**, and only once:

- **sideways in the probed frame** - the yaw is kept and composed, and the
  90-degree tip below is applied on top of it.
- **still not sideways** - the forest is not sideways. Nothing is rotated at all;
  the probe was measured out-of-place and the cloud was never touched.

**The correction.** When the verdict is sideways, `las_1` is rotated 90 degrees
about the **non-prominent** horizontal axis, through `pivot1`, standing the
prominent axis up onto +Z (prominent X -> rotate about Y; prominent Y -> rotate
about X). Either direction of turn would stand the forest up; the one used puts
the long axis on +Z rather than -Z, leaving 1A.2 the easier of the two questions.

Three matrices are recorded: `R_sideways_yaw` (the probe, identity unless kept),
`R_sideways_90` (the tip) and their composition `R_sideways_pre <- R_sideways_90
%*% R_sideways_yaw`, which is what actually gets applied here and what 1A.4 folds
into `R_align_1`. All of it turns about `pivot1`, the same point every other
rotation in the pipeline uses, so nothing here can introduce a shift.

```{r}
#| label: params-align-sideways-detect
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Bounding-box sideways test, 45 deg probe, and the 90 deg tip"


# Fraction of ALL trees that must be wider than tall for the forest to be
# potentially sideways.
align_sw_wide_frac <- 0.60

# Fraction of the WIDE trees that must share the same prominent axis for the
# verdict to be sideways.
align_sw_axis_frac <- 0.80

# Probe rotation about +Z, applied only when the wide test passes and the axis
# test fails. Negative = clockwise seen from above.
align_sw_probe_deg <- -45

# ── Master toggle for the whole rough-alignment block ─────────────────────────
# FALSE leaves las_1 exactly as loaded and records an identity alignment, so the
# downstream save list is always complete either way.
#
# This lives here, in 1A.0's params chunk, because 1A.0 is the first step that
# reads it. It previously sat in params-align-ellipse-fit, one step LATER in
# 1A.1 - so on a clean run the `if (run_rough_alignment)` below hit a name that
# did not exist yet. Knitting the document twice in one session hid it: the
# value left in the global environment by the previous knit satisfied the read.
# A fresh session, or the batch driver's per-pair new.env(), does not.
#
# The rule this broke is worth keeping in mind for any future params split: a
# parameter belongs to the params chunk of the FIRST step that reads it, not the
# step it feels thematically closest to.
run_rough_alignment <- TRUE

align_check_n    <- 2000L

.par_apply("params-align-sideways-detect")
```

```{r}
#| label: align-sideways-detect
#| code-summary: "Bounding-box sideways test (+ one 45 deg probe); tip las_1 90 deg upright if sideways"

# Defaults, so 1A.4 can compose unconditionally whatever the verdict.
R_sideways_yaw         <- diag(3)
R_sideways_90          <- diag(3)
R_sideways_pre         <- diag(3)
align_sideways         <- FALSE
align_sideways_rotated <- FALSE
align_sw_probed        <- FALSE
align_sw_verdict       <- NULL
align_bbox_1           <- NULL

# ── Composition witness ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# A sample of las_1 points as it stands RIGHT NOW - before any Stage 1A rotation
# touches it. 1A.4 re-derives these same points from the recorded R_align_1 and
# compares. That is the only way to prove the single recorded matrix really is
# the total of whatever combination was applied (yaw, 90 deg tip, residual, or
# none of them): every other check verifies a matrix against another matrix.
align_check_idx  <- NULL
align_check_xyz0 <- NULL

.sw_report <- function(v, label) {
  cat(sprintf("  %s\n", label))
  cat(sprintf("    wide (max(x,y) > z)      : %d of %d trees = %.1f%% (need >= %.0f%%) -> %s\n",
              v$n_wide, v$n_trees, 100 * v$frac_wide, 100 * align_sw_wide_frac,
              if (v$wide_ok) "PASS" else "fail"))
  if (v$n_wide > 0L)
    cat(sprintf("    prominent axis           : %s (%d x / %d y) = %.1f%% (need >= %.0f%%) -> %s\n",
                toupper(v$prominent), v$n_x, v$n_y, 100 * v$frac_axis,
                100 * align_sw_axis_frac, if (v$axis_ok) "PASS" else "fail"))
  cat(sprintf("    verdict                  : %s\n",
              if (v$sideways) "SIDEWAYS" else "not sideways"))
}

if (run_rough_alignment) {

  .n_pts <- nrow(las_1@data)
  # Evenly spaced, NOT sampled: drawing from the RNG here would shift the stream
  # every later seeded step reads from.
  align_check_idx  <- if (.n_pts <= align_check_n) seq_len(.n_pts) else
                        unique(round(seq(1, .n_pts, length.out = align_check_n)))
  align_check_xyz0 <- as.matrix(las_1@data[align_check_idx, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  rm(.n_pts)

  # -- Pass 1: bounding boxes in the cloud's own frame -------------------------
  align_bbox_1 <- .tree_bbox_frame(las_1)
  .sw1 <- .sideways_verdict(align_bbox_1, align_sw_wide_frac, align_sw_axis_frac)

  cat("-- Sideways detection (per-tree bounding boxes) --------------------------\n")
  .sw_report(.sw1, "pass 1 (as loaded)")

  align_sw_verdict <- .sw1

  # -- The one probe: wide trees, but no agreed axis -> yaw 45 deg and re-test --
  # Measured OUT OF PLACE: the cloud is only rotated below, and only if the
  # probed frame actually returns a sideways verdict. Run once, never twice.
  if (.sw1$wide_ok && !.sw1$axis_ok) {
    .R_probe <- .yaw_matrix(align_sw_probe_deg)
    align_bbox_1_probe <- .tree_bbox_frame(las_1, R = .R_probe, pivot = pivot1)
    .sw2 <- .sideways_verdict(align_bbox_1_probe, align_sw_wide_frac, align_sw_axis_frac)
    align_sw_probed <- TRUE

    cat(sprintf("  %.0f deg %s probe about pivot1 applied (axis test failed above)\n",
                abs(align_sw_probe_deg),
                if (align_sw_probe_deg < 0) "clockwise" else "anticlockwise"))
    .sw_report(.sw2, "pass 2 (probed frame)")

    if (isTRUE(.sw2$sideways)) {
      R_sideways_yaw   <- .R_probe          # kept: the tip is measured in this frame
      align_sw_verdict <- .sw2
      align_bbox_1     <- align_bbox_1_probe
    } else {
      cat("    probe discarded - cloud not rotated.\n")
    }
    rm(.R_probe)
  }

  align_sideways <- isTRUE(align_sw_verdict$sideways)

  # -- Correction: stand the prominent axis up onto +Z -------------------------
  if (align_sideways) {
    R_sideways_90  <- .axis90_matrix(align_sw_verdict$prominent)
    R_sideways_pre <- R_sideways_90 %*% R_sideways_yaw     # yaw first, then tip

    .M  <- as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
    .Mc <- sweep(.M, 2, pivot1, "-")
    .Mr <- sweep(.Mc %*% t(R_sideways_pre), 2, pivot1, "+")
    las_1@data$X <- .Mr[, 1]
    las_1@data$Y <- .Mr[, 2]
    las_1@data$Z <- .Mr[, 3]
    las_1 <- lidR::las_update(las_1)        # refresh header bbox
    xyz_1 <- as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
    align_sideways_rotated <- TRUE

    cat(sprintf("  correction: 90 deg about %s (the non-prominent axis), through pivot1\n",
                if (identical(align_sw_verdict$prominent, "x")) "Y" else "X"))
    cat(sprintf("    R_sideways_yaw det       : %.6f%s\n", det(R_sideways_yaw),
                if (align_sw_probed)
                  sprintf("  (%.0f deg probe composed in)", abs(align_sw_probe_deg)) else "  (identity)"))
    cat(sprintf("    R_sideways_pre det       : %.6f (should be 1; applied to las_1 now)\n",
                det(R_sideways_pre)))
    cat("    las_1 tipped upright; the coarse fit in 1A.1 runs on the tipped cloud.\n")
    cat("    R_sideways_pre is composed into R_align_1 at 1A.4.\n")
    rm(.M, .Mc, .Mr)
  } else {
    cat("  no correction applied - las_1 left exactly as loaded.\n")
  }

} else {
  cat("Sideways detection SKIPPED (run_rough_alignment = FALSE).\n")
}
```


## 1A.1 Alignment Ellipse Fitting

A coarse pass over every epoch-1 stem: 5 cm slices every 40 cm, up each stem's
full range, then the same consensus + MAD clean, masked refit and second clean
the main pipeline uses. This is deliberately cheaper and taller than the Step
1.1 fit - it only has to reveal the area-vs-height trend and a stem axis, not
support the final measurement.

```{r}
#| label: params-align-ellipse-fit
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Fit + clean + refit + reclean a coarse ellipse set up every epoch-1 stem"

# The master toggle for this whole block, run_rough_alignment, used to live here
# in 1A.1 - one step AFTER the 1A.0 chunk that reads it. It is now set in
# params-align-sideways-detect, the params chunk of the first step that uses it.

# ── Slice band (epoch 1, full range) ──────────────────────────────────────────
align_slice_width  <- 0.10     # 10 cm slices
align_slice_step   <- 0.20     # 20 cm between slice centres
align_slice_bot    <- 0.0      # from each stem's base

align_slice_top    <- NULL     # NULL = each stem's own top (entire range)
align_height_min   <- 2.0     # NULL = fit every stem, however short

# ── Tree subset (largest stems only) ───────────────────────────────────────────
# Stage 1A only needs enough stems to establish a reliable forest axis, so the
# fit is restricted to the align_n_largest_trees epoch-1 stems with the
# greatest bounding-box extent. "Size" is the single largest of a stem's own
# X, Y and Z point-cloud ranges - i.e. max(diff(range(X)), diff(range(Y)),
# diff(range(Z))) - so a tall narrow stem and a short wide crown are both
# ranked on whichever dimension actually makes them large. NULL = use every
# epoch-1 stem (previous behaviour).
align_n_largest_trees <- 20L

# ── RANSAC budget ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 10 mm, DELIBERATELY WIDER than Step 1.1's default. This fit runs at a coarse
# slice step on the twenty largest stems and only has to be good enough to find
# the forest axis; a tight inlier band on a sparse epoch returns too few usable
# slices to fit an axis through at all. Set here and NOT governed by the density
# probe below, which decides Step 1.1 onward.
align_distance_threshold <- 0.010
align_iter_per_point     <- 1.0
align_iter_max           <- 750L
align_iter_min           <- 1L
align_fit_seed           <- 33L

.par_apply("params-align-ellipse-fit")
```

```{r}
#| label: align-ellipse-fit
#| code-summary: "Fit + clean + refit + reclean a coarse ellipse set up every epoch-1 stem"


# ── Cleaning parameters (mirror Step 1.2 defaults) ────────────────────────────
# LEAN PREDICTION: Steps 1.2/1.3 expose their own use_local_lean / lean_k /
# pred_pad_mult / r_floor_frac and are tuned independently of this block.
# Nothing set there reaches Stage 1A. Omitting them here leaves Stage 1A on the
# helper defaults (lean ON, k = 4, pad 2.0, floor 0.75), which is deliberate:
# this fit runs at a coarser slice step, so its per-slice lean offset is larger
# and there is no reason for it to share the main pipeline's tuning.
align_clean_args <- list(
  frac_c    = 0.40, frac_maj = 0.40, frac_min = 0.40,
  max_gap   = NULL, sort_axes = TRUE, tol_floor = NULL, tol_cap = NULL,
  do_mad = TRUE,  mad_mult     = 3.0, mad_min_n     = 5L,
  do_mad_maj = TRUE, mad_maj_mult = 3.0, mad_maj_min_n = 5L
)

# ── Refit parameters (mirror Step 1.3 defaults) ───────────────────────────────
align_refit_args <- list(
  mask_scale = 1.75, min_pts = 5L, seed = 42L,
  distance_threshold = NULL, n_iterations = NULL, early_exit = FALSE,
  targets = "consensus",
  iter_per_point = align_iter_per_point,
  iter_max = align_iter_max, iter_min = align_iter_min
)

# ── Reclean parameters: identical to pass 1 (mirror Step 1.4 defaults) ─────────
align_reclean_args <- align_clean_args

if (run_rough_alignment) {

  # ── Select the N largest trees by bounding-box extent ────────────────────────
  # Per-tree size = the greatest of that stem's own X, Y and Z point ranges.
  # Using the largest dimension (rather than, say, height alone) means a stem
  # that is large in any direction - including one still lying on its side,
  # which is exactly the case this block has to diagnose - is not discounted
  # for having a short Z extent before the orientation is even known.
  # Same bounding boxes 1A.0 tested for sideways-ness, re-measured here because
  # las_1 may have been tipped since. .tree_bbox_frame() is the one definition.
  .align_dt <- .tree_bbox_frame(las_1)
  data.table::setorder(.align_dt, -bbox_max_dim)

  if (is.null(align_n_largest_trees)) {
    align_tree_ids <- .align_dt$TreeID
  } else {
    align_tree_ids <- head(.align_dt$TreeID, align_n_largest_trees)
  }

  align_las_1 <- lidR::filter_poi(las_1, TreeID %in% align_tree_ids)

  cat(sprintf(
    "Stage 1A tree subset: %d of %d epoch-1 stem(s) selected by largest bounding-box dimension%s\n",
    length(align_tree_ids), nrow(.align_dt),
    if (is.null(align_n_largest_trees)) "" else sprintf(" (top %d)", align_n_largest_trees)
  ))
  print(head(.align_dt[, .(TreeID, bbox_x, bbox_y, bbox_z, bbox_max_dim)],
             length(align_tree_ids)))

  align_res_1 <- .fit_clean_refit_reclean(
    las = align_las_1, label = "las_1 (align)", seed = align_fit_seed,
    slice_bot = align_slice_bot, slice_top = align_slice_top,
    slice_step = align_slice_step, slice_width = align_slice_width,
    height_min = align_height_min,
    distance_threshold = align_distance_threshold,
    iter_per_point = align_iter_per_point,
    iter_max = align_iter_max, iter_min = align_iter_min,
    clean_args = align_clean_args, refit_args = align_refit_args,
    reclean_args = align_reclean_args,
    track_history = FALSE
  )

  align_kept_1 <- align_res_1$valid2

  .n_stem <- length(Filter(function(d) !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0, align_kept_1))
  .n_ell  <- sum(vapply(align_kept_1, function(d)
                        if (is.null(d)) 0L else nrow(d), integer(1)))
  cat(sprintf("\nAlignment fit complete: %d stem(s) with kept ellipses, %d ellipse(s) total.\n",
              .n_stem, .n_ell))

} else {
  cat("Rough vertical alignment SKIPPED (run_rough_alignment = FALSE).\n")
  align_res_1  <- NULL
  align_kept_1 <- NULL
}
```

## 1A.1b Point-Cloud Density Probe

The same coarse 20-stem fit, read a second time as a *density measurement*. For
each epoch it reports four numbers - points per slice, points per KEPT slice,
inliers per slice, inliers per KEPT slice - so the slice thickness used by the
main Step 1.1 fit can be chosen from what the clouds actually contain rather
than fixed by hand.

Why those four and not one: `points per slice` is the raw sampling of the cloud
and is available for every attempted slice, fitted or not. `inliers per slice`
is how much of that sampling RANSAC could actually place on an ellipse.
The two `per kept slice` variants restrict the same quantities to the slices
that survived both cleaning passes, which is the population the pipeline is
really made of - a cloud can average plenty of points per slice and still keep
almost nothing, and that gap is exactly what a thickness change is meant to
close.

Epoch 1 reuses the 1A.1 fit (same stems, same geometry, no refit). Epoch 2 has
no alignment fit of its own, so the probe runs one here on `las_2`'s largest
stems - it exists only to be measured and is not used by any later step.

Reported at the probe's own slice thickness, and again scaled linearly to 5 cm
and 10 cm, since points per slice is very nearly proportional to slice width and
a threshold is only meaningful once the thickness is pinned down.

```{r}
#| label: params-align-density-probe
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Point-cloud density probe + automatic slice-width choice"

# ── Master toggle ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Independent of run_rough_alignment: the slice-width decision is needed whether
# or not the rough vertical alignment runs. With the alignment off, the probe
# fits its own las_1 subset instead of reusing 1A.1's.
run_density_probe <- TRUE

# ── Probe subset + geometry (NULL = inherit the 1A.1 alignment fit) ───────────
# Inheriting is the default so epoch 1 costs nothing: the probe reads the fit
# 1A.1 already produced. Set any of these and epoch 1 is refitted at the new
# geometry too, so that the two epochs stay comparable.
density_probe_n_trees     <- NULL   # NULL = align_n_largest_trees
density_probe_slice_width <- NULL   # NULL = align_slice_width
density_probe_slice_step  <- NULL   # NULL = align_slice_step

# ── Scarcity ramp ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The probe turns the two epochs into ONE number, density_scarcity (t), running
# from 0 (dense - change nothing) to 1 (as scarce as the ramp goes - every
# parameter at its cap). Everything downstream interpolates its own base value
# toward the caps below by t, so there is one dial and no per-parameter rules.
#
# ANCHORED ON MEASURED RUNS, not on theory:
#   TLS/TLS, ~2600 pts per kept slice  -> 43-49% of slices kept at the base
#                                         settings. Nothing needs widening.
#   TLS epoch of a TLS/ULS pair, ~1630 -> works at the base settings.
#   ULS epoch, 472                     -> 0.6% kept at 10 cm / 10 mm / 0.30.
#   ULS epoch, 162                     -> 0.9% kept at 5 cm / 5 mm / 0.30.
# So 1000 is comfortably inside the region that works and 150 is past the worst
# observed epoch: t = 0 at or above the first, t = 1 at or below the second.
#
# Linear rather than logarithmic between them, deliberately: the two failing
# epochs sit at 162 and 472, and a log ramp would put the 472 case at only
# t = 0.40 when the evidence is that it needs most of the available room.
density_pts_ref_dense  <- 1000   # >= this: t = 0
density_pts_ref_scarce <- 150    # <= this: t = 1

# Judged on points per KEPT slice rather than per slice: an epoch can average
# plenty of points across all slices and still keep almost nothing, and it is
# the population that survives cleaning the rest of the pipeline is built from.
# Measured at the probe's OWN slice thickness, so both references only mean
# what they say alongside density_probe_slice_width.
#
# BOTH epochs take the SCARCER epoch's t. They must be fitted identically or
# their ellipses are not comparable across time, so the thinner one decides.

# ── Base values (t = 0) ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# The TLS settings, which the logs show working as they are.
density_base_slice_width        <- 0.05
density_base_distance_threshold <- 0.005

# ── Caps (t = 1) ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Slice width and the three consensus fractions are capped where you set them.
#
# The distance threshold cap is 15 mm, three times the TLS value. It is NOT
# ramped further on purpose: the threshold is the half-width of the inlier band
# around the candidate ellipse, so it only helps while it stays small against
# the stem radius. These stems have semi-minor axes of roughly 5-15 cm, so
# +/-15 mm is already 10-30% of the radius; past that the fit stops being
# constrained by the stem surface and starts accepting anything in the slice,
# which shows up downstream as the inflated semi-axes already visible in the
# scarce epochs (median centre tolerances of 6-16 cm imply semi-minor axes far
# larger than any real stem here). Widening the band cannot recover a slice
# that does not contain a resolvable stem cross-section.
density_max_slice_width        <- 0.20
density_max_distance_threshold <- 0.015
density_max_frac_centre        <- 1.00
density_max_frac_minor         <- 0.60
density_max_frac_major         <- 0.60

# FALSE = measure and report, change nothing downstream.
density_apply_regime <- TRUE

.par_apply("params-align-density-probe")
```

```{r}
#| label: align-density-probe
#| code-summary: "Measure per-slice point and inlier density on both epochs; recommend a slice width"

# ── Resolve the probe geometry ────────────────────────────────────────────────
.dp_n     <- if (is.null(density_probe_n_trees))     align_n_largest_trees else density_probe_n_trees
.dp_width <- if (is.null(density_probe_slice_width)) align_slice_width     else density_probe_slice_width
.dp_step  <- if (is.null(density_probe_slice_step))  align_slice_step      else density_probe_slice_step

# Epoch 1 can be reused only if 1A.1 actually ran AND at this same geometry.
.dp_inherit_1 <- run_rough_alignment && exists("align_res_1") && !is.null(align_res_1) &&
                 isTRUE(all.equal(.dp_n,     align_n_largest_trees)) &&
                 isTRUE(all.equal(.dp_width, align_slice_width))     &&
                 isTRUE(all.equal(.dp_step,  align_slice_step))

# ── Per-slice counts for one epoch ────────────────────────────────────────────
# All four numbers come off ONE fit result, so "kept" is genuinely a subset of
# "all" and the two columns are directly comparable.
#
# POINTS: always taken from the pass-1 raw frame, for kept and unkept slices
# alike. A refit row's slice_point_ids holds the MASKED candidate set, not the
# slice's full population, so reading it for kept slices would report the mask
# radius rather than the cloud density. Kept slices are matched back to their
# raw row on slice_z.
#
# INLIERS: taken from the operative row - the raw fit for the all-slices
# columns, the kept row itself for the kept columns. A refit slice was fitted
# twice and it is the second fit that survived, so its own inlier count is the
# one that describes the ellipse the pipeline kept.
.density_counts <- function(res, step) {

  raw  <- res$raw
  kept <- res$valid2
  eps  <- max(step / 4, 1e-6)

  parts <- lapply(names(raw), function(tid) {
    r <- raw[[tid]]
    if (is.null(r) || nrow(r) == 0L) return(NULL)

    n_pts <- if ("slice_point_ids" %in% names(r))
               as.numeric(lengths(r$slice_point_ids)) else rep(NA_real_, nrow(r))

    fitted <- !is.na(r$center_x)
    n_inl  <- rep(NA_real_, nrow(r))
    if ("inlier_ids" %in% names(r))
      n_inl[fitted] <- as.numeric(lengths(r$inlier_ids[fitted]))

    k <- if (is.null(kept)) NULL else kept[[tid]]
    n_pts_k <- numeric(0); n_inl_k <- numeric(0)

    if (!is.null(k) && nrow(k) > 0L) {
      # One raw row per kept slice, matched on slice_z (same grid, same tree).
      hit <- vapply(k$slice_z, function(z) {
        h <- which(abs(r$slice_z - z) <= eps)
        if (length(h) == 1L) h else NA_integer_
      }, integer(1))

      n_pts_k <- n_pts[hit]
      n_inl_k <- if ("inlier_ids" %in% names(k))
                   as.numeric(lengths(k$inlier_ids))
                 else n_inl[hit]
    }

    list(TreeID = as.integer(tid),
         pts = n_pts, inl = n_inl, fitted = fitted,
         pts_k = n_pts_k, inl_k = n_inl_k)
  })

  Filter(Negate(is.null), parts)
}

# Pooled over every slice in the epoch, not a mean of per-tree means: a stem
# with 200 slices should weigh more than one with 20, because the question is
# what a typical SLICE holds.
.density_row <- function(parts, cloud, width) {
  pool <- function(f) unlist(lapply(parts, f), use.names = FALSE)

  pts   <- pool(function(p) p$pts)
  inl   <- pool(function(p) p$inl)
  pts_k <- pool(function(p) p$pts_k)
  inl_k <- pool(function(p) p$inl_k)

  m  <- function(x) if (length(x) && any(is.finite(x))) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)   else NA_real_
  md <- function(x) if (length(x) && any(is.finite(x))) stats::median(x, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_

  data.frame(
    cloud       = cloud,
    width_cm    = width * 100,
    n_trees     = length(parts),
    n_slices    = length(pts),
    n_fitted    = sum(pool(function(p) p$fitted), na.rm = TRUE),
    n_kept      = length(pts_k),
    pts_per_slice          = m(pts),   pts_per_slice_med          = md(pts),
    pts_per_kept_slice     = m(pts_k), pts_per_kept_slice_med     = md(pts_k),
    inliers_per_slice      = m(inl),   inliers_per_slice_med      = md(inl),
    inliers_per_kept_slice = m(inl_k), inliers_per_kept_slice_med = md(inl_k),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

.density_tree_rows <- function(parts, cloud) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(parts, function(p) data.frame(
    cloud                  = cloud,
    TreeID                 = p$TreeID,
    n_slices               = length(p$pts),
    n_fitted               = sum(p$fitted, na.rm = TRUE),
    n_kept                 = length(p$pts_k),
    pts_per_slice          = if (length(p$pts))   mean(p$pts,   na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    pts_per_kept_slice     = if (length(p$pts_k)) mean(p$pts_k, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    inliers_per_slice      = if (any(p$fitted))   mean(p$inl,   na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    inliers_per_kept_slice = if (length(p$inl_k)) mean(p$inl_k, na.rm = TRUE) else NA_real_,
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )))
}

# Largest-N subset, by the same bounding-box rule 1A.1 uses.
.density_subset <- function(las, n) {
  dt <- .tree_bbox_frame(las)
  data.table::setorder(dt, -bbox_max_dim)
  ids <- if (is.null(n)) dt$TreeID else head(dt$TreeID, n)
  lidR::filter_poi(las, TreeID %in% ids)
}

if (run_density_probe) {

  cat("\n== Stage 1A.1b - point-cloud density probe ==\n")
  cat(sprintf("Probe geometry: %.0f cm slices every %.0f cm | %s stem(s) per epoch\n",
              .dp_width * 100, .dp_step * 100,
              if (is.null(.dp_n)) "all" else format(.dp_n)))

  # ── Epoch 1 ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (.dp_inherit_1) {
    cat("las_1: reusing the 1A.1 alignment fit (same stems, same geometry).\n")
    density_res_1 <- align_res_1
  } else {
    cat("las_1: fitting a probe set here",
        if (!run_rough_alignment) "(rough alignment is off)" else "(probe geometry differs from 1A.1)", "...\n")
    density_res_1 <- .fit_clean_refit_reclean(
      las = .density_subset(las_1, .dp_n), label = "las_1 (density)",
      seed = align_fit_seed,
      slice_bot = align_slice_bot, slice_top = align_slice_top,
      slice_step = .dp_step, slice_width = .dp_width,
      height_min = align_height_min,
      distance_threshold = align_distance_threshold,
      iter_per_point = align_iter_per_point,
      iter_max = align_iter_max, iter_min = align_iter_min,
      clean_args = align_clean_args, refit_args = align_refit_args,
      reclean_args = align_reclean_args, track_history = FALSE
    )
  }

  # ── Epoch 2 - never inherited, there is no las_2 alignment fit ─────────────
  density_res_2 <- .fit_clean_refit_reclean(
    las = .density_subset(las_2, .dp_n), label = "las_2 (density)",
    seed = align_fit_seed,
    slice_bot = align_slice_bot, slice_top = align_slice_top,
    slice_step = .dp_step, slice_width = .dp_width,
    height_min = align_height_min,
    distance_threshold = align_distance_threshold,
    iter_per_point = align_iter_per_point,
    iter_max = align_iter_max, iter_min = align_iter_min,
    clean_args = align_clean_args, refit_args = align_refit_args,
    reclean_args = align_reclean_args, track_history = FALSE
  )

  .dp_parts_1 <- .density_counts(density_res_1, .dp_step)
  .dp_parts_2 <- .density_counts(density_res_2, .dp_step)

  density_stats <- rbind(.density_row(.dp_parts_1, "las_1", .dp_width),
                         .density_row(.dp_parts_2, "las_2", .dp_width))

  density_stats_by_tree <- rbind(.density_tree_rows(.dp_parts_1, "las_1"),
                                 .density_tree_rows(.dp_parts_2, "las_2"))

  density_probe_width <- .dp_width
  density_probe_step  <- .dp_step

  # ── Report ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  .dp_show <- function(suffix, title) {
    cat(sprintf("\n%s (per slice, %.0f cm slices):\n", title, .dp_width * 100))
    d <- data.frame(
      cloud    = density_stats$cloud,
      slices   = density_stats$n_slices,
      fitted   = density_stats$n_fitted,
      kept     = density_stats$n_kept,
      pts      = round(density_stats[[paste0("pts_per_slice", suffix)]], 1),
      pts_kept = round(density_stats[[paste0("pts_per_kept_slice", suffix)]], 1),
      inl      = round(density_stats[[paste0("inliers_per_slice", suffix)]], 1),
      inl_kept = round(density_stats[[paste0("inliers_per_kept_slice", suffix)]], 1),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
    print(d, row.names = FALSE)
  }
  .dp_show("",     "MEAN")
  .dp_show("_med", "MEDIAN")
  cat("  pts / pts_kept = points in the slice | inl / inl_kept = RANSAC inliers\n")
  cat("  *_kept restricted to slices surviving both cleaning passes.\n")

  # ── Scarcity ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # One number per epoch, then the scarcer of the two.
  .dp_kept <- setNames(density_stats$pts_per_kept_slice, density_stats$cloud)
  .dp_t <- vapply(.dp_kept, function(v) {
    if (!is.finite(v)) return(1)          # nothing measurable = treat as scarce
    max(0, min(1, (density_pts_ref_dense - v) /
                  (density_pts_ref_dense - density_pts_ref_scarce)))
  }, numeric(1))

  density_scarcity <- max(.dp_t)
  density_regime   <- if (density_scarcity > 0) "scarce" else "dense"

  cat(sprintf("\nScarcity ramp: t = 0 at >= %s pts per kept slice, t = 1 at <= %s\n",
              format(density_pts_ref_dense, big.mark = ","),
              format(density_pts_ref_scarce, big.mark = ",")))
  for (.cl in names(.dp_kept))
    cat(sprintf("  %-6s %9.1f  t = %.2f%s\n", .cl, .dp_kept[[.cl]], .dp_t[[.cl]],
                if (isTRUE(.dp_t[[.cl]] == density_scarcity) && density_scarcity > 0)
                  "  <- decides for both epochs" else ""))
  cat(sprintf("  -> %s (t = %.2f)\n", toupper(density_regime), density_scarcity))

  # ── What t buys ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  .dscale <- function(base, cap) base + density_scarcity * (cap - base)

  density_slice_width_reco        <- .dscale(density_base_slice_width,
                                             density_max_slice_width)
  density_distance_threshold_reco <- .dscale(density_base_distance_threshold,
                                             density_max_distance_threshold)

  if (isTRUE(density_apply_regime)) {
    cat("\n  parameter             base   ->  applied      cap\n")
    cat(sprintf("  slice width         %5.2f m  -> %5.2f m   %5.2f m\n",
                density_base_slice_width, density_slice_width_reco,
                density_max_slice_width))
    cat(sprintf("  distance threshold  %5.1f mm -> %5.1f mm  %5.1f mm\n",
                density_base_distance_threshold * 1000,
                density_distance_threshold_reco * 1000,
                density_max_distance_threshold * 1000))
    cat("  consensus fractions are scaled by the same t inside Steps 1.2 and 3.5,\n")
    cat("  each from its OWN base (Stage 1 uses 0.30, Stage 3 uses 0.20).\n")
  } else {
    cat("  density_apply_regime = FALSE - reported only; every stage keeps its own settings.\n")
    density_slice_width_reco <- NULL
    density_distance_threshold_reco <- NULL
  }

  # ── Centre scatter, reported ────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Not part of the decision - a second opinion on it. The probe already cleaned
  # both epochs, so the median local |dc/dz| its consensus filter had to correct
  # for is free to read here. Across the sample logs this tracked the kept share
  # more closely than density did (~0.15 where cleaning kept 34-43% of slices,
  # 0.5-1.1 where it kept nothing), so if a run comes back scarce on density but
  # low on scatter - or the reverse - the ramp is being asked the wrong question.
  .dp_scatter <- function(res) {
    if (is.null(res$clean_result)) return(NA_real_)
    v <- vapply(res$clean_result, function(r)
           if (is.null(r$med_lean_mag)) NA_real_ else r$med_lean_mag, numeric(1))
    if (all(is.na(v))) NA_real_ else stats::median(v, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  density_centre_scatter <- c(las_1 = .dp_scatter(density_res_1),
                              las_2 = .dp_scatter(density_res_2))
  cat(sprintf("\n  Centre scatter (median local |dc/dz|, reported): las_1 %.3f | las_2 %.3f\n",
              density_centre_scatter[["las_1"]], density_centre_scatter[["las_2"]]))

  .tally(density_probe_width_cm      = .dp_width * 100,
         density_pts_per_slice_1     = density_stats$pts_per_slice[1],
         density_pts_per_slice_2     = density_stats$pts_per_slice[2],
         density_pts_per_kept_1      = density_stats$pts_per_kept_slice[1],
         density_pts_per_kept_2      = density_stats$pts_per_kept_slice[2],
         density_inliers_per_slice_1 = density_stats$inliers_per_slice[1],
         density_inliers_per_slice_2 = density_stats$inliers_per_slice[2],
         density_inliers_per_kept_1  = density_stats$inliers_per_kept_slice[1],
         density_inliers_per_kept_2  = density_stats$inliers_per_kept_slice[2],
         density_regime              = density_regime,
         density_scarcity            = density_scarcity,
         density_scatter_1           = unname(density_centre_scatter[["las_1"]]),
         density_scatter_2           = unname(density_centre_scatter[["las_2"]]),
         density_slice_width_cm      = if (is.null(density_slice_width_reco))
                                         NA_real_ else density_slice_width_reco * 100,
         density_dist_thresh_mm      = if (is.null(density_distance_threshold_reco))
                                         NA_real_ else density_distance_threshold_reco * 1000)

  rm(list = intersect(
    c(".dp_parts_1", ".dp_parts_2", ".dp_show", ".dp_kept", ".dp_t", ".cl",
      ".dscale", ".dp_scatter"),
    ls(all.names = TRUE)))

} else {
  cat("Density probe SKIPPED (run_density_probe = FALSE).\n")
  density_res_1 <- NULL; density_res_2 <- NULL
  density_stats <- NULL; density_stats_by_tree <- NULL
  density_probe_width <- NULL; density_probe_step <- NULL
  density_regime <- NA_character_; density_scarcity <- 0
  density_centre_scatter <- c(las_1 = NA_real_, las_2 = NA_real_)
  density_slice_width_reco <- NULL; density_distance_threshold_reco <- NULL
}
```


### Vis - Stage 1A slice status

Same per-slice status view as *Vis - slice x thresh inliers Reclean* in the
main Step 1.4 pipeline, but for the single Stage 1A alignment fit: there is
only one cloud (`align_las_1`, the 20 largest trees) and one RANSAC threshold,
so the epoch/threshold column grid collapses to one column per tree. A stem
that lost every slice before pass 2 (printed above as *"enters pass 2 with no
surviving slices"*) still gets its own panel here - every one of its rows is
shown, coloured by whichever stage removed it (`mad1` or `unrefit`), rather
than being silently dropped from the gallery.

```{r}
#| label: align-vis-slice-status
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Per-slice panels for the Stage 1A alignment fit; grey background = refit, red/orange/black borders = removal stage"

if (!second_run && params$make_plots && run_rough_alignment &&
    exists("align_res_1") && !is.null(align_res_1)) {

  if (is.null(align_res_1$refit_flagged) || length(align_res_1$refit_flagged) == 0L)
    stop("align_res_1$refit_flagged not found - run the align-ellipse-fit chunk first.")

  # ── User input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  align_vis_treeids     <- NULL     # NULL = every Stage 1A alignment tree
  align_vis_n_rows      <- NULL     # NULL = every slice; k = first k from the lowest
  align_slice_match_eps <- 1e-6

  # ── Appearance (identical palette/meaning to the Step 1.4 diagnostic) ───────
  align_bg_refit       <- "#ECCCCC"   # light grey - slice was refit
  align_bg_plain       <- "white"
  align_col_consensus2 <- "#D7263D"   # red    - removed by 2nd-pass consensus
  align_col_mad2       <- "#F07C10"   # orange - removed by 2nd-pass MAD
  align_col_mad1       <- "purple"    # 1st-pass MAD removal (thicker border)
  align_col_unrefit    <- "blue"      # 1st-pass consensus removal, refit failed
  align_px             <- 6
  align_px_mad1        <- 10

  align_label_offset <- (if (is.null(align_slice_bot)) 0 else align_slice_bot) +
                        align_slice_width / 2

  # ── Per-slice status, read from the stored Stage 1A results (not recomputed)─
  # Priority, identical to the main pipeline's post-refit diagnostic:
  #   mad1       - dropped by the first MAD stage (never a refit target)
  #   unrefit    - dropped by first-pass consensus, refit did not succeed
  #   consensus2 - entered pass 2, dropped by consensus
  #   mad2       - entered pass 2, dropped by MAD
  #   kept       - survived everything
  # A stem with zero pass-2 candidates (clean2$flagged has 0 rows, or the tree
  # is absent from clean2 altogether) falls straight to the mad1/unrefit branch
  # for every one of its rows, so it still renders a full column of panels.
  .align_status_frame <- function(refit_flagged, clean2_result, tid) {
    base <- refit_flagged[[as.character(tid)]]
    if (is.null(base) || nrow(base) == 0L) return(NULL)
    base <- as.data.frame(base)

    c2 <- if (!is.null(clean2_result)) clean2_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged else NULL
    c2 <- if (is.null(c2) || nrow(c2) == 0L) NULL else as.data.frame(c2)

    n      <- nrow(base)
    status <- rep(NA_character_, n)

    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      if (isTRUE(base$unfitted[i])) next          # never fitted -> blank cell

      if (isTRUE(base$mad_minor_out[i]) ||
          isTRUE(base$mad_major_out[i])) { status[i] <- "mad1"; next }

      hit <- if (is.null(c2)) integer(0) else
               which(abs(c2$slice_z - base$slice_z[i]) <= align_slice_match_eps)

      if (length(hit) != 1L) { status[i] <- "unrefit"; next }

      status[i] <-
        if (isTRUE(c2$no_consensus[hit]))  "consensus2" else
        if (isTRUE(c2$mad_minor_out[hit]) ||
            isTRUE(c2$mad_major_out[hit]))  "mad2"       else "kept"
    }

    data.frame(
      slice_z = base$slice_z,
      dz      = base$slice_z - min(base$slice_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      status  = status,
      refit   = if ("refit" %in% names(base)) base$refit else rep(FALSE, n),
      row_idx = seq_len(n),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Geometry for a panel: prefer the pass-2 frame when the slice reached it
  # (that is the frame the second cleaning judged), else fall back to
  # refit_flagged - the only case that matters is mad1 and unrefit slices,
  # which pass 2 never saw.
  .align_row <- function(refit_flagged, clean2_result, tid, row_idx, slice_z) {
    c2 <- if (!is.null(clean2_result)) clean2_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged else NULL
    if (!is.null(c2) && nrow(c2) > 0L) {
      c2  <- as.data.frame(c2)
      hit <- which(abs(c2$slice_z - slice_z) <= align_slice_match_eps)
      if (length(hit) == 1L) return(c2[hit, , drop = FALSE])
    }
    base <- as.data.frame(refit_flagged[[as.character(tid)]])
    base[row_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  align_pts_cache <- as.data.frame(align_las_1@data[, c("point_id", "X", "Y")])

  wanted <- if (is.null(align_vis_treeids)) align_tree_ids else
              as.character(align_vis_treeids)
  wanted <- as.character(wanted)
  wanted <- wanted[wanted %in% names(align_res_1$refit_flagged)]
  if (length(wanted) == 0L) stop("No renderable Stage 1A trees.")

  cat(sprintf("Rendering %d Stage 1A alignment tree(s) (of %d selected).\n",
              length(wanted), length(align_tree_ids)))

  # ── One grid per tree, single column - Stage 1A has only one cloud ──────────
  make_align_grid <- function(tid) {

    st <- .align_status_frame(align_res_1$refit_flagged, align_res_1$clean2, tid)
    if (is.null(st)) return(NULL)

    keep_dz <- st$dz[!is.na(st$status)]
    if (length(keep_dz) == 0L) return(NULL)
    dz_all <- sort(unique(round(st$dz, 6)))
    dz_all <- dz_all[dz_all <= max(keep_dz) + align_slice_match_eps]
    if (!is.null(align_vis_n_rows) && length(dz_all) > align_vis_n_rows)
      dz_all <- dz_all[seq_len(align_vis_n_rows)]

    panel_col  <- vector("list", length(dz_all))
    status_col <- vector("list", length(dz_all))
    refit_col  <- vector("list", length(dz_all))

    for (r in seq_along(dz_all)) {
      hit <- which(abs(st$dz - dz_all[r]) <= align_slice_match_eps)
      if (length(hit) != 1L || is.na(st$status[hit])) {
        panel_col[[r]] <- NULL; status_col[[r]] <- NA_character_; refit_col[[r]] <- FALSE
        next
      }
      row_data <- .align_row(align_res_1$refit_flagged, align_res_1$clean2, tid,
                             st$row_idx[hit], st$slice_z[hit])
      panel_col[[r]]  <- make_threshold_panel(row_data, align_pts_cache)
      status_col[[r]] <- st$status[hit]
      refit_col[[r]]  <- isTRUE(st$refit[hit])
    }

    list(
      matrix     = lapply(panel_col,  function(x) list(x)),
      status     = lapply(status_col, function(x) list(x)),
      refit      = lapply(refit_col,  function(x) list(x)),
      row_labels = sprintf("h \u2248 %.3f m", dz_all + align_label_offset),
      col_labels = "las_1 (align)"
    )
  }

  # ── Renderer - single-column version of the Step 1.4 grid renderer ──────────
  render_align_grid <- function(grid_obj, lb_id, w = 3.2, h = 3.2, dpi = 140) {

    panel_matrix  <- grid_obj$matrix
    status_matrix <- grid_obj$status
    refit_matrix  <- grid_obj$refit
    row_labels    <- grid_obj$row_labels
    col_labels    <- grid_obj$col_labels
    n_col         <- length(col_labels)

    has_content <- any(vapply(panel_matrix, function(row)
      any(!vapply(row, is.null, logical(1))), logical(1)))
    if (!has_content) return(HTML("<p>No data.</p>"))

    encode_plot <- function(p) {
      if (is.null(p)) return(NA_character_)
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
      on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
      ggsave(tmp, plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi, bg = NA)
      paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(tmp))
    }

    border_spec <- function(status) {
      switch(as.character(status),
             "consensus2" = c(align_col_consensus2, align_px),
             "mad2"       = c(align_col_mad2,       align_px),
             "mad1"       = c(align_col_mad1,       align_px_mad1),
             "unrefit"    = c(align_col_unrefit,    align_px),
             c("transparent", align_px_mad1))   # kept: reserve the widest gutter
    }

    cell_tag <- function(src, status, is_refit) {
      if (is.na(src))
        return('<div style="background:#f4f4f4;border-radius:6px;min-height:120px;"></div>')
      bs  <- border_spec(status)
      bg  <- if (isTRUE(is_refit)) align_bg_refit else align_bg_plain
      sprintf(
        '<div style="background:%s;border:%spx solid %s;border-radius:6px;
                     box-sizing:border-box;padding:2px;">
           <img src="%s"
                style="width:100%%;display:block;border-radius:4px;cursor:zoom-in;"
                onclick="openLb_%s(this.src)" />
         </div>',
        bg, bs[2], bs[1], src, lb_id
      )
    }

    header_row <- sprintf(
      '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;margin-bottom:4px;"><div></div>%s</div>',
      n_col,
      paste(vapply(col_labels, function(lbl)
        sprintf('<div style="font-size:12px;font-weight:600;text-align:center;padding:2px;">%s</div>', lbl),
        character(1)), collapse = ""))

    swatch <- function(col, px, txt, bg = "white")
      sprintf('<span style="display:inline-block;width:16px;height:16px;background:%s;
                            border:%dpx solid %s;vertical-align:-3px;
                            margin:0 5px 0 14px;box-sizing:border-box;"></span>%s',
              bg, px, col, txt)

    legend <- sprintf(
      '<div style="font-size:12px;margin:0 0 10px 2px;line-height:1.9;">%s%s%s%s%s</div>',
      swatch("#cccccc", 1, "refit slice (grey background)", align_bg_refit),
      swatch(align_col_consensus2, align_px,      "2nd-pass consensus removal"),
      swatch(align_col_mad2,       align_px,      "2nd-pass MAD removal"),
      swatch(align_col_mad1,       align_px_mad1, "1st-pass MAD removal"),
      swatch(align_col_unrefit,    align_px,      "consensus removal, refit failed"))

    body_rows <- paste(
      vapply(seq_along(panel_matrix), function(r) {
        cells <- vapply(panel_matrix[[r]], encode_plot, character(1))
        stats <- status_matrix[[r]]
        rfs   <- refit_matrix[[r]]
        imgs  <- paste(vapply(seq_along(cells),
                              function(k) cell_tag(cells[k], stats[[k]], rfs[[k]]),
                              character(1)), collapse = "")
        sprintf(
          '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:6px;">
             <div style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;">%s</div>%s
           </div>',
          n_col, row_labels[r], imgs
        )
      }, character(1)),
      collapse = "\n"
    )

    HTML(sprintf('
<style>
  #lbOv_%s{display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9999;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,.82);align-items:center;justify-content:center;}
  #lbOv_%s.open{display:flex;}
  #lbOv_%s img{max-width:95vw;max-height:95vh;border-radius:6px;background:#fff;
    box-shadow:0 4px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6);}
  #lbCl_%s{position:fixed;top:16px;right:20px;font-size:32px;color:#fff;
    cursor:pointer;line-height:1;user-select:none;z-index:10000;}
</style>
<div id="lbOv_%s" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeLb_%s()">
  <span id="lbCl_%s" onclick="closeLb_%s()">&#x2715;</span>
  <img id="lbIm_%s" src=""/>
</div>
<div style="padding:10px;overflow-x:auto;">%s%s%s</div>
<script>
  window.openLb_%s  = s => {
    document.getElementById("lbIm_%s").src = s;
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.add("open");
  };
  window.closeLb_%s = () =>
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.remove("open");
</script>',
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
      legend, header_row, body_rows,
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id
    ))
  }

  # ── One grid per selected tree ───────────────────────────────────────────────
  align_tree_blocks <- lapply(seq_along(wanted), function(i) {

    tid <- wanted[i]

    grid_obj <- make_align_grid(tid)
    if (is.null(grid_obj)) return(NULL)

    n_of <- function(v) sum(vapply(grid_obj$status,
                                   function(rw) sum(vapply(rw, function(s)
                                     !is.na(s) && s == v, logical(1))),
                                   integer(1)))
    n_refit <- sum(vapply(grid_obj$refit,
                          function(rw) sum(vapply(rw, isTRUE, logical(1))),
                          integer(1)))

    tagList(
      h3(sprintf("Tree %d of %d \u2014 las_1 TreeID %s (Stage 1A alignment fit)",
                 i, length(wanted), tid)),
      h4(sprintf("%d refit | kept %d | consensus2 %d | mad2 %d | mad1 %d | unrefit %d",
                 n_refit, n_of("kept"), n_of("consensus2"),
                 n_of("mad2"), n_of("mad1"), n_of("unrefit"))),
      render_align_grid(grid_obj, sprintf("aligngrid_%s", tid))
    )
  })

  browsable(tagList(
    h3("Slice status after the Stage 1A alignment fit + refit + second cleaning"),
```
