```{r}
    h4("Rows = slice-centre height above each stem's own lowest point \u2014 single column (Stage 1A fits only the align_las_1 subset)"),
    h4("Grey background = refit | red = 2nd-pass consensus | orange = 2nd-pass MAD | thick black = 1st-pass MAD"),
    align_tree_blocks
  ))

} else {
  cat("\nStage 1A slice-status visualisation SKIPPED (make_plots = FALSE, second_run = TRUE, or alignment not run).\n")
}
```

### Vis - Stage 1A.1b las_2 slice status

The same per-slice status view for the *second* epoch. Stage 1A itself never
fits `las_2` - the rough vertical alignment rotates `las_1` only - so there is
no `align_res_2` to read. What there is, is the density probe's own fit: step
1A.1b runs the identical fit -> clean -> masked refit -> reclean on `las_2`'s
largest stems purely to measure them, and `density_res_2` holds the full result
with the same structure `align_res_1` has. This renders that.

Two things follow from where the data comes from. The panels only exist when
`run_density_probe` is TRUE, and they are drawn at the PROBE's geometry
(`density_probe_width` / `density_probe_step`), which is not necessarily the
thickness Step 1.1 went on to use - so read these as a picture of what the
scarce epoch looks like, not as a preview of the main fit.

```{r}
#| label: align-vis-slice-status-las2
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Per-slice panels for the las_2 density-probe fit; grey background = refit, red/orange/purple/blue borders = removal stage"

if (!second_run && params$make_plots &&
    exists("density_res_2") && !is.null(density_res_2)) {

  if (is.null(density_res_2$refit_flagged) || length(density_res_2$refit_flagged) == 0L)
    stop("density_res_2$refit_flagged not found - run the align-density-probe chunk first.")

  # ── User input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  a2_vis_treeids     <- NULL     # NULL = every tree in the probe fit
  a2_vis_n_rows      <- NULL     # NULL = every slice; k = first k from the lowest
  a2_slice_match_eps <- 1e-6

  # ── Appearance (identical palette/meaning to the las_1 view) ───────────────
  a2_bg_refit       <- "#ECCCCC"   # slice was refit
  a2_bg_plain       <- "white"
  a2_col_consensus2 <- "#D7263D"   # red    - removed by 2nd-pass consensus
  a2_col_mad2       <- "#F07C10"   # orange - removed by 2nd-pass MAD
  a2_col_mad1       <- "purple"    # 1st-pass MAD removal (thicker border)
  a2_col_unrefit    <- "blue"      # 1st-pass consensus removal, refit failed
  a2_px             <- 6
  a2_px_mad1        <- 10

  # The probe's own geometry, not Step 1.1's - these panels are the probe's fit.
  a2_slice_width <- if (exists("density_probe_width") && !is.null(density_probe_width))
                      density_probe_width else align_slice_width
  a2_label_offset <- (if (is.null(align_slice_bot)) 0 else align_slice_bot) +
                     a2_slice_width / 2

  # ── Per-slice status, read from the stored probe results (not recomputed) ──
  # Priority is identical to the las_1 view, and can be, because density_res_2
  # comes out of the same .fit_clean_refit_reclean() call:
  #   mad1       - dropped by the first MAD stage (never a refit target)
  #   unrefit    - dropped by first-pass consensus, refit did not succeed
  #   consensus2 - entered pass 2, dropped by consensus
  #   mad2       - entered pass 2, dropped by MAD
  #   kept       - survived everything
  # This matters more on las_2 than it did on las_1: the probe reported 16 of 20
  # stems entering pass 2 with no surviving slices, and every one of those
  # renders here as a full column of unrefit panels rather than vanishing.
  .a2_status_frame <- function(refit_flagged, clean2_result, tid) {
    base <- refit_flagged[[as.character(tid)]]
    if (is.null(base) || nrow(base) == 0L) return(NULL)
    base <- as.data.frame(base)

    c2 <- if (!is.null(clean2_result)) clean2_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged else NULL
    c2 <- if (is.null(c2) || nrow(c2) == 0L) NULL else as.data.frame(c2)

    n      <- nrow(base)
    status <- rep(NA_character_, n)

    for (i in seq_len(n)) {
      if (isTRUE(base$unfitted[i])) next          # never fitted -> blank cell

      if (isTRUE(base$mad_minor_out[i]) ||
          isTRUE(base$mad_major_out[i])) { status[i] <- "mad1"; next }

      hit <- if (is.null(c2)) integer(0) else
               which(abs(c2$slice_z - base$slice_z[i]) <= a2_slice_match_eps)

      if (length(hit) != 1L) { status[i] <- "unrefit"; next }

      status[i] <-
        if (isTRUE(c2$no_consensus[hit]))  "consensus2" else
        if (isTRUE(c2$mad_minor_out[hit]) ||
            isTRUE(c2$mad_major_out[hit]))  "mad2"       else "kept"
    }

    data.frame(
      slice_z = base$slice_z,
      dz      = base$slice_z - min(base$slice_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      status  = status,
      refit   = if ("refit" %in% names(base)) base$refit else rep(FALSE, n),
      row_idx = seq_len(n),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }

  # Geometry for a panel: prefer the pass-2 frame when the slice reached it,
  # else fall back to refit_flagged (mad1 and unrefit slices, which pass 2
  # never saw).
  .a2_row <- function(refit_flagged, clean2_result, tid, row_idx, slice_z) {
    c2 <- if (!is.null(clean2_result)) clean2_result[[as.character(tid)]]$flagged else NULL
    if (!is.null(c2) && nrow(c2) > 0L) {
      c2  <- as.data.frame(c2)
      hit <- which(abs(c2$slice_z - slice_z) <= a2_slice_match_eps)
      if (length(hit) == 1L) return(c2[hit, , drop = FALSE])
    }
    base <- as.data.frame(refit_flagged[[as.character(tid)]])
    base[row_idx, , drop = FALSE]
  }

  # The probe did not keep its subset cloud, so rebuild the cache from las_2
  # restricted to exactly the trees the probe fitted - filter_poi rather than
  # the whole cloud, since the panels only ever index points on these stems.
  a2_tree_ids <- names(density_res_2$refit_flagged)
  a2_las      <- lidR::filter_poi(las_2, TreeID %in% as.integer(a2_tree_ids))
  a2_pts_cache <- as.data.frame(a2_las@data[, c("point_id", "X", "Y")])

  wanted2 <- if (is.null(a2_vis_treeids)) a2_tree_ids else as.character(a2_vis_treeids)
  wanted2 <- wanted2[wanted2 %in% names(density_res_2$refit_flagged)]
  if (length(wanted2) == 0L) stop("No renderable las_2 probe trees.")

  cat(sprintf("Rendering %d las_2 density-probe tree(s) (of %d fitted).\n",
              length(wanted2), length(a2_tree_ids)))

  # ── One grid per tree, single column ───────────────────────────────────────
  make_a2_grid <- function(tid) {

    st <- .a2_status_frame(density_res_2$refit_flagged, density_res_2$clean2, tid)
    if (is.null(st)) return(NULL)

    keep_dz <- st$dz[!is.na(st$status)]
    if (length(keep_dz) == 0L) return(NULL)
    dz_all <- sort(unique(round(st$dz, 6)))
    dz_all <- dz_all[dz_all <= max(keep_dz) + a2_slice_match_eps]
    if (!is.null(a2_vis_n_rows) && length(dz_all) > a2_vis_n_rows)
      dz_all <- dz_all[seq_len(a2_vis_n_rows)]

    panel_col  <- vector("list", length(dz_all))
    status_col <- vector("list", length(dz_all))
    refit_col  <- vector("list", length(dz_all))

    for (r in seq_along(dz_all)) {
      hit <- which(abs(st$dz - dz_all[r]) <= a2_slice_match_eps)
      if (length(hit) != 1L || is.na(st$status[hit])) {
        panel_col[[r]] <- NULL; status_col[[r]] <- NA_character_; refit_col[[r]] <- FALSE
        next
      }
      row_data <- .a2_row(density_res_2$refit_flagged, density_res_2$clean2, tid,
                          st$row_idx[hit], st$slice_z[hit])
      panel_col[[r]]  <- make_threshold_panel(row_data, a2_pts_cache)
      status_col[[r]] <- st$status[hit]
      refit_col[[r]]  <- isTRUE(st$refit[hit])
    }

    list(
      matrix     = lapply(panel_col,  function(x) list(x)),
      status     = lapply(status_col, function(x) list(x)),
      refit      = lapply(refit_col,  function(x) list(x)),
      row_labels = sprintf("h \u2248 %.3f m", dz_all + a2_label_offset),
      col_labels = "las_2 (probe)"
    )
  }

  # ── Renderer - same single-column grid, own lightbox ids ───────────────────
  render_a2_grid <- function(grid_obj, lb_id, w = 3.2, h = 3.2, dpi = 140) {

    panel_matrix  <- grid_obj$matrix
    status_matrix <- grid_obj$status
    refit_matrix  <- grid_obj$refit
    row_labels    <- grid_obj$row_labels
    col_labels    <- grid_obj$col_labels
    n_col         <- length(col_labels)

    has_content <- any(vapply(panel_matrix, function(row)
      any(!vapply(row, is.null, logical(1))), logical(1)))
    if (!has_content) return(HTML("<p>No data.</p>"))

    encode_plot <- function(p) {
      if (is.null(p)) return(NA_character_)
      tmp <- tempfile(fileext = ".png")
      on.exit(unlink(tmp), add = TRUE)
      ggsave(tmp, plot = p, width = w, height = h, dpi = dpi, bg = NA)
      paste0("data:image/png;base64,", base64enc::base64encode(tmp))
    }

    border_spec <- function(status) {
      switch(as.character(status),
             "consensus2" = c(a2_col_consensus2, a2_px),
             "mad2"       = c(a2_col_mad2,       a2_px),
             "mad1"       = c(a2_col_mad1,       a2_px_mad1),
             "unrefit"    = c(a2_col_unrefit,    a2_px),
             c("transparent", a2_px_mad1))   # kept: reserve the widest gutter
    }

    cell_tag <- function(src, status, is_refit) {
      if (is.na(src))
        return('<div style="background:#f4f4f4;border-radius:6px;min-height:120px;"></div>')
      bs  <- border_spec(status)
      bg  <- if (isTRUE(is_refit)) a2_bg_refit else a2_bg_plain
      sprintf(
        '<div style="background:%s;border:%spx solid %s;border-radius:6px;
                     box-sizing:border-box;padding:2px;">
           <img src="%s"
                style="width:100%%;display:block;border-radius:4px;cursor:zoom-in;"
                onclick="openLb_%s(this.src)" />
         </div>',
        bg, bs[2], bs[1], src, lb_id
      )
    }

    header_row <- sprintf(
      '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;margin-bottom:4px;"><div></div>%s</div>',
      n_col,
      paste(vapply(col_labels, function(lbl)
        sprintf('<div style="font-size:12px;font-weight:600;text-align:center;padding:2px;">%s</div>', lbl),
        character(1)), collapse = ""))

    swatch <- function(col, px, txt, bg = "white")
      sprintf('<span style="display:inline-block;width:16px;height:16px;background:%s;
                            border:%dpx solid %s;vertical-align:-3px;
                            margin:0 5px 0 14px;box-sizing:border-box;"></span>%s',
              bg, px, col, txt)

    legend <- sprintf(
      '<div style="font-size:12px;margin:0 0 10px 2px;line-height:1.9;">%s%s%s%s%s</div>',
      swatch("#cccccc", 1, "refit slice (grey background)", a2_bg_refit),
      swatch(a2_col_consensus2, a2_px,      "2nd-pass consensus removal"),
      swatch(a2_col_mad2,       a2_px,      "2nd-pass MAD removal"),
      swatch(a2_col_mad1,       a2_px_mad1, "1st-pass MAD removal"),
      swatch(a2_col_unrefit,    a2_px,      "consensus removal, refit failed"))

    body_rows <- paste(
      vapply(seq_along(panel_matrix), function(r) {
        cells <- vapply(panel_matrix[[r]], encode_plot, character(1))
        stats <- status_matrix[[r]]
        rfs   <- refit_matrix[[r]]
        imgs  <- paste(vapply(seq_along(cells),
                              function(k) cell_tag(cells[k], stats[[k]], rfs[[k]]),
                              character(1)), collapse = "")
        sprintf(
          '<div style="display:grid;grid-template-columns:90px repeat(%d,1fr);gap:6px;align-items:center;margin-bottom:6px;">
             <div style="font-size:11px;font-weight:600;">%s</div>%s
           </div>',
          n_col, row_labels[r], imgs
        )
      }, character(1)),
      collapse = "\n"
    )

    HTML(sprintf('
<style>
  #lbOv_%s{display:none;position:fixed;inset:0;z-index:9999;
    background:rgba(0,0,0,.82);align-items:center;justify-content:center;}
  #lbOv_%s.open{display:flex;}
  #lbOv_%s img{max-width:95vw;max-height:95vh;border-radius:6px;background:#fff;
    box-shadow:0 4px 40px rgba(0,0,0,.6);}
  #lbCl_%s{position:fixed;top:16px;right:20px;font-size:32px;color:#fff;
    cursor:pointer;line-height:1;user-select:none;z-index:10000;}
</style>
<div id="lbOv_%s" onclick="if(event.target===this)closeLb_%s()">
  <span id="lbCl_%s" onclick="closeLb_%s()">&#x2715;</span>
  <img id="lbIm_%s" src=""/>
</div>
<div style="padding:10px;overflow-x:auto;">%s%s%s</div>
<script>
  window.openLb_%s  = s => {
    document.getElementById("lbIm_%s").src = s;
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.add("open");
  };
  window.closeLb_%s = () =>
    document.getElementById("lbOv_%s").classList.remove("open");
</script>',
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id,
      legend, header_row, body_rows,
      lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id, lb_id
    ))
  }

  # ── One grid per selected tree ─────────────────────────────────────────────
  a2_tree_blocks <- lapply(seq_along(wanted2), function(i) {

    tid <- wanted2[i]

    grid_obj <- make_a2_grid(tid)
    if (is.null(grid_obj)) return(NULL)

    n_of <- function(v) sum(vapply(grid_obj$status,
                                   function(rw) sum(vapply(rw, function(s)
                                     !is.na(s) && s == v, logical(1))),
                                   integer(1)))
    n_refit <- sum(vapply(grid_obj$refit,
                          function(rw) sum(vapply(rw, isTRUE, logical(1))),
                          integer(1)))

    tagList(
      h3(sprintf("Tree %d of %d \u2014 las_2 TreeID %s (density-probe fit)",
                 i, length(wanted2), tid)),
      h4(sprintf("%d refit | kept %d | consensus2 %d | mad2 %d | mad1 %d | unrefit %d",
                 n_refit, n_of("kept"), n_of("consensus2"),
                 n_of("mad2"), n_of("mad1"), n_of("unrefit"))),
      render_a2_grid(grid_obj, sprintf("a2grid_%s", tid))
    )
  })

  browsable(tagList(
    h3("Slice status after the las_2 density-probe fit + refit + second cleaning"),
    h4(sprintf(paste0("Rows = slice-centre height above each stem's own lowest point ",
                      "\u2014 single column (probe geometry: %.0f cm slices every %.0f cm)"),
               a2_slice_width * 100,
               (if (exists("density_probe_step") && !is.null(density_probe_step))
                  density_probe_step else align_slice_step) * 100)),
    h4("Grey background = refit | red = 2nd-pass consensus | orange = 2nd-pass MAD | purple = 1st-pass MAD | blue = refit failed"),
    a2_tree_blocks
  ))

} else {
  cat("\nlas_2 slice-status visualisation SKIPPED (make_plots = FALSE, second_run = TRUE, or the density probe did not run).\n")
}
```

```{r}
#| label: params-align-upside-down
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Quarter-coverage filter, kept-count MAD filter, and the asymmetric verdict band"


# ── Quarter-coverage filter ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Minimum kept ellipses required in EACH of the four equal-height quarters that
# span a stem's lowest-to-highest kept ellipse. Anchors the area-vs-height
# regression across the whole stem instead of a cluster at one end. A stem needs
# at least 4 * align_qtr_min kept ellipses to have any chance of passing.
align_qtr_min <- 2L

# ── Kept-ellipse-count MAD filter ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Multiplier on the scaled MAD of the per-stem kept-ellipse count. Stems further
# than this from the median count are dropped before the slope is read.
align_mad_mult <- 3.0

# Kept ellipses a surviving stem needs before .align_slope_frame() will fit it an
# area-vs-height slope (helper default is 3L).
align_ud_min_n <- 3L

# ── Asymmetric verdict band ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
# align_frac = n_neg / (n_neg + n_pos). At or below _lo the cloud is called
# upside-down; at or above _hi it is right-side-up confidently; between them it
# is right-side-up BY ASSUMPTION, since 1A.0 has already settled sideways
# geometrically. Deliberately asymmetric: upside-down has to be proven, so a
# bare majority of positive slopes no longer flips the cloud.
align_ud_frac_lo <- 0.25
align_ud_frac_hi <- 0.75

.par_apply("params-align-upside-down")
```

```{r}
#| label: align-upside-down
#| code-summary: "Quarter-coverage + MAD filter on stems, then majority slope sign sets the verdict"

if (run_rough_alignment && !is.null(align_kept_1)) {

  # ── Quarter-coverage filter: >= align_qtr_min kept ellipses in each of the four
  #    equal-height quarters spanning a stem's lowest-to-highest kept ellipse ────
  # Anchors the taper regression across the whole stem, not a cluster at one end.
  # Non-destructive: align_kept_1 itself is left intact.
  .qtr_ok <- vapply(align_kept_1, function(d) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) < 4L * align_qtr_min) return(FALSE)
    z  <- d$slice_z
    zr <- range(z)
    sp <- zr[2L] - zr[1L]
    if (!is.finite(sp) || sp <= 0) return(FALSE)   # zero span -> all in one quarter
    q  <- pmin(4L, floor((z - zr[1L]) / sp * 4) + 1L)   # zmax lands in bin 5 -> clamp to 4
    all(tabulate(q, nbins = 4L) >= align_qtr_min)
  }, logical(1))

  align_kept_1_qtr  <- align_kept_1[.qtr_ok]
  align_qtr_dropped <- names(align_kept_1)[!.qtr_ok]

  cat(sprintf("Quarter-coverage filter (>= %d per quarter): %d of %d stems kept\n",
              align_qtr_min, sum(.qtr_ok), length(.qtr_ok)))
  if (length(align_qtr_dropped) > 0L)
    cat(sprintf("  dropped %d stem(s): %s\n",
                length(align_qtr_dropped), paste(align_qtr_dropped, collapse = ", ")))

  # ── MAD filter: drop stems whose kept-ellipse count is an outlier ────────────
  # Operates on the quarter-coverage survivors. Rebuilt each run, so re-running
  # at a different multiplier does not compound.
  .n_kept <- vapply(align_kept_1_qtr, function(d)
    if (is.null(d)) 0L else nrow(d), integer(1))
  .med  <- if (length(.n_kept)) stats::median(.n_kept) else NA_real_
  .madn <- if (length(.n_kept)) stats::mad(.n_kept)    else NA_real_   # scaled (x 1.4826)

  if (is.finite(.madn) && .madn > 0) {
    .keep_mad <- abs(.n_kept - .med) <= align_mad_mult * .madn
  } else {
    .keep_mad <- rep(TRUE, length(.n_kept))   # no spread -> nothing to flag
  }
  align_kept_1_mad  <- align_kept_1_qtr[.keep_mad]
  align_mad_dropped <- names(align_kept_1_qtr)[!.keep_mad]

  cat(sprintf("Kept-ellipse-count MAD filter (mult = %g): median %g, MAD %g -> %d of %d stems kept\n",
              align_mad_mult, .med, .madn, sum(.keep_mad), length(.keep_mad)))
  if (length(align_mad_dropped) > 0L)
    cat(sprintf("  dropped %d stem(s): %s\n",
                length(align_mad_dropped), paste(align_mad_dropped, collapse = ", ")))

  align_slope_df <- .align_slope_frame(align_kept_1_mad, align_ud_min_n)

  # Counts come from the helper; the fraction and the verdict are derived here so
  # the n_neg/(n_neg+n_pos) metric lives entirely in this chunk.
  .verdict <- .align_orientation_verdict(align_slope_df)

  n_pos <- .verdict$n_pos
  n_neg <- .verdict$n_neg
  .denom     <- n_neg + n_pos
  align_frac <- if (.denom > 0L) n_neg / .denom else NA_real_

  # ASYMMETRIC BAND. Upside-down has to clear align_ud_frac_lo; everything else,
  # grey zone included, stays right-side-up. An undefined fraction (no scored
  # stem) is not evidence either, so it lands right-side-up as well.
  # align_sideways is 1A.0's and is not touched here.
  align_upside_down <- isTRUE(align_frac <= align_ud_frac_lo)
  align_orientation <- if (align_upside_down) "upside-down" else "right-side-up"

  # TRUE when the band decided, FALSE when the grey zone did (or nothing was
  # scorable). Recorded so a weak verdict can be told from a firm one later.
  align_ud_confident <- is.finite(align_frac) &&
    (align_frac <= align_ud_frac_lo || align_frac >= align_ud_frac_hi)

  cat(sprintf("Area-vs-height slope per stem (n = %d scored of %d):\n",
              .verdict$n_scored, nrow(align_slope_df)))
  cat(sprintf("  negative (tapering, upright)   : %d\n", n_neg))
  cat(sprintf("  positive (widening, inverted)  : %d\n", n_pos))
  cat(sprintf("  fraction n_neg / (n_neg+n_pos) : %s  (band: <= %.2f upside-down | >= %.2f right-side-up)\n",
              if (is.finite(align_frac)) sprintf("%.3f", align_frac) else "undefined",
              align_ud_frac_lo, align_ud_frac_hi))
  cat(sprintf("  verdict: cloud is %s%s%s\n",
              if (align_upside_down) "UPSIDE-DOWN -> forest axis will be reversed"
              else if (align_ud_confident) "right-side-up"
              else "right-side-up (ASSUMED - fraction in the grey zone, cloud left as it stands)",
              if (isTRUE(.verdict$majority_upside_down) && !align_upside_down)
                " [note: positive slopes are in the majority, but the fraction did not clear the band]" else "",
              if (isTRUE(align_sideways_rotated))
                " (read on the cloud 1A.0 tipped upright)" else ""))

  # ── Optional diagnostic: one area-vs-height panel per stem ───────────────────
  if (isTRUE(params$make_plots) && .verdict$n_scored > 0L) {
    .ad <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(align_kept_1_mad), function(tid) {
      d <- align_kept_1_mad[[tid]]
      if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L) return(NULL)
      sl <- align_slope_df$slope[align_slope_df$TreeID == tid]
      data.frame(TreeID = tid,
                 h    = d$slice_z,
                 area = pi * d$semi_a * d$semi_b,
                 sign = if (length(sl) == 0L || is.na(sl)) "n/a"
                        else if (sl > 0) "positive" else "negative",
                 stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }))
    if (!is.null(.ad) && nrow(.ad) > 0L) {
      # Facet label carries the per-stem slope sign so each panel is self-describing.
      .ad$facet <- sprintf("%s (%s)", .ad$TreeID, .ad$sign)
      print(
        ggplot(.ad, aes(h, area, colour = sign)) +
          geom_line(alpha = 0.6) +
          geom_point(size = 0.9) +
          facet_wrap(~ facet, scales = "free") +
          scale_colour_manual(values = c(positive = "#2196F3",
                                          negative = "#FF5722", `n/a` = "grey70")) +
          scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0, 0)) +
          labs(title = "Epoch-1 ellipse area vs height (one panel per stem)",
               subtitle = sprintf("%d positive / %d negative slopes -> %s",
                                   n_pos, n_neg, align_orientation),
               x = "Height (m)", y = expression(Ellipse~area~(m^2)),
               colour = "Slope") +
          theme(legend.position = "bottom")
      )
    }
  }

} else {
  align_slope_df    <- NULL
  align_kept_1_qtr  <- NULL
  align_kept_1_mad   <- NULL
  align_orientation  <- "right-side-up"
  align_upside_down  <- FALSE
  align_ud_confident <- FALSE
  cat("Upside-down evaluation skipped; verdict defaults to right-side-up.\n")
}
```

## 1A.3 Forest Average Axis

A stem axis is fit to every epoch-1 stem by Theil-Sen regression of `x ~ z` and
`y ~ z` over **all** its kept ellipse centres - robust to the odd stray centre
and, because the direction vector is `(b_x, b_y, 1)` normalised, always pointing
up (`vz > 0`) by construction. The per-stem unit vectors are averaged into a
single forest axis, which is **reversed** if the cloud was diagnosed upside-down.

```{r}
#| label: params-align-forest-axis
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Per-stem Theil-Sen axis over all kept centres, averaged into one forest vector"


align_axis_min_n    <- 4L      # kept centres a stem needs to contribute an axis
align_axis_ts_max_n <- 120L    # above this, sample pairs instead of all pairs
align_axis_ts_pairs <- 20000L
align_axis_seed     <- 42L

.par_apply("params-align-forest-axis")
```

```{r}
#| label: align-forest-axis
#| code-summary: "Per-stem Theil-Sen axis over all kept centres, averaged into one forest vector"

if (run_rough_alignment && !is.null(align_kept_1)) {

  .fa <- .align_forest_axis(align_kept_1,
                            min_n    = align_axis_min_n,
                            ts_max_n = align_axis_ts_max_n,
                            ts_pairs = align_axis_ts_pairs,
                            seed     = align_axis_seed)

  if (is.null(.fa))
    stop("Rough alignment: no epoch-1 stem yielded a valid axis - loosen align_axis_min_n or check the fit.")

  # Averaged per-stem axis, BEFORE any upside-down reversal. Every per-stem
  # vector has vz > 0 by construction, so this mean also points up; the flip
  # below is the only thing that can send the forest axis downward.
  forest_axis_pre_1 <- .fa$axis

  # Apply the flip iff the cloud was diagnosed upside-down (1A.2), and record
  # the verdict as its own flag so downstream / the write-up can read it back.
  # A sideways forest was already tipped upright in 1A.0, before the fit these
  # centres come from, so there is no deferred case left to handle here.
  align_axis_flipped <- isTRUE(align_upside_down)
  forest_axis_vec_1  <- if (align_axis_flipped) -forest_axis_pre_1 else forest_axis_pre_1

  cat(sprintf("Per-stem axes: %d of %d stems yielded a vector.\n",
              .fa$n_ok, .fa$n_total))

  # ── Flip verdict (explicit) ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (align_axis_flipped) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Forest axis FLIPPED (cloud diagnosed upside-down in 1A.2).\n  before flip: (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n  after  flip: (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
      forest_axis_pre_1[1], forest_axis_pre_1[2], forest_axis_pre_1[3],
      forest_axis_vec_1[1], forest_axis_vec_1[2], forest_axis_vec_1[3]))
  } else {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Forest axis NOT flipped (cloud diagnosed right-way-up in 1A.2).\n  axis: (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)\n",
      forest_axis_vec_1[1], forest_axis_vec_1[2], forest_axis_vec_1[3]))
  }

  cat(sprintf("Tilt from vertical: %.2f deg\n",
              acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, abs(forest_axis_vec_1[3])))) * 180 / pi))

} else {
  forest_axis_vec_1  <- c(0, 0, 1)
  forest_axis_pre_1  <- c(0, 0, 1)
  align_axis_flipped <- FALSE
  cat("Forest axis skipped; defaults to global +Z (no flip, no rotation).\n")
}
```

## 1A.4 Rough Vertical Alignment

`las_1` is rotated so the forest axis points along global +Z, about the current
`pivot1`. The rotation is the minimal one carrying the forest vector onto the Z
axis (Rodrigues; a 180-degree flip about a horizontal axis in the upside-down
case). `xyz_1` is refreshed from the rotated cloud; **`pivot1` is not**. It stays
exactly where it was, so that this rough rotation and the fine XYZ rotation
Stage 2 solves turn about the *same* point - which is what keeps their
composition a pure rotation rather than a rotation plus a spurious translation.
`las_2` is untouched.

When 1A.0 tipped a sideways forest upright, that rotation (`R_sideways_pre` -
the 90-degree tip, with the 45-degree probe composed in if one was kept) is
already in the cloud. Only the **residual** rotation `R_residual`, carrying the
tipped forest axis the rest of the way onto +Z, is applied here; the recorded
`R_align_1 <- R_residual %*% R_sideways_pre` is the **total** original ->
aligned rotation. Both legs turn about the same `pivot1`, so applying the
residual now leaves the cloud exactly where applying the composed `R_align_1` to
the original would have. Outside the sideways case `R_sideways_pre` is the
identity and `R_align_1` reduces to the residual, so behaviour is unchanged.

```{r}
#| label: align-rotate-cloud
#| code-summary: "Rotate las_1 onto vertical; record R_align_1 and refresh pivot1 / xyz_1"

# Minimal rotation carrying unit vector u onto unit vector v (Rodrigues).
.rotation_from_to <- function(u, v) {
  u <- u / sqrt(sum(u^2)); v <- v / sqrt(sum(v^2))
  d <- sum(u * v)
  if (d >  1 - 1e-12) return(diag(3))
  if (d < -1 + 1e-12) {                      # antiparallel: 180 deg about any u-perp axis
    a <- if (abs(u[1]) < 0.9) c(1, 0, 0) else c(0, 1, 0)
    k <- a - sum(a * u) * u; k <- k / sqrt(sum(k^2))
    K <- matrix(c(0, -k[3], k[2], k[3], 0, -k[1], -k[2], k[1], 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)
    return(diag(3) + 2 * (K %*% K))
  }
  ax <- c(u[2]*v[3] - u[3]*v[2], u[3]*v[1] - u[1]*v[3], u[1]*v[2] - u[2]*v[1])
  s  <- sqrt(sum(ax^2)); k <- ax / s
  K  <- matrix(c(0, -k[3], k[2], k[3], 0, -k[1], -k[2], k[1], 0), 3, 3, byrow = TRUE)
  diag(3) + s * K + (1 - d) * (K %*% K)       # sin = s, cos = d
}

if (run_rough_alignment) {

  align_pivot_1 <- pivot1                       # rotate about the footprint centre

  # Residual rotation: carry the (possibly already-tipped) forest axis onto +Z.
  R_residual    <- .rotation_from_to(forest_axis_vec_1, c(0, 0, 1))

  # Total Stage-1A rotation = residual composed with any sideways correction
  # already applied to las_1 in 1A.0 (90 deg tip, plus the 45 deg probe when one
  # was kept). R_sideways_pre is the identity unless a sideways forest was
  # tipped, so this reduces to R_residual in the usual case.
  R_align_1     <- R_residual %*% R_sideways_pre

  # Apply ONLY the residual now: the sideways correction (if any) is already in
  # the cloud, and both rotations share align_pivot_1, so this leaves the cloud
  # where applying the composed R_align_1 to the original cloud would have.
  M   <- as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
  Mc  <- sweep(M, 2, align_pivot_1, "-")
  Mr  <- Mc %*% t(R_residual)
  Mr  <- sweep(Mr, 2, align_pivot_1, "+")

  las_1@data$X <- Mr[, 1]
  las_1@data$Y <- Mr[, 2]
  las_1@data$Z <- Mr[, 3]
  las_1 <- lidR::las_update(las_1)              # refresh header bbox

  xyz_1 <- as.matrix(las_1@data[, c("X", "Y", "Z")])

  # ── pivot1 is NOT recomputed - it stays exactly where it was ─────────────────
  # ONE PIVOT FOR BOTH ROTATIONS. The rough alignment here and the fine XYZ
  # rotation Stage 2 solves both turn about this same point, and that is what
  # makes their composition a pure rotation: R_xyz %*% R_align_1 about pivot1,
  # with no translation of its own.
  #
  # Recomputing pivot1 from the rotated bounding box (which earlier versions did)
  # moved it, because rotating a cloud does not move its bounding-box centre to
  # the rotated position of the old one - the box itself is re-fitted. The two
  # legs then turned about different points, their composition acquired a
  # residual translation, and every stage downstream had to carry a "shift" that
  # no stage had solved and that nothing in the data corresponds to. A rotation
  # should not produce a shift.
  #
  # The rotated bbox centre is still computed and reported below, as a
  # diagnostic only. pivot1 no longer sits exactly at the centre of the aligned
  # cloud's extent, and that is fine: a pivot has to be a well-defined point in
  # a known place relative to the cloud, consistent across every stage. It does
  # not have to be the centre of anything.
  .xr <- range(las_1@data$X); .yr <- range(las_1@data$Y); .zr <- range(las_1@data$Z)
  .bbox_centre_rot <- c(mean(.xr), mean(.yr), mean(.zr))

  cat("── Rough vertical alignment applied to las_1 ────────────────────────────\n")
  cat(sprintf("  orientation  : %s%s\n", align_orientation,
              if (isTRUE(align_sideways_rotated))
                sprintf(" (sideways: 90 deg tip%s composed in)",
                        if (isTRUE(align_sw_probed))
                          sprintf(" + %.0f deg probe", abs(align_sw_probe_deg)) else "")
              else ""))
  cat(sprintf("  forest axis  : (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)  (upside-down = %s)\n",
              forest_axis_vec_1[1], forest_axis_vec_1[2], forest_axis_vec_1[3],
              align_upside_down))
  cat(sprintf("  residual det : %.6f (should be 1)\n", det(R_residual)))
  cat(sprintf("  R_align_1 det: %.6f (should be 1; total original -> aligned)\n", det(R_align_1)))
  cat(sprintf("  pivot        : (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)  [align_pivot_1 == pivot1, unchanged]\n",
              align_pivot_1[1], align_pivot_1[2], align_pivot_1[3]))
  cat(sprintf("  rotated bbox centre (diagnostic only): (%.4f, %.4f, %.4f)  offset %.4f m\n",
              .bbox_centre_rot[1], .bbox_centre_rot[2], .bbox_centre_rot[3],
              sqrt(sum((.bbox_centre_rot - pivot1)^2))))
  cat("  las_2 left unchanged.\n")
  rm(.xr, .yr, .zr, .bbox_centre_rot)

  # ── Composition check: does R_align_1 reproduce the cloud? ──────────────────
  # Rotate the pre-Stage-1A sample by the SINGLE recorded matrix about
  # align_pivot_1 and compare against where those same rows actually ended up
  # after the (up to three) rotations that were applied one at a time. Anything
  # above a millimetre means the record and the cloud have parted company, and
  # every frame downstream - Stage 2's R_align_xyz_1, Stage 6's export - is
  # built on the record.
  align_check_max_err <- NA_real_
  if (!is.null(align_check_xyz0)) {
    .pred <- sweep(sweep(align_check_xyz0, 2, align_pivot_1, "-") %*% t(R_align_1),
                   2, align_pivot_1, "+")
    .act  <- as.matrix(las_1@data[align_check_idx, c("X", "Y", "Z")])
    align_check_max_err <- max(sqrt(rowSums((.pred - .act)^2)))
    cat(sprintf("  composition check: R_align_1 reproduces %d sampled point(s) to %.3e m\n",
                length(align_check_idx), align_check_max_err))
    if (!is.finite(align_check_max_err) || align_check_max_err > 1e-3)
      stop(sprintf(paste0("[1A.4] R_align_1 does NOT reproduce the rotated cloud (max error %.4g m).\n",
                          "  The recorded rotation and the rotations actually applied disagree, so\n",
                          "  every composition downstream would be wrong. Check the 1A.0 sideways\n",
                          "  correction and the residual composed here."), align_check_max_err))
    rm(.pred, .act)
  }

  # ── One record of every rotation Stage 1A applied ───────────────────────────
  # Each leg, the composition, the pivot they all share, and the flags saying
  # which legs were active. Saved whole so a run can be audited without
  # reconstructing anything from prose.
  .ang <- function(R) acos(pmax(-1, pmin(1, (sum(diag(R)) - 1) / 2))) * 180 / pi
  align_rotations <- list(
    pivot            = as.numeric(align_pivot_1),
    R_sideways_yaw   = R_sideways_yaw,
    R_sideways_90    = R_sideways_90,
    R_sideways_pre   = R_sideways_pre,
    R_residual       = R_residual,
    R_align_1        = R_align_1,
    order            = "R_align_1 = R_residual %*% R_sideways_90 %*% R_sideways_yaw, all about pivot",
    angles_deg       = c(yaw      = .ang(R_sideways_yaw),
                         tip90    = .ang(R_sideways_90),
                         sideways = .ang(R_sideways_pre),
                         residual = .ang(R_residual),
                         total    = .ang(R_align_1)),
    sideways         = isTRUE(align_sideways),
    sideways_rotated = isTRUE(align_sideways_rotated),
    probed           = isTRUE(align_sw_probed),
    upside_down      = align_upside_down,
    ud_confident     = isTRUE(align_ud_confident),
    orientation      = align_orientation,
    forest_axis      = as.numeric(forest_axis_vec_1),
    check_max_err_m  = align_check_max_err,
    check_n_points   = length(align_check_idx)
  )

  cat("  rotation ledger (deg): ")
  cat(paste(sprintf("%s %.4f", names(align_rotations$angles_deg),
                    align_rotations$angles_deg), collapse = " | "), "\n")
  rm(.ang)

} else {
  R_align_1           <- diag(3)
  R_residual          <- diag(3)
  align_pivot_1       <- pivot1
  align_check_max_err <- 0
  align_rotations <- list(
    pivot = as.numeric(align_pivot_1),
    R_sideways_yaw = diag(3), R_sideways_90 = diag(3), R_sideways_pre = diag(3),
    R_residual = diag(3), R_align_1 = diag(3),
    order = "identity - run_rough_alignment = FALSE",
    angles_deg = c(yaw = 0, tip90 = 0, sideways = 0, residual = 0, total = 0),
    sideways = FALSE, sideways_rotated = FALSE, probed = FALSE,
    upside_down = FALSE, ud_confident = FALSE, orientation = "right-side-up",
    forest_axis = c(0, 0, 1), check_max_err_m = 0, check_n_points = 0L
  )
  cat("No rotation applied (run_rough_alignment = FALSE); R_align_1 = identity.\n")
}
```

# Stage 1B - Temporal Pairs Identification



### Data - Tree Heights

```{r}
#| label: diag-tree-height-iqr
#| code-summary: "Diagnostic: IQR of per-tree heights (max Z - min Z) per epoch"

# ── Per-tree height = highest point - lowest point, for one cloud ──────────────
.tree_heights <- function(las, tids) {
  d <- las@data
  vapply(tids, function(tid) {
    z <- d$Z[!is.na(d$TreeID) & d$TreeID == tid]
    if (length(z) == 0L) NA_real_ else max(z, na.rm = TRUE) - min(z, na.rm = TRUE)
  }, numeric(1))
}

# ── Report quartiles / IQR for one epoch ──────────────────────────────────────
.report_height_iqr <- function(h, label) {
  h  <- h[is.finite(h)]
  if (length(h) == 0L) {
    cat(sprintf("[%s] no trees with finite heights.\n", label))
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  q  <- stats::quantile(h, c(0.25, 0.50, 0.75), na.rm = TRUE, names = FALSE)
  iqr <- q[3] - q[1]
  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("[%s] n = %d trees\n",
           "        min    = %6.2f m\n",
           "        Q1     = %6.2f m\n",
           "        median = %6.2f m\n",
           "        Q3     = %6.2f m\n",
           "        max    = %6.2f m\n",
           "        IQR    = %6.2f m   (fences: %.2f - %.2f m)\n"),
    label, length(h), min(h), q[1], q[2], q[3], max(h),
    iqr, q[1] - 1.5 * iqr, q[3] + 1.5 * iqr
  ))
  invisible(c(n = length(h), Q1 = q[1], median = q[2], Q3 = q[3], IQR = iqr))
}

heights_1 <- .tree_heights(las_1, treeids_1)
heights_2 <- .tree_heights(las_2, treeids_2)

cat("=== Per-tree height (max Z - min Z) – interquartile summary ===\n\n")
h_iqr_1 <- .report_height_iqr(heights_1, "las_1")
cat("\n")
h_iqr_2 <- .report_height_iqr(heights_2, "las_2")

# ── Epoch-to-epoch delta ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (!is.null(h_iqr_1) && !is.null(h_iqr_2)) {
  cat(sprintf("\n[delta] median %+.2f m | IQR %+.2f m (las_2 - las_1)\n",
              h_iqr_2[["median"]] - h_iqr_1[["median"]],
              h_iqr_2[["IQR"]]    - h_iqr_1[["IQR"]]))
}
```
  
## 1.1 Ellipse Fitting

```{r}
#| label: params-s1-ellipse-fitting-Run-1
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Subset LAS data (if using CSV) and run brute-force RANSAC ellipse fitting"


# ── Stage 1: RANSAC ellipse fitting (Step 1.1) ────────────────────────────────
ransac_slice_bot        <- 0.0    # m above tree base – lower edge of first slice
ransac_slice_top        <- 15.0   # m above tree base – CEILING on the last slice.
                                  #   A tree shorter than this is still fitted, just
                                  #   up to its own highest point. NULL = no ceiling.
ransac_height_min       <- 5.0    # m above tree base – a tree must be at least this

                                  #   tall to be fitted at all. NULL = fit every tree.
ransac_slice_step       <- 0.10   # step between slice centres (m)

                                                               # scalar (e.g. 0.04) → single fit, as before
                                                               # vector             → the whole fit (Parts B-D below)
                                                               #                      is repeated once per value
ransac_active_threshold     <- NULL   # which value in ransac_distance_threshold feeds Step 1.2 onward
ransac_track_history        <- FALSE   # record per-iteration convergence history (see fp_i below)

# ── Adaptive iteration budget ────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each slice gets iter_per_point x (candidate points available to that fit)
# iterations, clamped to [iter_min, iter_max]. Applies to BOTH RANSAC runs: the
# Step 1.1 fit and the Step 1.3b masked refit, where the point count is the
# masked subset. Set ransac_iter_per_point <- NULL to go back to a fixed budget.
ransac_iter_per_point       <- 1.0
ransac_iter_max             <- 750L
ransac_iter_min             <- 1L     # raise this if very sparse slices need a floor
                                       # (res_1/res_2/ellipses_zt_*_all/etc.). NULL → use the first value.
ransac_seed                 <- 33L    # RNG seed for reproducible sampling
#Subset Diagnostic (This only works in CSV mode:
s1_fit_treeids_1 <- NULL #   NULL → fit every tree (normal operation), c(1, 13)  → fit only las_1 TreeIDs 1 and 13

.par_apply("params-s1-ellipse-fitting-Run-1")
```

```{r}
#| label: s1-ellipse-fitting-Run-1
#| code-summary: "Subset LAS data (if using CSV) and run brute-force RANSAC ellipse fitting"

ransac_slice_width      <- 0.05   # slice thickness (m)

ransac_distance_threshold   <- 0.005   # distance from ellipse edge for point to be counted

# ── Fit settings from the 1A.1b density probe ─────────────────────────────────
# The probe measured both epochs and picked a regime; this adopts it. A NO-OP
# when the probe did not run, or when density_apply_regime is FALSE, in which
# case the values set above stand.
#
# This has to sit INSIDE this chunk rather than in its params chunk: both
# settings are assigned here and consumed a few lines below, so a value applied
# after the chunk - as the driver's parameter overrides are - would land too
# late to reach the fit.
if (exists("density_slice_width_reco") && !is.null(density_slice_width_reco) &&
    is.finite(density_slice_width_reco)) {
  ransac_slice_width <- density_slice_width_reco
  cat(sprintf("[1.1] density probe (%s, t = %.2f): slice thickness %.0f cm\n",
              density_regime, density_scarcity, ransac_slice_width * 100))
}
if (exists("density_distance_threshold_reco") && !is.null(density_distance_threshold_reco) &&
    all(is.finite(density_distance_threshold_reco))) {
  # A deliberately-set SWEEP vector is replaced by the single probe value, so
  # say so rather than let a threshold comparison silently collapse to one fit.
  if (length(ransac_distance_threshold) > 1L)
    message(sprintf(paste0("[1.1] density probe replaced the %d-value ransac_distance_threshold ",
                           "sweep with a single %.0f mm fit. Set density_apply_regime <- FALSE ",
                           "to keep the sweep."),
                    length(ransac_distance_threshold), density_distance_threshold_reco * 1000))
  ransac_distance_threshold <- density_distance_threshold_reco
  cat(sprintf("[1.1] density probe (%s, t = %.2f): distance threshold %.1f mm\n",
              density_regime, density_scarcity, ransac_distance_threshold * 1000))
}


if (!second_run) {

# ── Part A: Filter TreeIDs by CSV (Conditional) ──────────────────────────────
run_spatial_pairing <- !use_csv_pairs

use_treeid_subset <- !is.null(s1_fit_treeids_1) && length(s1_fit_treeids_1) > 0L

if (use_treeid_subset && !use_csv_pairs) {
  stop(
    "s1_fit_treeids_1 is set, but use_csv_pairs = FALSE.\n",
    "  The diagnostic TreeID subset needs temporal pairs to already exist so the\n",
    "  epoch-2 partners can be looked up. Spatial pairing (Step 1.3) instead\n",
    "  derives pairs from the fitted ellipses, so a subset would produce a\n",
    "  meaningless pairing over the few stems that happen to be present.\n",
    "  Either set use_csv_pairs <- TRUE, or set s1_fit_treeids_1 <- NULL."
  )
}

if (use_csv_pairs) {
  if (!file.exists(pairs_csv_path)) {
    stop(paste("Mapping CSV not found at:", pairs_csv_path))
  }

  mapping_df <- read.csv(pairs_csv_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

  # Identify which trees from the LAS files are present in the CSV columns
  csv_ids_1 <- unique(mapping_df[[col_treeid_las1]])
  csv_ids_2 <- unique(mapping_df[[col_treeid_las2]])

  # Overwrite the global treeid lists
  treeids_1 <- treeids_1[treeids_1 %in% csv_ids_1]
  treeids_2 <- treeids_2[treeids_2 %in% csv_ids_2]

  if (use_treeid_subset) {

    requested <- unique(s1_fit_treeids_1)

    # 1. The ID must appear in the pair CSV at all.
    not_in_csv <- setdiff(requested, csv_ids_1)
    if (length(not_in_csv) > 0L) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "s1_fit_treeids_1 contains %d TreeID(s) absent from the '%s' column of the pair CSV: %s",
        length(not_in_csv), col_treeid_las1, paste(not_in_csv, collapse = ", ")
      ))
    }

    # 2. The epoch-1 stem must exist in las_1.
    not_in_cloud <- setdiff(requested, treeids_1)
    if (length(not_in_cloud) > 0L) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "s1_fit_treeids_1 contains %d TreeID(s) that are paired in the CSV but absent from las_1: %s",
        length(not_in_cloud), paste(not_in_cloud, collapse = ", ")
      ))
    }

    # 3. Every epoch-2 partner must exist in las_2. Reported per epoch-1 stem,
    #    since that is the ID the user actually typed and has to correct.
    pair_rows <- mapping_df[mapping_df[[col_treeid_las1]] %in% requested,
                            c(col_treeid_las1, col_treeid_las2), drop = FALSE]
    partner_ok <- pair_rows[[col_treeid_las2]] %in% treeids_2

    if (!all(partner_ok)) {
      bad <- pair_rows[!partner_ok, , drop = FALSE]
      stop(sprintf(
        paste0("%d requested TreeID(s) have no usable epoch-2 partner in las_2:\n  %s\n",
               "  The diagnostic subset requires a complete temporal pair for every\n",
               "  requested stem - a stem fitted without its partner is dropped by\n",
               "  Step 1.3 regardless. Remove these IDs from s1_fit_treeids_1, or fix\n",
               "  the pair CSV / las_2 TreeIDs."),
        nrow(bad),
        paste(sprintf("las_1 %s -> las_2 %s (missing from las_2)",
                      bad[[col_treeid_las1]], bad[[col_treeid_las2]]),
              collapse = "\n  ")
      ))
    }

    treeids_1 <- requested
    treeids_2 <- treeids_2[treeids_2 %in% unique(pair_rows[[col_treeid_las2]])]

    cat("── DIAGNOSTIC SUBSET ACTIVE ────────────────────────────────────────────\n")
    cat(sprintf("  Requested las_1 TreeIDs : %s\n", paste(treeids_1, collapse = ", ")))
    cat(sprintf("  Partners from CSV       : %s\n", paste(treeids_2, collapse = ", ")))
    cat("  All requested stems have a complete pair.\n")
    cat("  This is a partial fit. Do NOT save a Stage 1 checkpoint from this run\n")
    cat("  and expect Stages 2-6 to be valid - set s1_fit_treeids_1 <- NULL first.\n\n")
  }

  # Subset the LAS data to the CSV-listed trees before RANSAC fitting runs.
  las_1 <- lidR::filter_poi(las_1, TreeID %in% treeids_1)
  las_2 <- lidR::filter_poi(las_2, TreeID %in% treeids_2)

  cat(sprintf("CSV Mode Active: Stage 1 will only process %d trees (las_1) and %d trees (las_2).\n", 
              length(treeids_1), length(treeids_2)))
  cat("Step 1.3 (Spatial Pairing) has been flagged for DEACTIVATION.\n\n")

} else {
  cat("Spatial Mode Active: Processing all available trees for automatic matching.\n\n")
}

# ── Parts B-D: RANSAC Parameter Setup + Fitting, repeated per threshold ──────
# ransac_distance_threshold may be a scalar (single fit, old behaviour) or a
# vector (e.g. c(0.001, 0.005, 0.01, 0.05)), in which case Parts B-D below
# are re-run in full – separately for las_1 and las_2 – once per value.
# Every run's outputs are kept in s1_threshold_results, keyed by the
# threshold value, so nothing from an earlier run is overwritten.

s1_threshold_results <- list()

for (rdt in ransac_distance_threshold) {

  rdt_key <- as.character(rdt)
  cat(sprintf(
    "\n════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n"
  ))
  cat(sprintf("ransac_distance_threshold = %s\n", rdt_key))
  cat(sprintf(
    "════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════\n"
  ))

  # ── Part B: RANSAC Parameter Setup ─────────────────────────────────────────
  fp_i <- ransac_ellipse_fit_params(
    bot                = ransac_slice_bot,
    top                = ransac_slice_top,
    height_min         = ransac_height_min,
    step               = ransac_slice_step,
    width              = ransac_slice_width,
    distance_threshold = rdt,
    n_iterations        = 1000L,   # ignored while ransac_iter_per_point is set
    iter_per_point      = ransac_iter_per_point,
    iter_max            = ransac_iter_max,
    iter_min            = ransac_iter_min,
    early_exit          = FALSE,
    # Records the best hypothesis's inlier count and angular coverage after
    # every iteration, per slice, for the convergence diagnostic further down.
    # Costs ~8 KB per slice in memory and in the Stage 1 checkpoint at 1000
    # iterations, so set FALSE for production runs that do not need it.
    track_history       = ransac_track_history
  )

  # ── Part C: Run Brute-Force RANSAC Fitting ─────────────────────────────────
  # Every point falling inside a slice is passed directly to RANSAC, matching
  # the approach used in Step 4.2. ransac_ellipse_run() processes the
  # already-subsetted las_1 and las_2 objects directly.
  # ── Progress reporting for the library fit ──────────────────────────────────
  # This is the single longest step in the pipeline and it happens INSIDE the
  # sourced RANSAC library, where nothing in this file can wrap a bar around the
  # per-tree loop. So rather than guess at the library's interface, its formals
  # are inspected: if it accepts a progress argument it is passed through, and if
  # it does not, that is said once, plainly, instead of leaving the console
  # silent for several minutes with no explanation.
  .run_args <- list(las = las_1, fit_params = fp_i, clean = FALSE,
                    seed = ransac_seed, label = "las_1")
  .pg_arg <- intersect(c("show_progress", "progress", "verbose"),
                       names(formals(ransac_ellipse_run)))
  if (length(.pg_arg)) {
    .run_args[[.pg_arg[1]]] <- show_progress_bars
  } else {
    cat("  note: ransac_ellipse_run() exposes no progress argument, so this step\n",
        "        reports only when it finishes. Add show_progress to the RANSAC\n",
        "        library to get a per-tree bar here.\n", sep = "")
  }

  cat(sprintf("[%s] Starting RANSAC ellipse fitting over %d tree(s)...\n",
              "las_1", length(treeids_1)))
  .t_fit <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  res_1_i <- do.call(ransac_ellipse_run, .run_args)
  cat(sprintf("[las_1] done in %.1f min\n", (proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - .t_fit) / 60))

  cat(sprintf("\n[%s] Starting RANSAC ellipse fitting over %d tree(s)...\n",
              "las_2", length(treeids_2)))
  .run_args$las <- las_2; .run_args$label <- "las_2"
  .t_fit <- proc.time()[["elapsed"]]
  res_2_i <- do.call(ransac_ellipse_run, .run_args)
  cat(sprintf("[las_2] done in %.1f min\n", (proc.time()[["elapsed"]] - .t_fit) / 60))
  rm(.run_args, .pg_arg, .t_fit)

  # ── Part D: Extract and Summarise ──────────────────────────────────────────
  ellipses_zt_1_all_i   <- res_1_i$raw
  ellipses_zt_2_all_i   <- res_2_i$raw
  ransac_inlier_ids_1_i <- res_1_i$inlier_ids
  ransac_inlier_ids_2_i <- res_2_i$inlier_ids

  cat(sprintf(
    "\nFitting complete.\n  las_1: %d trees | las_2: %d trees\n",
    length(res_1_i$raw), length(res_2_i$raw)
  ))

  ee_summary_1_i <- ransac_ellipse_summarise_early_exit(res_1_i$raw, label = "las_1")
  ee_summary_2_i <- ransac_ellipse_summarise_early_exit(res_2_i$raw, label = "las_2")

  s1_threshold_results[[rdt_key]] <- list(
    ransac_distance_threshold = rdt,
    fp                  = fp_i,
    res_1               = res_1_i,
    res_2               = res_2_i,
    ellipses_zt_1_all   = ellipses_zt_1_all_i,
    ellipses_zt_2_all   = ellipses_zt_2_all_i,
    ransac_inlier_ids_1 = ransac_inlier_ids_1_i,
    ransac_inlier_ids_2 = ransac_inlier_ids_2_i,
    ee_summary_1        = ee_summary_1_i,
    ee_summary_2        = ee_summary_2_i
  )
}

# ── Select the "active" threshold and expose it under the original,          ─
#    singular variable names (fp, res_1, res_2, ellipses_zt_1_all, ...) so   ─
#    Step 1.2 onward continue to work unchanged. ─────────────────────────────
ransac_active_threshold_key <- if (is.null(ransac_active_threshold)) {
  as.character(ransac_distance_threshold[1])
} else {
  as.character(ransac_active_threshold)
}

if (!ransac_active_threshold_key %in% names(s1_threshold_results)) {
  stop(sprintf(
    "ransac_active_threshold (%s) is not one of the values fitted in ransac_distance_threshold (%s).",
    ransac_active_threshold_key, paste(ransac_distance_threshold, collapse = ", ")
  ))
}

cat(sprintf(
  "\n── Active threshold for Step 1.2 onward: %s ──\n", ransac_active_threshold_key
))

active <- s1_threshold_results[[ransac_active_threshold_key]]
fp                  <- active$fp
res_1               <- active$res_1
res_2               <- active$res_2
ellipses_zt_1_all   <- active$ellipses_zt_1_all
ellipses_zt_2_all   <- active$ellipses_zt_2_all
ransac_inlier_ids_1 <- active$ransac_inlier_ids_1
ransac_inlier_ids_2 <- active$ransac_inlier_ids_2
ee_summary_1        <- active$ee_summary_1
ee_summary_2        <- active$ee_summary_2

# Quick cross-threshold comparison of raw tree/ellipse counts
if (length(s1_threshold_results) > 1L) {
  cat("\n── Threshold comparison (raw fit counts) ──\n")
  cmp <- data.frame(
    ransac_distance_threshold = names(s1_threshold_results),
    n_trees_las_1  = sapply(s1_threshold_results, function(x) length(x$res_1$raw)),
    n_trees_las_2  = sapply(s1_threshold_results, function(x) length(x$res_2$raw))
  )
  print(cmp, row.names = FALSE)
}
}
```

## 1.2 Ellipse Cleaning

```{r}
#| label: params-ransac-ellipse-clean
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Neighbour-slice consensus (adaptive) + MAD semi-minor outlier filter"


# ── Stage A: consensus parameters ─────────────────────────────────────────────
# Each fitted slice is compared with the nearest fitted slice above and below it
# in slice_z. Unfitted slices are skipped over, so a gap does not break the
# chain. Two slices i, j AGREE if ALL of:
#   centre offset  <= frac_centre * mean(minor_i, minor_j)
#   |Δ semi-minor| <= frac_minor  * min(minor_i, minor_j)
#   |Δ semi-major| <= frac_major  * min(major_i, major_j)
# A slice with no agreeing neighbour is removed.
#
# CENTRE OFFSET IS NOT THE RAW XY DISTANCE. A stem leaning theta must move
# step * tan(theta) between neighbouring slices - that is geometry, not error,
# and measuring it as disagreement rejects perfectly fitted leaning stems. The
# offset is therefore measured against the LEAN-PREDICTED centre from
# .local_lean() (Section 0.2), with the pair under test WITHHELD from that fit
# so two adjacent slices sharing an error cannot validate each other. Set
# consensus_use_local_lean <- FALSE to recover the old vertical-stem behaviour.
#
# Because lean no longer contributes to the residual, the three fractions below
# are now a pure error budget and can be tighter than they had to be when they
# were also absorbing the stem's tilt.
consensus_frac_centre <- 0.30   # of the MEAN semi-minor of the two slices
consensus_frac_minor  <- 0.30   # of the SMALLER semi-minor of the two slices
consensus_frac_major  <- 0.30   # of the SMALLER semi-major of the two slices

# ── Local-lean prediction (Step 1.2 only – Stage 1A sets its own) ─────────────
# Exposed here so the main pipeline can be tuned independently of the Stage 1A
# rough fit, which runs at a coarser slice step and so sees a larger per-slice
# lean offset. These feed .consensus_clean() -> .consensus_flag_one().
consensus_use_local_lean <- TRUE  # FALSE = compare raw centres (vertical-stem assumption)
consensus_lean_k         <- 4L    # kept centres per side used for the local axis fit;

consensus_tol_floor <- NULL     # optional absolute floor on any tolerance (m)
consensus_tol_cap   <- NULL     # optional absolute cap on any tolerance (m)
consensus_max_gap   <- NULL     # max vertical gap to count as neighbours (m)
consensus_sort_axes <- TRUE     # compare max-to-max / min-to-min, not a-to-a

# ── Stage B: MAD semi-minor outlier parameters ────────────────────────────────
# Runs on the slices that SURVIVED consensus, per tree. The semi-minor axis is
# scored against that stem's own median; anything further than mult * MAD is
# removed. z = (b - median(b)) / MAD, with MAD carrying the 1.4826 constant.
mad_minor_mult  <- 2.0    # MAD multiplier
mad_minor_min_n <- 5L     # need at least this many kept slices to run the test
run_mad_minor   <- TRUE   # FALSE = consensus only

# ── Stage C: MAD semi-major outlier parameters ────────────────────────────────
# Runs on the slices that survived consensus AND the semi-minor test, per tree.
# The same rule applied to the semi-major axis: z = (a - median(a)) / MAD.
# Because Stage B has already removed slices, the median and MAD here come from
# a narrower population than Stage B saw, so the same multiplier is stricter in
# practice than it looks.
mad_major_mult  <- 2.0    # MAD multiplier
mad_major_min_n <- 5L     # need at least this many surviving slices to run it
run_mad_major   <- TRUE   # FALSE = skip the semi-major stage

run_ellipse_cleaning <- TRUE    # FALSE = pass raw through as-is

.par_apply("params-ransac-ellipse-clean")
```

```{r}
#| label: ransac-ellipse-clean
#| code-summary: "Neighbour-slice consensus (adaptive) + MAD semi-minor outlier filter"

# ── Consensus fractions from the Stage 1A.1b scarcity ramp ───────────────────
# Each fraction is interpolated from ITS OWN base above toward the cap the probe
# carries, by the single scarcity t the probe measured. A NO-OP at t = 0, and
# when the probe did not run or was set to report only.
#
# Why these three and not the MAD multipliers: the logs put 68-78% of every
# scarce epoch's slices in the `orphan` column and under 1% in `madB`/`madA`.
# Consensus is what is removing the stems; MAD is barely participating, so
# loosening it would change nothing and would only cost real outlier rejection.
#
# Pass 2 follows automatically - consensus2_frac_* are NULL and inherit these.
if (exists("density_scarcity") && isTRUE(density_scarcity > 0) &&
    isTRUE(density_apply_regime)) {
  .dscale <- function(base, cap) base + density_scarcity * (cap - base)
  .old_c  <- c(consensus_frac_centre, consensus_frac_minor, consensus_frac_major)

  consensus_frac_centre <- .dscale(consensus_frac_centre, density_max_frac_centre)
  consensus_frac_minor  <- .dscale(consensus_frac_minor,  density_max_frac_minor)
  consensus_frac_major  <- .dscale(consensus_frac_major,  density_max_frac_major)

  cat(sprintf(paste0("[1.2] scarcity t = %.2f: frac_centre %.2f -> %.2f | ",
                     "frac_minor %.2f -> %.2f | frac_major %.2f -> %.2f\n"),
              density_scarcity,
              .old_c[1], consensus_frac_centre,
              .old_c[2], consensus_frac_minor,
              .old_c[3], consensus_frac_major))
  rm(.dscale, .old_c)
}

                                  #   bracketing (both sides) is preferred over
                                  #   one-sided extrapolation, which uses up to 2 * k


# The consensus + MAD cleaning functions (.consensus_flag_one, .mad_minor_flag_one,
# .mad_major_flag_one, .consensus_clean, .print_consensus_summary) are defined once
# in Section 0.5 (ellipse-pipeline-functions), shared with the Stage 1A fit.

# ── Run ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
if (run_ellipse_cleaning) {

  windowed_1 <- .filter_min_ellipses(res_1$raw, "las_1")
  windowed_2 <- .filter_min_ellipses(res_2$raw, "las_2")

  .clean_args <- list(
    frac_c    = consensus_frac_centre,
    frac_maj  = consensus_frac_major,
    frac_min  = consensus_frac_minor,
    max_gap   = consensus_max_gap,
    sort_axes = consensus_sort_axes,
    tol_floor = consensus_tol_floor,
    tol_cap   = consensus_tol_cap,
    do_mad        = run_mad_minor,
    mad_mult      = mad_minor_mult,
    mad_min_n     = mad_minor_min_n,
    do_mad_maj    = run_mad_major,
    mad_maj_mult  = mad_major_mult,
    mad_maj_min_n = mad_major_min_n,
    use_local_lean = consensus_use_local_lean,
    lean_k         = consensus_lean_k
  )

  clean_result_1 <- do.call(.consensus_clean, c(list(windowed_1), .clean_args))
  clean_result_2 <- do.call(.consensus_clean, c(list(windowed_2), .clean_args))

  consensus_summary_1 <- .print_consensus_summary(clean_result_1, "las_1")
  consensus_summary_2 <- .print_consensus_summary(clean_result_2, "las_2")

  res_1$clean <- clean_result_1
  res_2$clean <- clean_result_2
  res_1$valid <- lapply(clean_result_1, `[[`, "valid")
  res_2$valid <- lapply(clean_result_2, `[[`, "valid")

} else {

  cat("\nEllipse cleaning SKIPPED (run_ellipse_cleaning = FALSE).\n",
      "Raw ellipses are used as-is for downstream steps.\n")
  res_1$valid <- res_1$raw
  res_2$valid <- res_2$raw
  res_1$clean <- NULL
  res_2$clean <- NULL
}

# ── Cleaning parameter record ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
cp <- list(
  method         = "consensus_adaptive_lean_then_mad_minor_then_mad_major",
  use_local_lean = consensus_use_local_lean,
  lean_k         = consensus_lean_k,
  frac_centre    = consensus_frac_centre,
  frac_minor     = consensus_frac_minor,
  frac_major     = consensus_frac_major,
  tol_floor      = consensus_tol_floor,
  tol_cap        = consensus_tol_cap,
  max_gap        = consensus_max_gap,
  sort_axes      = consensus_sort_axes,
  mad_minor      = run_mad_minor,
  mad_minor_mult = mad_minor_mult,
  mad_minor_n    = mad_minor_min_n,
  mad_major      = run_mad_major,
  mad_major_mult = mad_major_mult,
  mad_major_n    = mad_major_min_n
)

ellipses_zt_1_valid_all <- res_1$valid
ellipses_zt_2_valid_all <- res_2$valid
results_1_all           <- res_1$valid
results_2_all           <- res_2$valid
clean_results_1_all     <- res_1$clean
clean_results_2_all     <- res_2$clean

cat(sprintf(
  "\nValid ellipses ready for downstream steps:\n  las_1: %d trees | las_2: %d trees\n",
  length(Filter(function(d) !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0, ellipses_zt_1_valid_all)),
  length(Filter(function(d) !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0, ellipses_zt_2_valid_all))
))
```

### Vis - cleaning1 MAD Select
```{r}
#| label: params-diag-mad-minor-multiplier
#| code-summary: "Parameters - Diagnostic: MAD z-scores of semi-minor axis per slice, to choose mad_minor_mult"


# ── Parameters ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
mad_diag_treeids_1 <- NULL                  # NULL = every tree; else c(1, 13, ...)
mad_diag_mult_grid <- c(1, 1.5, 2, 3, 6)    # multipliers to compare in the table

mad_diag_ref_lines <- c(3, 6)               # multipliers drawn on the plots
mad_diag_pad       <- 0.1                   # y-axis padding beyond min/max z
mad_diag_plot      <- TRUE                  # FALSE = sweep table only

.par_apply("params-diag-mad-minor-multiplier")
```

### Diag - MAD

```{r}
#| label: diag-mad-minor-multiplier
#| code-summary: "Diagnostic: MAD z-scores of semi-minor axis per slice, to choose mad_minor_mult"
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 4

mad_diag_show      <- if (exists("mad_minor_mult")) mad_minor_mult else 3.0

# ── Build the per-slice score frame from the cleaning output ──────────────────
# Scores are computed on the CONSENSUS SURVIVORS only, matching where the MAD
# stage actually runs. Slices already dropped by consensus are excluded from the
# median and MAD, so the reference distribution here is the same one the filter
# sees – not the raw spread.
.mad_diag_frame <- function(clean_result, label) {
  if (is.null(clean_result) || length(clean_result) == 0L) return(NULL)

  dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(clean_result), function(tid) {
    df <- clean_result[[tid]]$flagged
    if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) return(NULL)

    # minor_len is written by .consensus_flag_one() and respects sort_axes, so
    # this scores exactly the value the filter scores.
    b <- if ("minor_len" %in% names(df)) df$minor_len else
           pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b)

    elig <- !df$unfitted & !df$no_consensus & !is.na(b)
    if (sum(elig) < 2L) return(NULL)

    med  <- median(b[elig], na.rm = TRUE)
    madr <- mad(b[elig], center = med, na.rm = TRUE)   # includes 1.4826
    if (is.na(madr) || madr < 1e-12) madr <- NA_real_

    data.frame(
      epoch   = label,
      TreeID  = tid,
      slice_z = df$slice_z[elig],
      h       = df$slice_z[elig] - min(df$slice_z, na.rm = TRUE),
      minor   = b[elig],
      z       = (b[elig] - med) / madr,
      med     = med,
      madr    = madr,
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}

if (!exists("clean_results_1_all") || is.null(clean_results_1_all))
  stop("clean_results_1_all not found – run the ransac-ellipse-clean chunk first.")

mad_diag_1 <- .mad_diag_frame(clean_results_1_all, "las_1")
mad_diag_2 <- .mad_diag_frame(clean_results_2_all, "las_2")
mad_diag   <- dplyr::bind_rows(mad_diag_1, mad_diag_2)

if (is.null(mad_diag) || nrow(mad_diag) == 0L)
  stop("No scoreable slices – every tree has fewer than 2 consensus survivors.")

# ── Multiplier sweep: what each choice would remove ───────────────────────────
sweep <- do.call(rbind, lapply(mad_diag_mult_grid, function(k) {
  d <- mad_diag[!is.na(mad_diag$z), ]
  do.call(rbind, lapply(split(d, d$epoch), function(dd) {
    flag <- abs(dd$z) > k
    data.frame(
      mult        = k,
      epoch       = dd$epoch[1],
      n_slices    = nrow(dd),
      n_flagged   = sum(flag),
      pct_flagged = round(100 * mean(flag), 2),
      n_trees_hit = length(unique(dd$TreeID[flag])),
      # A tree losing most of its slices to this filter is the failure mode to
      # watch: it means the stem's own spread, not a few bad fits, is driving it.
      worst_tree_pct = round(100 * max(c(0, sapply(split(dd, dd$TreeID),
                              function(t) mean(abs(t$z) > k)))), 1),
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE
    )
  }))
}))

cat("── MAD semi-minor multiplier sweep ──\n")
cat("z = (b - median(b)) / MAD  [MAD includes the 1.4826 constant]\n\n")
print(sweep[order(sweep$epoch, sweep$mult), ], row.names = FALSE)

cat(sprintf("\nScore range: las_1 |z| max %.2f | las_2 |z| max %.2f\n",
            suppressWarnings(max(abs(mad_diag$z[mad_diag$epoch == "las_1"]), na.rm = TRUE)),
            suppressWarnings(max(abs(mad_diag$z[mad_diag$epoch == "las_2"]), na.rm = TRUE))))
cat(sprintf("Currently set: mad_minor_mult = %.1f\n", mad_diag_show))

# ── Per-tree dual-axis plots ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Left axis  : z score. The y range is clipped to that tree's own observed range
#              (+/- mad_diag_pad), so the shape of the series is readable rather
#              than squashed by the threshold lines – which means a reference
#              line above the highest score simply does not appear on that
#              tree's panel.
# Right axis : semi-minor axis length, which is z rescaled by that tree's own
#              median and MAD (b = med + z * MAD). The mapping is exact and
#              linear, so one series carries both readings – the right axis is a
#              second way of reading the same points, not a second variable.
if (mad_diag_plot) {

  wanted_1 <- if (is.null(mad_diag_treeids_1)) unique(mad_diag_1$TreeID) else
                as.character(mad_diag_treeids_1)

  mk_mad_plot <- function(d, epoch_label, colour) {
    if (is.null(d) || nrow(d) == 0L || all(is.na(d$z))) return(NULL)
    d   <- d[order(d$h), ]
    med <- d$med[1]; madr <- d$madr[1]
    if (is.na(madr)) return(NULL)

    d$flagged <- abs(d$z) > mad_diag_show

    z_lo <- min(d$z, na.rm = TRUE) - mad_diag_pad
    z_hi <- max(d$z, na.rm = TRUE) + mad_diag_pad

    ggplot(d, aes(h, z)) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * rep(mad_diag_ref_lines, each = 2),
                 linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.3) +
      geom_hline(yintercept = c(-1, 1) * mad_diag_show,
                 linetype = "dashed", colour = "#D7263D", linewidth = 0.6) +
      geom_line(colour = colour, alpha = 0.5, linewidth = 0.4) +
      geom_point(aes(shape = flagged, size = flagged), colour = colour, alpha = 0.85) +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 4), guide = "none") +
      scale_size_manual(values  = c(`FALSE` = 2.2, `TRUE` = 3.6), guide = "none") +
      scale_y_continuous(
        name     = "MAD z-score of semi-minor axis",
        sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . * madr + med, name = "Semi-minor axis b (m)")
      ) +
      # coord_cartesian clips the view without dropping rows, so the connecting
      # line still runs to an off-panel point instead of breaking. It must do
      # the clipping rather than scale_y_continuous(limits=), which would set
      # out-of-range values to NA and also recompute the secondary axis breaks
      # from the truncated data.
      coord_cartesian(ylim = c(z_lo, z_hi)) +
      labs(
        title    = sprintf("[%s] Tree %s", epoch_label, d$TreeID[1]),
        subtitle = sprintf("median b %.4f m | MAD %.4f | %d of %d flagged at mult %.1f",
                           med, madr, sum(d$flagged), nrow(d), mad_diag_show),
        x        = "Height above stem's lowest fitted slice (m)",
        caption  = sprintf("dashed = current mult (%.1f) | dotted = %s | y clipped to observed z \u00b1 %.1f",
                           mad_diag_show,
                           paste(mad_diag_ref_lines, collapse = ", "),
                           mad_diag_pad)
      ) +
      theme_bw(base_size = 11)
  }

  for (tid in wanted_1) {
    p <- mk_mad_plot(mad_diag_1[mad_diag_1$TreeID == tid, ], "las_1", COL_1)
    if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
  }
  for (tid in unique(mad_diag_2$TreeID)) {
    p <- mk_mad_plot(mad_diag_2[mad_diag_2$TreeID == tid, ], "las_2", COL_2)
    if (!is.null(p)) print(p)
  }
}
```


### Vis - slice x thresh inliers post clean
```{r}
#| label: fig-ransac-threshold-slice-compare
#| standalone: true
#| fig: false
#| results: asis
#| column: page
#| code-summary: "Threshold x epoch x slice grid; red outline = consensus removal, orange = MAD semi-minor removal"

if (!second_run && params$make_plots) {

  if (!exists("s1_threshold_results") || length(s1_threshold_results) == 0L) {
    stop("s1_threshold_results not found – run the s1-ellipse-fitting-Run-1 chunk first.")
  }

  # ── User input ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  vis_thr_treeids_1 <- NULL
  n_thr_rows        <- NULL
  slice_match_eps   <- 1e-6

  # ── Outline appearance ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  outline_consensus_col <- "#D7263D"   # red    - dropped by neighbour consensus
  outline_mad_col       <- "#F07C10"   # orange - dropped by MAD semi-minor filter
  outline_px            <- 6

  slice_label_offset <- (if (is.null(ransac_slice_bot)) 0 else ransac_slice_bot) +
                        ransac_slice_width / 2

  thr_keys  <- names(s1_threshold_results)
  raw_1_ref <- s1_threshold_results[[thr_keys[1]]]$res_1$raw
  raw_2_ref <- s1_threshold_results[[thr_keys[1]]]$res_2$raw

  # ── Cleaning rule, self-contained ──────────────────────────────────────────
  # Uses the Step 1.2 globals when this chunk runs after cleaning; otherwise
  # falls back to these defaults so it stands alone in its current position,
  # ABOVE 1.2. Removal is recomputed per threshold column, since the stored
  # clean_results_* exist only for the active threshold.
  .vis_frac_c   <- if (exists("consensus_frac_centre")) consensus_frac_centre else 0.10
  .vis_frac_maj <- if (exists("consensus_frac_major"))  consensus_frac_major  else 0.10
  .vis_frac_min <- if (exists("consensus_frac_minor"))  consensus_frac_minor  else 0.10
  .vis_floor    <- if (exists("consensus_tol_floor"))   consensus_tol_floor   else NULL
  .vis_cap      <- if (exists("consensus_tol_cap"))     consensus_tol_cap     else NULL
  .vis_max_gap  <- if (exists("consensus_max_gap"))     consensus_max_gap     else NULL
  .vis_sort_ax  <- if (exists("consensus_sort_axes"))   consensus_sort_axes   else TRUE
  .vis_mad_on   <- if (exists("run_mad_minor"))         run_mad_minor         else TRUE
  .vis_mad_mult <- if (exists("mad_minor_mult"))        mad_minor_mult        else 3.0
  .vis_mad_n    <- if (exists("mad_minor_min_n"))       mad_minor_min_n       else 5L
  .vis_madA_on   <- if (exists("run_mad_major"))       run_mad_major         else TRUE
  .vis_madA_mult <- if (exists("mad_major_mult"))      mad_major_mult        else 3.0
  .vis_madA_n    <- if (exists("mad_major_min_n"))     mad_major_min_n       else 5L

  cat(sprintf(
    paste0("Outline rule: centre %.0f%% mean-minor | minor %.0f%% lower-minor | ",
           "major %.0f%% lower-major | MAD semi-minor x%.1f%s\n"),
    .vis_frac_c * 100, .vis_frac_min * 100, .vis_frac_maj * 100, .vis_mad_mult,
    if (exists("consensus_frac_centre")) " (from Step 1.2)" else " (chunk defaults)"
  ))

  # Returns, for one stem at one threshold, a data.frame of slice_z + status:
  #   "kept" | "consensus" | "mad"
  # Same two-stage rule as Step 1.2: adaptive-tolerance neighbour agreement,
  # then MAD on the semi-minor axis of the survivors only.
  .vis_slice_status <- local({
    cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
    function(raw_list, tid, cache_key) {
      if (!is.null(cache[[cache_key]])) return(cache[[cache_key]])

      df <- raw_list[[as.character(tid)]]
      if (is.null(df) || nrow(df) == 0L) {
        out <- data.frame(slice_z = numeric(0), status = character(0))
        cache[[cache_key]] <- out; return(out)
      }

      fitted <- !is.na(df$center_x) & !is.na(df$center_y) &
                !is.na(df$semi_a)   & !is.na(df$semi_b)   & !is.na(df$slice_z)

      maj  <- if (.vis_sort_ax) pmax(df$semi_a, df$semi_b) else df$semi_a
      min_ <- if (.vis_sort_ax) pmin(df$semi_a, df$semi_b) else df$semi_b

      .cl <- function(t) {
        if (!is.null(.vis_floor)) t <- max(t, .vis_floor)
        if (!is.null(.vis_cap))   t <- min(t, .vis_cap)
        t
      }

      # ── Stage A: neighbour consensus ───────────────────────────────────────
      agrees <- rep(FALSE, nrow(df))
      idx    <- which(fitted)
      if (length(idx) >= 2L) {
        ord <- idx[order(df$slice_z[idx])]
        for (k in seq_len(length(ord) - 1L)) {
          i <- ord[k]; j <- ord[k + 1L]
          if (!is.null(.vis_max_gap) &&
              abs(df$slice_z[j] - df$slice_z[i]) > .vis_max_gap) next

          tol_c   <- .cl(.vis_frac_c   * mean(c(min_[i], min_[j])))
          tol_min <- .cl(.vis_frac_min * min(min_[i], min_[j]))
          tol_maj <- .cl(.vis_frac_maj * min(maj[i],  maj[j]))

          d_centre <- sqrt((df$center_x[j] - df$center_x[i])^2 +
                           (df$center_y[j] - df$center_y[i])^2)

          if (d_centre               <= tol_c   &&
              abs(min_[j] - min_[i]) <= tol_min &&
              abs(maj[j]  - maj[i])  <= tol_maj) {
            agrees[i] <- TRUE; agrees[j] <- TRUE
          }
        }
      }

      status <- ifelse(!fitted, NA_character_,
                       ifelse(agrees, "kept", "consensus"))

      # ── Stage B: MAD on semi-minor, consensus survivors only ───────────────
      if (.vis_mad_on) {
        elig <- !is.na(status) & status == "kept" & !is.na(min_)
        if (sum(elig) >= .vis_mad_n) {
          med <- median(min_[elig], na.rm = TRUE)
          m   <- mad(min_[elig], center = med, na.rm = TRUE)
          if (!is.na(m) && m >= 1e-12) {
            out <- elig & abs(min_ - med) > .vis_mad_mult * m
            status[out] <- "mad"
          }
        }
      }

      # ── Stage C: MAD on semi-major, survivors of Stage B only ──────────────
      # Shares the "mad" status, so both MAD stages draw the same orange border.
      if (.vis_madA_on) {
        eligA <- !is.na(status) & status == "kept" & !is.na(maj)
        if (sum(eligA) >= .vis_madA_n) {
          medA <- median(maj[eligA], na.rm = TRUE)
          mA   <- mad(maj[eligA], center = medA, na.rm = TRUE)
          if (!is.na(mA) && mA >= 1e-12) {
            outA <- eligA & abs(maj - medA) > .vis_madA_mult * mA
            status[outA] <- "mad"
          }
        }
      }

      keep_rows <- !is.na(status)
      out <- data.frame(slice_z = df$slice_z[keep_rows],
                        status  = status[keep_rows],
                        stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
      cache[[cache_key]] <- out
      out
    }
  })

  # ── Pair lookup: las_1 TreeID -> las_2 TreeID ──────────────────────────────
  pair_lookup <- if (exists("pairs_matched") && is.data.frame(pairs_matched) &&
                     nrow(pairs_matched) > 0L) {
    data.frame(TreeID_1 = as.character(pairs_matched$TreeID_1),
               TreeID_2 = as.character(pairs_matched$TreeID_2),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else if (exists("mapping_df") && is.data.frame(mapping_df) &&
             nrow(mapping_df) > 0L) {
    data.frame(TreeID_1 = as.character(mapping_df[[col_treeid_las1]]),
               TreeID_2 = as.character(mapping_df[[col_treeid_las2]]),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    stop(paste0(
      "No temporal pair table available, so las_2 partners cannot be resolved.\n",
      "  Set use_csv_pairs <- TRUE (Step 1.1 loads mapping_df), or run the\n",
      "  temporal-pairing chunk first so pairs_matched exists."
    ))
  }

  pair_lookup <- unique(pair_lookup[!is.na(pair_lookup$TreeID_1) &
                                    !is.na(pair_lookup$TreeID_2), , drop = FALSE])

  # ── Resolve the requested stems ────────────────────────────────────────────
  if (is.null(vis_thr_treeids_1)) {
    wanted <- unique(pair_lookup$TreeID_1)
  } else {
    wanted   <- unique(as.character(vis_thr_treeids_1))
    unpaired <- setdiff(wanted, pair_lookup$TreeID_1)
    if (length(unpaired) > 0L) {
      stop(sprintf(
        "vis_thr_treeids_1 contains %d las_1 TreeID(s) with no temporal partner: %s",
        length(unpaired), paste(unpaired, collapse = ", ")
      ))
    }
  }

  pairs_vis <- pair_lookup[match(wanted, pair_lookup$TreeID_1), , drop = FALSE]

  has_fit <- function(raw, tid) {
    d <- raw[[tid]]
    !is.null(d) && nrow(d) > 0L && any(!is.na(d$center_x))
  }
  ok <- vapply(seq_len(nrow(pairs_vis)), function(i)
    has_fit(raw_1_ref, pairs_vis$TreeID_1[i]) &&
    has_fit(raw_2_ref, pairs_vis$TreeID_2[i]), logical(1))

  if (any(!ok)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      "Skipping %d temporal pair(s) with no fitted ellipses on one or both sides: %s\n",
      sum(!ok),
      paste(sprintf("las_1 %s / las_2 %s",
                    pairs_vis$TreeID_1[!ok], pairs_vis$TreeID_2[!ok]),
            collapse = ", ")
    ))
  }
  pairs_vis <- pairs_vis[ok, , drop = FALSE]
```
